citation: Elucidating the role of Pyroptosis in papillary thyroid cancer: prognostic, immunological, and therapeutic perspectives (PMID: 38287330)
sample_size: TCGA PTC cohort plus 20 pairs of clinical samples and 16 cell lines
summary: H2BC8 was identified as one of nine pyroptosis-related genes (PRGs) with dysregulated expression in papillary thyroid cancer (PTC). It was incorporated into a PyroScore prognostic model predicting thyroid cancer-free interval, with expression validated across six external datasets, 16 cell lines, and 20 pairs of clinical samples. Its dysregulated expression was associated with tumor immune microenvironment remodeling in PTC.

citation: Identification of key genes and immune infiltration modulated by CPAP in obstructive sleep apnea by integrated bioinformatics analysis (PMID: 34529670)
summary: H2BC8 was identified as one of eleven hub genes in peripheral blood mononuclear cells whose expression was significantly correlated with CPAP treatment response in obstructive sleep apnea patients via weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). These hub genes were used to construct a random forest model predicting CPAP therapeutic efficacy with an AUC of 0.92. H2BC8 expression was also partially correlated with monocyte infiltration associated with OSA remission.

citation: Tribulus terrestris L. protects glomerular endothelial cells via the miR155-H2AC6 interaction network in hypertensive renal injury (PMID: 34926670)
summary: In AngII-induced hypertensive renal injury in glomerular endothelial cells, miR-155-5p expression was negatively correlated with H2AC6 expression. Tribulus terrestris L. treatment upregulated miR-155-5p, which in turn negatively regulated H2AC6, suggesting H2AC6 is a downstream target of miR-155-5p in hypertensive renal injury. This miRNA-mRNA interaction network was identified through differential expression profiling and validated by qRT-PCR.

citation: Unveiling the Therapeutic Potential of Baicalin in Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptome Analysis with Experimental Validation of PANoptosis Inhibition (PMID: 40463856)
summary: H2AC6 was identified as one of five core PANoptosis-related genes significantly upregulated in degenerated intervertebral discs. Baicalin treatment effectively downregulated H2AC6 at both mRNA and protein levels in an IL-1β-induced nucleus pulposus cell degeneration model in vitro and in a puncture-induced rat IVDD model in vivo. These findings implicate H2AC6 in PANoptosis (integrated pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis) during disc degeneration.

citation: Inhibition of lactylation by LRP1 expression increases the risk of intervertebral disc degeneration: A multi-omics summary-based Mendelian randomization analysis (PMID: 40988222)
summary: Using summary-based Mendelian randomization integrating GWAS, cis-eQTL, and cis-mQTL data, H2AC6 expression was found to be positively correlated with the risk of intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). H2AC6 was identified as a lactylation-related gene with a causal effect on IVDD at the gene expression level (p_SMR < 0.05, p_HEIDI > 0.01).

citation: Mitochondrial metabolism and succinylation-related gene signatures for predicting prognosis and drug resistance in colon adenocarcinoma (PMID: 42176930)
summary: H2AC6 was identified as one of two hub genes in a prognostic model (OPISV) for colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), derived from differentially expressed mitochondrial metabolism and succinylation-related genes. H2AC6 was an independent prognostic factor for COAD, and its expression patterns were consistent across single-cell sequencing and qRT-PCR validation. The model achieved a 3-year time-dependent ROC AUC of 0.665.

citation: Global comparative transcriptomes uncover novel and population-specific gene expression in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 37641095)
summary: H2AC6 was identified as one of three novel genes critical for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) survival through survival analysis using TCGA data. H2AC6 was among 166 novel differentially expressed genes discovered by cross-comparing gene expression patterns across six global ESCC populations. It was proposed as a potential biomarker for ESCC diagnosis and prognosis.

citation: Serum extracellular vesicle RNA profiles in long COVID: insights from exercise-induced gene modulation (PMID: 41588020)
summary: H2AC6 was among the top 5 downregulated genes in serum extracellular vesicle RNA profiles during peak exercise after a 10-week aerobic exercise training program in long COVID patients. H2AC6 was one of 50 downregulated differentially expressed genes identified at peak exercise post-training compared to rest, with genes primarily involved in inflammation and metabolism. This suggests H2AC6 may be modulated as part of exercise-induced transcriptional suppression of inflammation-related pathways.

citation: Selective ablation of the androgen receptor in mouse sertoli cells affects sertoli cell maturation, barrier formation and cytoskeletal development (PMID: 21152390)
phenotype: Altered Anxa9 transcript levels in Sertoli cells of SCARKO mice compared to controls; Anxa9 identified among genes related to cell adhesion and cytoskeletal dynamics with marked differences in expression; Context: defective Sertoli cell barrier formation, delayed barrier development, disturbances in Sertoli cell nuclear maturation, aberrant positioning of Sertoli cell nuclei and cytoskeletal elements

citation: ANXA9 facilitates S100A4 and promotes breast cancer progression through modulating STAT3 pathway. (PMID: 38609357)
summary: ANXA9 mediates S100A4 to regulate the AKT/mTOR/STAT3 pathway and participates in p53/Bcl-2 apoptosis in breast cancer. ANXA9 also transfers S100A4 into the tumor microenvironment and mediates cytokine excretion (IL-6, IL-8, CCL2, CCL5) to promote angiogenesis via self-phosphorylation at Ser2 and Thr69. In vivo, ANXA9 downregulation suppressed xenograft tumor growth and lung metastasis.

citation: Annexin A9 promotes cell proliferation by regulating the Wnt signaling pathway in colorectal cancer. (PMID: 37349657)
summary: ANXA9 expression is significantly elevated in CRC tissue and cells, and knockdown inhibits proliferation, invasion, and migration. Functional analysis revealed that ANXA9 co-expressed genes are enriched in the Wnt signaling pathway, and Wnt activation reversed the anti-proliferative effects of ANXA9 deletion. High ANXA9 expression correlates with shorter overall survival in CRC patients.

citation: Targeting the ZMYM2-ANXA9 Axis with FLT3 Inhibitor G749 Overcomes Oxaliplatin Resistance in Colorectal Cancer. (PMID: 40427072)
summary: ZMYM2 was identified as a transcriptional regulator of ANXA9, with ChIP-qPCR confirming ZMYM2 binding to the ANXA9 promoter, especially in oxaliplatin-resistant CRC cells. ANXA9 is significantly overexpressed in chemoresistant CRC tumors and oxaliplatin-resistant cell lines, and its knockdown reduces proliferation and enhances oxaliplatin sensitivity. The FLT3 inhibitor G749 suppresses ANXA9 expression in a dose-dependent manner and reduces tumor burden in CRC xenograft models.

citation: miR-186-ANXA9 signaling inhibits tumorigenesis in breast cancer. (PMID: 37841425)
summary: miR-186-5p directly targets ANXA9, validated by luciferase reporter assay, and there is a negative correlation between miR-186-5p and ANXA9 in human breast cancer clinical samples. Knockdown of ANXA9 mimicked miR-186-5p overexpression (inhibiting proliferation, inducing apoptosis), while reintroduction of ANXA9 rescued miR-186-5p-induced apoptosis in MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, and BT549 cells. The mechanism involves decreased Bcl-2 and increased p53 expression.

citation: Annexin A9 promotes invasion and metastasis of colorectal cancer and predicts poor prognosis. (PMID: 29393380)
summary: ANXA9 protein expression is significantly higher in CRC tissue than adjacent mucosa by immunohistochemistry, and is associated with invasion depth and lymphatic metastasis. ANXA9-positive patients show poor prognosis and ANXA9 is an independent risk factor for survival. ANXA9 siRNA knockdown in HCT116 cells decreased cell activity and metastatic capacity, downregulated ADAM17 and MMP9, and upregulated TIMP-1 and E-cadherin.

citation: Exosome-derived ANXA9 functions as an oncogene in breast cancer. (PMID: 37294149)
summary: ANXA9 is secreted by breast cancer tissue-derived exosomes and its expression is upregulated 1- to 7-fold in BCA cells treated with exosomes, but not in normal MCF10A cells. ANXA9 silencing reduced colony formation by ~30%, and decreased migration and invasion by ~65% and ~68%, respectively, in BCA cells. In a xenograft model, ANXA9 silencing reduced tumor size by nearly half, demonstrating its oncogenic role in breast cancer.

citation: High Expression of Annexin A9 Promotes Cell Proliferation and Migration in Gastric Cancer via the TGF-β Signaling Pathway. (PMID: 34587407)
summary: ANXA9 is overexpressed in gastric cancer cells and tissues compared to normal controls, and correlates with unfavorable prognosis. ANXA9 overexpression in HGC-27 cells increased migration and colony formation, altered cell cycle distribution (decreased G1, increased S and G2 phases), and modulated EMT-related proteins. Immunofluorescence showed ANXA9 mediates cell migration and growth through the TGF-β signaling pathway via SMAD2/3 and p-SMAD2/3.

citation: Hsa-miR-105-1 Regulates Cisplatin-Resistance in Ovarian Carcinoma Cells by Targeting ANXA9. (PMID: 33680718)
summary: ANXA9 is significantly upregulated in cisplatin-resistant ovarian carcinoma cells, while miR-105-1 is downregulated, and ANXA9 was validated as a direct target of miR-105-1 by luciferase reporter assay. miR-105-1 mimics inhibited ANXA9 expression and increased cisplatin sensitivity in resistant cells by upregulating P53, P21, and Bax and downregulating E2F1 and Bcl-2. Conversely, miR-105-1 inhibitor promoted ANXA9 expression and enhanced cisplatin resistance in sensitive cells.

citation: Frequent Alteration of Annexin A9 and A10 in HPV-Negative Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinomas: Correlation with the Histopathological Differentiation Grade. (PMID: 30744186)
summary: ANXA9 expression is downregulated in 42% of HPV-negative HNSCC tissue samples compared to normal epithelia. ANXA9 expression in tumors is significantly associated with oropharyngeal location and histological differentiation grade. These findings suggest ANXA9 may be implicated in the pathogenesis of HNSCC, in contrast to its upregulation seen in other cancers.

citation: ERα and ERβ Homodimers in the Same Cellular Context Regulate Distinct Transcriptomes and Functions. (PMID: 35872983)
summary: ERβ was found to bind to cis-regulatory chromatin of ANXA9 as a direct transcriptional target in MCF7 breast cancer cells, identified through RNA sequencing and chromatin binding analysis. ANXA9 was among ERβ-specific migration-related direct targets, suggesting it is regulated by estrogen signaling through ERβ. This identifies ANXA9 as part of the ERβ-specific transcriptome distinct from ERα-regulated genes.

citation: Loss of heterochromatin protein 1 gamma reduces the number of primordial germ cells via impaired cell cycle progression in mice. (PMID: 21778144)
phenotype: Dramatic loss of germ cells before meiosis in HP1gamma(-/-) mice; Reduction in primordial germ cells (PGCs) detectable from early bud stage (E7.25); Gradual reduction in PGC number after E7.25; Significantly reduced BrdU incorporation into PGCs at E7.25 and E12.5; Lower proportion of PGCs in S phase at E12.5; Higher proportion of PGCs in G1 phase at E12.5; Increased proportion of p21 (CDKN1A)-positive PGCs suggesting G1/S phase transition inhibition; No differences in fate determination, migration, apoptosis, or histone modification of PGCs compared to controls

citation: Aurora kinase B-phosphorylated HP1α functions in chromosomal instability. (PMID: 31130069)
phenotype: Mitotic chromosomal instability in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs); Formation of anaphase/telophase chromatin bridges; Formation of micronuclei; Phenotypes rescued by exogenous expression of wild-type HP1α or phosphomimetic (S92D) variant

citation: Inhibition of RUNX1 slows the progression of pulmonary hypertension by targeting CBX5. (PMID: 39151099)
phenotype: RUNX1 knockdown reduced right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) in PH mice; RUNX1 knockdown reduced right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH) in PH mice; RUNX1 knockdown reduced pulmonary artery remodeling in PH mice; CBX5 knockdown suppressed proliferation, invasion, and migration of PASMCs under hypoxia; CBX5 knockdown stimulated apoptosis in PASMCs under hypoxia; CBX5 overexpression promoted proliferation and movement of hypoxic PASMCs and decreased apoptosis

citation: Hierarchical maintenance of MLL myeloid leukemia stem cells employs a transcriptional program shared with embryonic rather than adult stem cells. (PMID: 19200802)
phenotype: Cbx5 is a critical component of the leukemia stem cell (LSC) maintenance transcriptional program in a mouse model of AML; Coexpression of Myb, Hmgb3, and Cbx5 suffices for Hoxa/Meis-independent immortalization of myeloid progenitors; Cbx5 knockdown impairs LSC self-renewal maintenance in MLL-driven AML mouse model

citation: miR-206 knockout shows it is critical for myogenesis and directly regulates newly identified target mRNAs. (PMID: 32129700)
phenotype: Cbx5 identified as a direct target of miR-206 in C2C12 mouse muscle cells; Functional experiments confirm Cbx5 is directly regulated by miR-206 during myogenesis in C2C12 cells

citation: Transcriptional control of CBX5 by the RNA binding proteins RBMX and RBMXL1 maintains chromatin state in myeloid leukemia (PMID: 34458856)
summary: RBMX and RBMXL1 directly bind CBX5 mRNA and control nascent transcription of the CBX5 locus in AML cells. Loss of RBMX/L1 reduced CBX5 expression, and forced CBX5 re-expression rescued the effects of RBMX/L1 depletion on cell growth and apoptosis, demonstrating CBX5 is a key downstream effector of RBMX/L1 in myeloid leukemogenesis.

citation: CBX5 loss drives EGFR inhibitor resistance and results in therapeutically actionable vulnerabilities in lung cancer (PMID: 36652476)
summary: An epigenome-wide shRNA screen identified CBX5 loss as a driver of EGFR inhibitor resistance in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. Mechanistically, CBX5 loss increases E2F1 expression, which upregulates the anti-apoptotic gene BIRC5 (survivin), attenuating apoptosis after EGFRi treatment; BET inhibitors restore CBX5 expression and re-sensitize resistant cells.

citation: CBX5/G9a/H3K9me-mediated gene repression is essential to fibroblast activation during lung fibrosis (PMID: 31095524)
summary: CBX5 (HP1α) partners with the histone methyltransferase G9a to deposit H3K9me marks and assemble a repressor complex that epigenetically silences PPARGC1A (PGC1α) in lung fibroblasts, sustaining fibroblast activation. Both TGFβ and increased matrix stiffness engage this CBX5/G9a pathway, and its inhibition reduces collagen accumulation in bleomycin-injured mouse lungs.

citation: Targeting the Epigenetic Regulator CBX5 Promotes Fibroblast Metabolic Reprogramming and Inhibits Lung Fibrosis (PMID: 39642371)
summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry showed CBX5 expression is enriched in pathogenic fibroblast populations and fibroblastic foci of IPF lungs. CBX5 silencing in IPF fibroblasts inhibited TGFβ-stimulated glycolysis, enhanced AMPK signaling and mitochondrial metabolism, and reduced collagen secretion, identifying CBX5 as an epigenetic regulator linking metabolic reprogramming to fibroblast activation.

citation: Defective Integrator activity shapes the transcriptome of patients with multiple sclerosis (PMID: 39029934)
summary: A subset of MS patients showed reduced CBX5 expression in monocytes, correlating with progressive disease stages and extensive transcriptomic alterations including impaired U snRNA maturation and altered RNA Pol II pause-release. Inactivation of Cbx5 in mice mirrored these transcriptional defects and caused hypersensitivity to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, revealing CBX5 as an unexpected regulator of Integrator complex activity.

citation: Biological functions of chromobox (CBX) proteins in stem cell self-renewal, lineage-commitment, cancer and development (PMID: 32979540)
summary: CBX5 (along with CBX1 and CBX3) is a chromodomain-containing HP1 family protein that reads H3K9me3 marks deposited by SUV39H1/H2, thereby promoting heterochromatin formation and transcriptional repression. CBX5 functions as part of the HP1 complex to maintain inaccessible heterochromatin and suppress lineage-specific gene expression during development and differentiation.

citation: Regulatory dissection of the CBX5 and hnRNPA1 bi-directional promoter in human breast cancer cells reveals novel transcript variants differentially associated with HP1α down-regulation in metastatic cells (PMID: 26791953)
summary: CBX5 is transcriptionally down-regulated in metastatic compared to non-metastatic breast cancer cells and patient tissues, functioning as a suppressor of metastasis. Multiple novel CBX5 transcript isoforms were identified, including a non-coding isoform (STET) that inversely correlates with HP1α-coding CBX5 mRNA, suggesting regulation via alternative polyadenylation and splicing contributes to HP1α loss in metastatic cells.

citation: HP1α promotes the progression of prostate cancer (PMID: 37014569)
summary: HP1α (CBX5) mRNA and protein were significantly overexpressed in prostate cancer tissues and cell lines compared to benign prostatic hyperplasia, positively correlating with Gleason score. Knockdown of HP1α in PC3 and LNCaP cells inhibited proliferation, invasion, and migration while promoting apoptosis and EMT in vitro, and suppressed tumorigenesis in mouse xenograft models in vivo.

citation: Genetic Profile of Endotoxemia Reveals an Association With Thromboembolism and Stroke (PMID: 34668383)
summary: A genome-wide association study of serum lipopolysaccharide activity in 11,296 individuals identified genome-wide significant associations at five independent loci; CBX5 was among the closest genes to one of these loci. The genetic risk score for endotoxemia was associated with deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and venous thromboembolism in 195,170 FinnGen participants.

citation: LINC02381 contributes to cell proliferation and hinders cell apoptosis in glioma by transcriptionally enhancing CBX5 (PMID: 34274429)
summary: In glioma cells, the lncRNA LINC02381 interacts with the transcription factor CEBPβ to bind the CBX5 promoter and activate CBX5 transcription. CBX5 upregulation was shown to promote glioma cell proliferation and inhibit apoptosis, and rescue experiments confirmed that CBX5 overexpression reversed the anti-proliferative effects of LINC02381 knockdown.

citation: Single-cell profiling reveals immune disturbances landscape and HLA-F-mediated immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface in preeclampsia (PMID: 37854606)
summary: Over-expression of HLA-F in Jar trophoblast cells promoted cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, while under-expression had the opposite effect. In NK-92MI cells, over-expression of HLA-F increased secretion of immunoregulatory cytokines CSF1 and CCL22 and promoted adaptive NKG2C+ NK cell transformation. HLA-F expression was confirmed reduced in preeclamptic placental decidua samples compared to controls by mIF staining.

citation: HLA-F regulates the proliferation of trophoblast via PKM2-dependent glycolysis in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia (PMID: 40251569)
summary: Over-expression of HLA-F in Jar trophoblast cells promoted proliferation and enhanced glycolysis by upregulating PKM2 protein expression and enzymatic activity; HLA-F was shown to bind the PKM gene promoter (via ChIP-seq) and reduce lactylation at PKM2 K305. Silencing PKM2 with siRNA abolished HLA-F-mediated glycolysis and proliferation, and a MiniPDX model confirmed that the PKM2 agonist TEPP-46 rescued proliferation in HLA-F-knockdown cells. HLA-F expression was reduced in extravillous trophoblast and villous cytotrophoblast from preeclampsia patients.

citation: HLA Class Ib-receptor interactions during embryo implantation and early pregnancy (PMID: 35234898)
summary: HLA-F is expressed in mid-secretory endometrium and fluctuates during the menstrual cycle, with high levels during the implantation window. HLA-F protein expression levels correlate with the number of CD56-positive NK cells in the mid-secretory endometrium. HLA-F and HLA-G SNP genotypes, including a SNP in a progesterone-responsive element, are associated with time-to-pregnancy and influence HLA-F expression levels.

citation: Endometrial HLA-F expression is influenced by genotypes and correlates differently with immune cell infiltration in IVF and recurrent implantation failure patients (PMID: 35689445)
sample_size: 85 RIF women and 36 IVF control women
summary: HLA-F protein is expressed in mid-secretory endometrium and its levels differ according to HLA-F SNP genotypes and diplotypes. Endometrial HLA-F was positively correlated with anti-inflammatory CD163+ M2 macrophage infiltration and CD56+ uNK cell abundance across the full cohort, though this relationship differed in recurrent implantation failure subgroups. HLA-F levels were negatively correlated with plasma progesterone in the female infertility RIF subgroup but positively correlated in the male infertility RIF subgroup.

citation: HLA-F transcriptional and protein differential expression according to its genetic polymorphisms (PMID: 37166140)
sample_size: 1000 Genomes Project samples; healthy PBMC donors
summary: Three noncoding SNPs (rs1362126, rs2523405, and rs2523393) located in HLA-F-AS1 or upstream of HLA-F were confirmed to be associated with HLA-F mRNA and protein expression levels in PBMCs from healthy individuals, with the highest effect size and a double-dose effect. HLA-F mRNA is detected in most cell types, while the protein is localized in the ER and Golgi apparatus and reaches the cell membrane upon activation. HLA-F can be expressed as open conformers binding KIRs or as peptide-bound forms binding ILT2 and ILT4.

citation: Tetrameric complexes of HLA-E, HLA-F, and HLA-G (PMID: 12213342)
summary: Tetrameric complexes of HLA-F were constructed and shown to bind to ILT2 (immunoglobulin-like transcript 2) and ILT4 receptors, identifying these as potential ligands/receptors for HLA-F. This parallels HLA-G tetramer interactions with ILT2 and ILT4, suggesting a shared receptor-binding mechanism among HLA class Ib molecules.

citation: HLA-F and LILRB1 Genetic Polymorphisms Associated with Alloimmunisation in Sickle Cell Disease (PMID: 37686397)
summary: Genetic polymorphisms in HLA-F and its receptor LILRB1 (located in their regulatory regions and associated with protein expression levels) were found to be associated with red blood cell alloimmunisation susceptibility in sickle cell disease patients. This suggests HLA-F participates in immune tolerance mechanisms relevant to transfusion alloimmunisation, analogous to its role in pregnancy tolerance.

citation: HLA-F-AS1/miR-330-3p/PFN1 axis promotes colorectal cancer progression (PMID: 31863778)
sample_size: CRC tissue samples and cell lines
summary: The lncRNA HLA-F-AS1 (antisense RNA 1 of HLA-F) was significantly upregulated in colorectal cancer tissues and cell lines, and its overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, invasion, and blocked apoptosis of CRC cells. HLA-F-AS1 acts as a competing endogenous RNA by sponging miR-330-3p, thereby upregulating PFN1 expression and driving CRC progression. Knockdown of HLA-F-AS1 had the opposite tumor-suppressive effects.

citation: HLA-E and HLA-F Are Overexpressed in Glioblastoma and HLA-E Increased After Exposure to Ionizing Radiation (PMID: 35181585)
sample_size: 69 GBM tissue samples and 21 non-tumor brain tissue controls
summary: HLA-F mRNA was significantly upregulated in glioblastoma (GBM) tissue samples compared to non-tumor brain tissue controls. Dysregulated HLA-F expression was also observed between patients with methylated versus unmethylated MGMT promoter status. These findings suggest HLA-F may contribute to immune escape in GBM and could serve as a diagnostic biomarker.

citation: ASHG 2010 - Identification of multiple genetic variants related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition through genome-wide scan (W. Su et al.)
sample_size: 277 NPC patients and 285 healthy controls, with independent replication sets
summary: A genome-wide association study in a Taiwanese population identified significant associations between nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and two SNPs in HLA-F (rs3129055 and rs9258122; p = 7.36×10⁻¹¹ and 3.33×10⁻¹⁰, respectively). This represents the first GWAS report linking HLA-F genetic variants to NPC susceptibility, alongside HLA-A and GABBR1 associations on chromosome 6p21.3.

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41033306)
variant_detail: de novo or loss-of-function variants in EIF3B (specific notations not provided in abstract)
phenotype: cardiac defects; craniofacial dysmorphisms; mild developmental delays; behavioral abnormalities
diagnostic_reason: De novo occurrence, loss-of-function variants in a gene highly constrained against loss of function, supported by zebrafish models showing developmental abnormalities including thin heart tubes, lack of craniofacial cartilage, and embryonic lethality; EIF3B located within minimally overlapping region for cardiac anomalies in 7p22.3 microdeletions

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41679311)
variant_detail: de novo or loss-of-function variants in EIF3B (specific notations not provided in abstract)
phenotype: cardiac defects; craniofacial dysmorphisms; mild developmental delays; behavioral abnormalities
diagnostic_reason: De novo occurrence, loss-of-function variants in a highly constrained gene, functional zebrafish model evidence, autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41033306)
phenotype: thin heart tubes; lack of craniofacial cartilage; embryonic lethality; developmental abnormalities

citation: A cardiovascular, craniofacial, and neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in the eIF3 complex component genes EIF3A and EIF3B (PMID: 41033306)
summary: De novo or loss-of-function variants in EIF3B were identified in 14 individuals presenting with cardiac defects, craniofacial dysmorphisms, mild developmental delays, and behavioral abnormalities, defining a novel autosomal-dominant neurodevelopmental syndrome. EIF3B is located within the minimally overlapping region implicated in cardiac anomalies associated with 7p22.3 microdeletions. Zebrafish models with mutations in the orthologous eif3ba gene showed thin heart tubes, lack of craniofacial cartilage, and embryonic lethality.

citation: Translation initiation factor eIF3b expression in human cancer and its role in tumor growth and lung colonization (PMID: 23575475)
sample_size: 317 bladder, 566 prostate tissue samples; 143 bladder tumor IHC samples
summary: eIF3b mRNA expression correlated with tumor grade, stage, and survival in human bladder (N=317) and prostate (N=566) cancer tissues, and protein expression stratified survival in bladder cancer. eIF3b depletion by siRNA inhibited G1-S cell-cycle transition by altering protein (but not RNA) levels of cyclin A, E, Rb, and p27Kip1, and reduced integrin α5 expression, disrupting actin cytoskeleton and focal adhesions. eIF3b-depleted bladder cancer cells formed fewer subcutaneous tumors and had reduced lung colonization in vivo.

citation: FOXA1-dependent PUS1 regulates EIF3b stability in a non-enzymatic pathway mediating prostate cancer bone metastasis (PMID: 39247811)
summary: EIF3b acts as a downstream effector of the FOXA1/PUS1 axis in prostate cancer bone metastasis; PUS1 protects EIF3b from ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation through a non-enzymatic mechanism. Overexpression of EIF3b rescued the metastasis suppression caused by PUS1 knockdown, confirming EIF3b as a key mediator. The PUS1 inhibitor Mogroside IV-E reduced PUS1 expression and exerted anti-metastatic effects.

citation: EIF3B‑METTL3 complex promotes cell proliferation, invasion and EGFR/AKT signaling in cervical cancer (PMID: 40576144)
summary: EIF3B physically interacts with METTL3 to form a complex in cervical cancer cells, as confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation; neither protein regulates the other's expression. The EIF3B-METTL3 complex, but not EIF3B alone, promotes cell proliferation, invasion, and activation of the EGFR/AKT signaling pathway, as METTL3 knockdown abolished the oncogenic effects of EIF3B overexpression in HeLa and SiHa cells.

citation: EIF3B stabilizes MAP2K2 to activate the ERK pathway and promote the progression of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 40691141)
summary: EIF3B directly interacts with the P3 domain of MAP2K2 and stabilizes it by inhibiting VHL-mediated ubiquitination at K169, thereby activating ERK/MAPK signaling in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma. EIF3B overexpression accelerated xenograft tumor growth, which was rescued by MAP2K2 knockdown, demonstrating that MAP2K2 kinase activity is essential for EIF3B-driven oncogenic signaling. EIF3B expression was upregulated in LSCC and correlated with poor patient survival.

citation: YTHDF2 Is a Therapeutic Target for HCC by Suppressing Immune Evasion and Angiogenesis Through ETV5/PD-L1/VEGFA Axis (PMID: 38247171)
summary: EIF3B (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit B) is recruited by the m6A reader YTHDF2 to facilitate cap-independent translation of ETV5 mRNA by recognizing m6A modification in its 5'-UTR. This mechanism links EIF3B's translation initiation function to immune evasion and angiogenesis in hepatocellular carcinoma via the ETV5/PD-L1/VEGFA axis.

citation: Prostate cancer cell-derived exosomes inhibit macrophage phagocytosis through EIF3B-mediated exosomal sorting of miR-100-5p (PMID: 40681642)
summary: EIF3B is highly expressed in prostate cancer cells and specifically binds miR-100-5p, mediating its selective sorting into exosomes, as confirmed by pull-down assay. EIF3B knockdown decreased the enrichment of miR-100-5p in PC-3-derived exosomes, revealing a novel non-canonical function of EIF3B in regulating miRNA packaging into exosomes. Transfer of EIF3B-sorted miR-100-5p to macrophages suppressed NOX4-mediated ROS generation and inhibited macrophage phagocytosis.

citation: EIF3B stabilizes PCNA by counteracting SYVN1-mediated ubiquitination to serve as a promotor in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 38687509)
summary: EIF3B is overexpressed in cholangiocarcinoma and correlates with pathological grade; its depletion or overexpression respectively inhibited or enhanced cancer cell survival and migration in vitro. Mechanistically, EIF3B stabilizes PCNA protein by inhibiting SYVN1 E3 ligase-mediated ubiquitination, and PCNA knockdown attenuated the pro-tumorigenic effects of EIF3B overexpression. Elevated P21 protein in shEIF3B cells was partially reversed by a P21 pathway inhibitor, implicating the P21 axis downstream.

citation: The miR-23a/27a/24-2 cluster drives immune evasion and resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 39736629)
summary: eIF3B levels are increased by the miR-23a/27a/24-2 cluster through targeting of MITF (microphthalmia-associated transcription factor), and elevated eIF3B downregulates MHC-I expression, contributing to immune evasion in NSCLC. Pharmacologic targeting of the eIF3B pathway increased MHC-I expression and dramatically sensitized tumors to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in patients with high miR-23a/27a/24-2 cluster expression. This identifies eIF3B as a regulator of antigen presentation and a therapeutic target for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.

citation: eIF3b regulates the cell proliferation and apoptosis processes in chronic myelogenous leukemia cell lines via regulating the expression of C3G (PMID: 32236758)
summary: shRNA-mediated knockdown of eIF3b in CML cell lines (TK-6 and K562) reduced cell viability by ~50% and increased apoptosis ~8-fold compared to controls, without significant effects on S-phase cell cycle distribution. RNA sequencing identified C3G as a downstream target of eIF3b, and in vivo xenograft experiments confirmed that eIF3b inhibition suppressed tumor formation and decreased C3G expression. These findings establish eIF3b as a regulator of proliferation and apoptosis in CML through C3G.

citation: De novo variants in ATXN7L3 lead to developmental delay, hypotonia and distinctive facial features (PMID: 38753057)
variant_detail: c.340C>T; p.(Arg114Ter)
phenotype: global motor developmental delay; language developmental delay; hypotonia; hypertelorism; epicanthal folds; blepharoptosis; small nose; small mouth; low-set posteriorly rotated ears
diagnostic_reason: De novo heterozygous variants identified by exome sequencing; recurrent nonsense variant with reduced ATXN7L3 protein levels in fibroblasts and increased H2Bub1 levels consistent with loss of DUB activity; absent from gnomAD or present at very low frequency; GeneMatcher used to aggregate cases
center_country: Not explicitly stated; multiple centers via GeneMatcher

citation: A Novel ATXN7L3 De Novo Variant Underlies Harel-Tora Neurodevelopmental Syndrome (HATONS) With Pre-Axial Polydactyly (PMID: 41760364)
phenotype: global developmental delay; hypotonia; speech impairment; distinctive facial dysmorphism; pre-axial polydactyly
diagnostic_reason: De novo nonsense variant identified by whole-genome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing; segregates with disease phenotype; RT-qPCR showed marked reduction in ATXN7L3 transcript levels; 3D protein modeling showed substantial structural distortions and loss of C-terminal domain

citation: ATXN7L3 and ENY2 Coordinate Activity of Multiple H2B Deubiquitinases Important for Cellular Proliferation and Tumor Growth (PMID: 27132940)
summary: ATXN7L3 is a non-enzymatic component of the SAGA deubiquitination module (DUBm) that coordinates the activity of multiple H2B deubiquitinases (USP22, USP27X, USP51). Depletion of ATXN7L3 results in increased global H2Bub1 levels (in contrast to USP22 depletion which reduces H2Bub1), and ATXN7L3 competes with USP22 for binding to USP27X and USP51. ATXN7L3 depletion suppresses tumor cell growth, implicating it in cancer-relevant proliferation pathways.

citation: Histone H2Bub1 deubiquitylation is essential for mouse development, but does not regulate global RNA polymerase II transcription (PMID: 33731875)
summary: Atxn7l3 knockout mice show developmental delay as early as embryonic day 7.5 and are embryonic lethal, demonstrating ATXN7L3 is essential for normal mouse development. Atxn7l3-null embryos and derived cell lines show strongly increased global H2Bub1 levels, confirming ATXN7L3 as the key coordinator of multiple DUBs targeting H2Bub1. Transcriptomic analyses of Atxn7l3-/- mouse embryonic stem cells and fibroblasts show that ATXN7L3-related DUB activity regulates only a subset of genes, and increased H2Bub1 does not correlate with global changes in RNA Polymerase II occupancy or elongation.

citation: The tightly controlled deubiquitination activity of the human SAGA complex differentially modifies distinct gene regulatory elements (PMID: 21746879)
summary: ATXN7L3 is a subunit of the human SAGA deubiquitination module (DUBm) that allosterically regulates USP22 activity through interactions with ATXN7 and ENY2. Downregulation of ATXN7L3 by shRNA specifically inactivates SAGA deubiquitination activity, leading to a strong increase in global H2Bub1 and moderate increase in H2Aub1, establishing SAGA as the major H2Bub deubiquitinase in human cells. ATXN7L3-dependent DUB activity is required for full activation of SAGA-dependent inducible genes.

citation: Cytoplasmic ATXN7L3B Interferes with Nuclear Functions of the SAGA Deubiquitinase Module (PMID: 27601583)
summary: ATXN7L3 is a nuclear adaptor protein of the SAGA DUB module that binds ENY2 and is required for USP22-mediated H2Bub1 deubiquitination; overexpression of ATXN7L3 decreases H2Bub1 levels. ATXN7L3B (a cytoplasmic paralog sharing 74% identity with the N-terminal region of ATXN7L3) competes with ATXN7L3 for ENY2 binding in vitro, and a USP22-ATXN7L3B-ENY2 complex cannot efficiently deubiquitinate H2Bub1. This competition mechanism reveals that ATXN7L3's interaction with ENY2 is critical for its function in the SAGA DUBm.

citation: ATXN7L3 positively regulates SMAD7 transcription in hepatocellular carcinoma with growth inhibitory function (PMID: 33186807)
summary: ATXN7L3 is expressed at lower levels in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor samples compared to normal tissue, and lower ATXN7L3 expression positively correlates with poor clinical outcome in HCC patients. ATXN7L3 functions as a coactivator for ERα-mediated transactivation and is recruited to the SMAD7 gene promoter, where it regulates histone H2B ubiquitination to enhance SMAD7 transcription. In vitro colony formation and in vivo xenograft experiments demonstrate that ATXN7L3 suppresses HCC tumor growth.

citation: Enhancer retargeting of CDX2 and UBTF::ATXN7L3 define a subtype of high-risk B-progenitor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 35192684)
sample_size: 3221 newly diagnosed and 177 relapsed B-ALL cases
summary: A focal deletion of exons 18-21 of UBTF at 17q21.31 results in a chimeric UBTF::ATXN7L3 fusion transcript, which together with CDX2 deregulation defines a novel high-risk B-ALL subtype. This fusion arises from aberrant recombination-activating gene (RAG) activation and is found in 17 newly diagnosed and 5 relapsed B-ALL cases with a distinct gene expression profile. Patients with this CDX2/UBTF subtype had high-risk clinical features including 56.3% with relapse or MRD >1% after induction.

citation: Concurrent CDX2 cis-deregulation and UBTF::ATXN7L3 fusion define a novel high-risk subtype of B-cell ALL (PMID: 35316324)
summary: The 17q21.31 microdeletion in B-ALL results in a UBTF::ATXN7L3 fusion transcript encoding a chimeric protein, co-occurring with CDX2 cis-deregulation via PAN3 enhancer hijacking (validated by 4C-sequencing and CRISPR interference). CDX2/UBTF ALL patients (n=17/723 adult Ph- B-ALL) showed dramatically poor treatment response, with 93% having MRD ≥10-4 post-induction and a 75% cumulative incidence of relapse. The subtype was enriched in young females (median age 31, male/female ratio 0.2).

citation: let-7b and let-7c microRNAs promote histone H2B ubiquitylation and inhibit cell migration by targeting multiple components of the H2B deubiquitylation machinery (PMID: 28604753)
summary: ATXN7L3 mRNA is a direct target of let-7b and let-7c microRNAs, which bind and inhibit its expression, leading to increased H2Bub1 levels in multiple cell lines. ATXN7L3 knockdown increases H2Bub1 levels and reduces cell migration in mammary epithelial and breast cancer cells, an anti-migratory effect abolished by simultaneous RNF20 knockdown. These findings identify ATXN7L3 as a component of the H2B deubiquitylation machinery through which let-7 miRNAs exert tumor-suppressive effects.

citation: Metformin ameliorates trophoblastic immunometabolic disorders via attenuating TLR4/NF-κB signaling through ATXN7L3-mediated histone H2B monoubiquitination (PMID: 40209519)
summary: ATXN7L3 was identified via proteomic screening as a mediator of metformin's effects in trophoblasts, where it regulates TLR4/NF-κB signaling through H2B monoubiquitylation. Pharmacologic doses of metformin (10 μM) corrected trophoblastic glycometabolic reprogramming and attenuated excessive inflammation via ATXN7L3-mediated H2Bub1. Chromatin immunoprecipitation and co-immunoprecipitation assays confirmed ATXN7L3's mechanistic role in epigenetic regulation of this inflammatory pathway in placental cells.

citation: Histone H2Bub dynamics in the 5' region of active genes are tightly linked to the UV-induced transcriptional response (PMID: 36659919)
summary: ATXN7L3-containing DUB module knockdown cells were used to demonstrate that deficient ATXN7L3-mediated DUB activity leads to increased RNA Polymerase II elongation rates in both non-irradiated and UV-irradiated conditions. H2Bub levels and patterns depend on intron-exon architecture and closely mirror post-UV dynamics of elongating RNAPII, with ATXN7L3-DUB activity ensuring faithful elongation speed during the DNA damage transcriptional response. These findings establish ATXN7L3 as a key regulator of H2Bub dynamics that couples histone modification to transcription elongation fidelity.

citation: DEAD-box RNA helicase DDX23 modulates glioma malignancy via elevating miR-21 biogenesis. (PMID: 26121981)
summary: DDX23 promotes miR-21 biogenesis by facilitating primary-to-precursor processing through interaction with the Drosha microprocessor, requiring its helicase activity. Knockdown of DDX23 suppressed glioma cell proliferation and invasion in vitro and in vivo, and ivermectin (an RNA helicase inhibitor) decreased miR-21 levels and blocked invasion. DDX23 expression was elevated in glioma tissues compared to normal brain and correlated with poor patient survival.

citation: SRSF1 interactome determined by proximity labeling reveals direct interaction with spliceosomal RNA helicase DDX23. (PMID: 38743621)
summary: DDX23 (also known as PRP28) directly interacts with the SR protein SRSF1, mediated by the N-terminal RS-like domain of DDX23 and both RRM1 and the RS domain of SRSF1, validated by bimolecular fluorescence complementation and in vitro binding assays. DDX23's ATPase activity is essential for the pre-B to B spliceosome complex transition and release of U1 snRNP from the 5' splice site. The RS-like region of DDX23's N-terminal domain is important for spliceosome incorporation, while larger deletions alter subnuclear localization.

citation: Splicing Factor DDX23, Transcriptionally Activated by E2F1, Promotes Ovarian Cancer Progression by Regulating FOXM1. (PMID: 34966670)
summary: DDX23 is upregulated in ovarian cancer and its high expression predicts poor prognosis; silencing DDX23 impeded cell proliferation and invasion in vitro and tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, DDX23 regulates mRNA processing of FOXM1, specifically promoting production of the oncogenic FOXM1C transcript. DDX23 transcription is activated by the transcription factor E2F1, as confirmed by luciferase reporter and ChIP assays.

citation: DEAD-box RNA helicase DDX-23 mediates dietary restriction induced health span in Caenorhabditis elegans. (PMID: 39578298)
summary: In C. elegans, DDX-23 (homolog of mammalian DDX23) functions in the germline during adulthood to regulate dietary restriction-induced longevity and is required for heat and oxidative stress responses. DDX-23 negatively regulates healthy lifespan extension by upregulating miR-231, which suppresses the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16, while PHA-4/FOXA acts downstream of DDX-23 to mediate transcriptional responses of SOD-related genes.

citation: The DDX23 Negatively Regulates Translation and Replication of Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus and Is Degraded by 3C Proteinase. (PMID: 33255534)
summary: DDX23 is a host nuclear helicase and IRES trans-acting factor (ITAF) that negatively regulates FMDV IRES-dependent translation and viral replication; overexpression reduced viral replication while knockout/knockdown increased it. DDX23 interacts with FMDV IRES domains III and IV, and is degraded by FMDV 3C proteinase via the lysosomal pathway. FMDV infection inhibited DDX23 expression, indicating a viral immune evasion strategy.

citation: DDX23-Linc00630-HDAC1 axis activates the Notch pathway to promote metastasis. (PMID: 28473661)
summary: DDX23 binds the promoter of Linc00630 to upregulate its RNA levels in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and elevated Linc00630 in turn stabilizes HDAC1 protein to activate downstream Notch pathway signaling promoting metastasis and proliferation. DDX23 was identified as a Linc00630-binding protein by RNA pull-down and mass spectrometry. This DDX23-Linc00630-HDAC1 axis was associated with tumor size, TNM stage, lymph node status, and poor patient outcomes in a cohort of 90 NSCLC patients.

citation: METTL3 enhances pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression and gemcitabine resistance through modifying DDX23 mRNA N6 adenosine methylation. (PMID: 36977668)
summary: DDX23 mRNA is a direct m6A methylation target of METTL3, regulated in a YTHDF1-dependent manner, leading to enhanced DDX23 expression in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). DDX23 silencing suppressed pancreatic cancer cell malignancy and inactivated PI3K/Akt signaling both in vitro and in vivo. Rescue experiments showed that forced DDX23 expression partially reversed the inhibitory effects of METTL3 silencing on cell phenotypes and gemcitabine resistance.

citation: DDX23 of black carp negatively regulates MAVS-mediated antiviral signaling in innate immune activation. (PMID: 37164277)
summary: Black carp DDX23 (bcDDX23) is mainly nuclear but translocates to the cytoplasm upon SVCV infection, where it interacts with MAVS (mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein) and suppresses MAVS-mediated IFN promoter transcription. Co-expression of bcDDX23 inhibited MAVS-mediated antiviral activity against SVCV in EPC cells, while knockdown of bcDDX23 enhanced host cell resistance to SVCV. This identifies DDX23 as a negative regulator of innate immune IFN signaling in teleost fish.

citation: LncPEDS1-AS promotes UTUC resistance to lipid peroxidation by regulating PEDS1 expression via DDX23. (PMID: 41360761)
summary: DDX23 acts as a splicing factor that interacts with the ultra-long antisense lncRNA LncPEDS1-AS, forming a nuclear RNA-protein complex that facilitates splicing and maturation of PEDS1 pre-mRNA in upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). PEDS1 encodes plasmanylethanolamine desaturase, which protects against lipid peroxidation, and the LncPEDS1-AS-DDX23-PEDS1 axis promotes ROS resistance and poor prognosis in UTUC. Antisense oligonucleotide therapy targeting LncPEDS1-AS suppressed tumor growth and enhanced ROS sensitivity in vitro and in vivo.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Identification of variants underlying biparietal perisylvian polymicrogyria in Finnish families (I. Järvelä et al.)
summary: A de novo or likely de novo pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant in DDX23 was identified by exome sequencing in a Finnish patient with bilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria (BPP), a malformation of cortical development characterized by overfolding of the cerebral cortex and abnormal cortical layering. This finding implicates DDX23 as a candidate gene for a neurodevelopmental disorder involving cortical malformation. The variant was one of six P/LP findings identified in 22 families studied.

phenotype: Developmental defects at multiple stages of B cell differentiation; Dysregulated TLR and BCR signaling pathways; Dysregulated AKT/FOXO1 pathway in B cells; Altered Lys63 ubiquitination in immune cells

citation: Loss of G-Protein Pathway Suppressor 2 Promotes Tumor Growth Through Activation of AKT Signaling. (PMID: 33490071)
phenotype: Increased tumor burden in orthotopic xenograft model; Enhanced proliferative properties of breast cancer cells in vivo; Increased migratory and invasive properties; Activation of PI3K/AKT signaling; Pro-oncogenic phenotypes rescued by AKT inhibitor MK2206

citation: Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening identified G protein pathway suppressor 2 as a novel tumor suppressor for uveal melanoma metastasis. (PMID: 35941228)
phenotype: Promoted proliferation of uveal melanoma cells in vivo; Promoted metastatic abilities of uveal melanoma cells in vivo; Upregulation of MAPK and PI3K-Akt oncogenic signaling pathways; Downregulation of Slit/Robo tumor suppressor signaling pathway

citation: G protein pathway suppressor 2 suppresses aerobic glycolysis through RACK1-mediated HIF-1α degradation in breast cancer. (PMID: 38942092)
sample_size: 21 BC cases plus in vitro/in vivo models
summary: GPS2 suppresses aerobic glycolysis in breast cancer cells by destabilizing HIF-1α, reducing transcription of downstream glycolytic regulators (PGK1, PGAM1, ENO1, PKM2, LDHA, PDK1/2/4). GPS2 directly binds RACK1 via its N-terminal residues 70-92 aa, stabilizing the HIF-1α/RACK1 interaction and promoting HIF-1α polyubiquitination and degradation. GPS2 is low-expressed in breast cancer tissues and negatively correlated with poor prognosis.

citation: Liquid-liquid phase separation of GPS2-LATS1 promotes colorectal cancer progression by reprogramming lipid metabolism. (PMID: 40715488)
summary: GPS2 is overexpressed in colorectal cancer and acts as an oncogenic driver by undergoing liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) via its coiled-coil domain. Phase-separated GPS2 interacts with the kinase domain of LATS1, inducing LATS1 LLPS and suppressing its activity, thereby releasing YAP to amplify SREBP1/PPARα-driven lipid metabolism. GPS2 depletion inhibits tumor growth in vitro and in vivo, while overexpression accelerates malignancy.

citation: Inhibition of K63 ubiquitination by G-Protein pathway suppressor 2 (GPS2) regulates mitochondria-associated translation. (PMID: 39094987)
summary: GPS2 inhibits non-proteolytic K63 ubiquitination mediated by the E2 enzyme Ubc13, with targets enriched for RNA-binding and translation proteins on the outer mitochondrial membrane, including PABPC1, RPS1, RACK1, and eIF3M. Removal of GPS2-mediated inhibition (via genetic deletion or stress-induced nuclear translocation) promotes import-coupled translation of selected mRNAs, increasing expression of an adaptive antioxidant program. This reveals GPS2 as a regulator of nuclear-mitochondria communication through spatially coordinated transcription and translation.

citation: Antagonistic action of GPS2 and KDM1A at enhancers governs alternative macrophage activation by interleukin 4. (PMID: 36610795)
summary: GPS2, as a core subunit of the HDAC3/SMRT/NCOR corepressor complex, represses IL4-dependent enhancer activation in mouse macrophages by antagonizing the lysine demethylase KDM1A (LSD1). Corepressor depletion increased KDM1A recruitment to enhancers of IL4-induced genes, causing demethylation of repressive H3K9me2/3 marks and enhancer/gene activation even in the absence of IL4/STAT6. This identifies a novel epigenetic corepressor-coactivator switching mechanism governing alternative macrophage activation.

citation: GPS2 promotes erythroid differentiation by control of the stability of EKLF protein. (PMID: 32384137)
summary: GPS2 interacts with the erythroid transcription factor EKLF/KLF1 and prevents its proteasome-mediated degradation, thereby increasing EKLF stability and transcriptional activity. Knockdown of GPS2 significantly suppresses erythroid differentiation of human CD34+ cells in vitro and in xenotransplantation models, and global GPS2 deletion in mice causes impaired fetal liver erythropoiesis and severe anemia. The GPS2-binding region maps to amino acids 191-230 of EKLF, which is highly conserved in mammals.

citation: GPS2 regulates embryonic angiogenesis by enhancing endothelial cell survival through stabilizing HOIP. (PMID: 41507360)
summary: EC-specific GPS2 knockout mice (Gps2ECKO) are embryonic lethal at E16.5 due to defective vascularization caused by aberrant TNFR1-mediated endothelial cell death. GPS2 binds the NZF domain of HOIP and inhibits K48-linked polyubiquitination at K579, K737, and K988, preventing HOIP proteasomal degradation and maintaining LUBAC stability and NF-κB activation. TNFR1 deletion in Gps2ECKO mice restores normal vascularization and rescues embryonic lethality.

citation: GPS2 confers l-asparaginase resistance in acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through ATF4/ASNS axis. (PMID: 40693356)
summary: GPS2 binds ATF4 and stabilizes it by impairing the interaction between ATF4 and the E3 ligase BTRC, thereby inhibiting ubiquitin-proteasome degradation of ATF4 and upregulating downstream asparagine synthetase (ASNS). GPS2 knockdown sensitizes ALL cells to l-asparaginase treatment in vitro and increases l-ASP efficacy against xenografted ALL tumors in vivo. These findings identify GPS2 as a positive regulator of the ATF4/ASNS axis conferring chemotherapy resistance.

citation: Recurrent FOXK1::GRHL and GPS2::GRHL fusions in trichogerminoma. (PMID: 35049062)
summary: RNA sequencing of trichogerminoma tumors identified recurrent in-frame GPS2::GRHL1, GPS2::GRHL2, and GPS2::GRHL3 fusion transcripts in 4 of 21 cases, alongside FOXK1::GRHL1/2 fusions. These gene fusions were not detected in other follicular tumor entities or basal cell carcinomas, suggesting GRHL gene rearrangements (including GPS2 as a fusion partner) may be the oncogenic driver in this subset of follicular tumors. The GPS2::GRHL fusions were validated by RT-qPCR and RNA-seq.

citation: Inherited Thrombocytopenia Related Genes: GPS2 Mediates the Interplay Between ANKRD26 and ETV6. (PMID: 39791724)
summary: GPS2, as a component of the NCoR complex, binds both ANKRD26 and ETV6, mediating their interaction and contributing to cytoplasmic retention of ETV6. ANKRD26 overexpression deregulates ETV6 transcriptional repression, and GPS2 is identified as the molecular bridge in a novel ANKRD26-ETV6-GPS2 axis relevant to inherited thrombocytopenias with predisposition to myeloid neoplasms. This provides mechanistic insight into how mutations in ANKRD26 may phenocopy ETV6-related thrombocytopenia.

citation: GPS2-mediated regulation of the adipocyte secretome modulates adipose tissue remodeling at the onset of diet-induced obesity. (PMID: 36731652)
summary: Adipocyte-specific GPS2 knockout (GPS2-AKO) mice fed a high-fat diet are significantly more inflamed, insulin resistant, and obese compared to wild-type counterparts, demonstrating GPS2's role in metabolic adaptation. Loss of GPS2 in adipocytes alters the exosomal secretome, promoting a TGFβ-driven fibrotic microenvironment and anti-adipogenic stromal cell composition. Single-cell RNA sequencing and proteomics revealed that GPS2 regulates intercellular communication between adipocytes and stromal cells during early obesity.

phenotype: Expanded retinal progenitor cell clones in cadm3-disrupted retinae; Increased retinal total cell number when Cadm3 lacking extracellular ig1 domain was overexpressed in RPCs; Recapitulation of clonal expansion phenotype seen in p15+ host retinae upon cadm3 disruption; Loss of coordinated proliferation in retinal neuroepithelium

phenotype: Single Cadm3 null mice: no overt axonal organization abnormalities on their own; Cadm3-/-/Cadm2-/- double mutants: abnormal distribution of Caspr and Kv1 potassium channels, phenocopying Cadm4 null mice; Cadm3-/-/Cadm1-/- double mutants: abnormal distribution of Caspr and Kv1 potassium channels; Cadm1-/-/Cadm2-/- double mutants: no significant axonal organization abnormalities; Cadm3 null mice heterozygous for Cadm2 and Cadm1: axonal organization abnormalities detected; Cadm3 identified as the main axonal ligand for glial Cadm4 in peripheral nervous system

phenotype: Cadm3 single knockout mice: no peripheral nervous system myelin abnormalities reported; Cadm3 null mice do not develop focal hypermyelination, tomacula, or myelin outfoldings; No abnormal axon-glial contact or redistribution of ion channels in Cadm3 single knockouts; Cadm3 expressed by sensory and motor neurons

citation: Necl-1/CADM3 regulates cone synapse formation in the mouse retina. (PMID: 38623325)
summary: Necl-1/CADM3 is localized at S- and S/M-opsin-containing cones and dendrites of type 4 OFF cone bipolar cells in the mouse retina. In Necl-1-/- mice, synapses between cones and type 4 OFF CBCs were dislocated, AMPA receptors were mislocalized, and short-wavelength-light-elicited signal transmission was aberrant. These findings establish CADM3 as a regulator of cone synapse formation mediating OFF cone pathways.

citation: A CADM3 variant causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease with marked upper limb involvement. (PMID: 33889941)
summary: A missense variant Tyr172Cys in CADM3 was identified in three unrelated families with axonal CMT2; mass spectrometry revealed a novel disulfide bond in the mutant protein, and in vitro studies showed retention of mutant CADM3 in the endoplasmic reticulum with reduced cell surface expression. STORM imaging demonstrated decreased co-localization of mutant CADM3 with CADM4 at intercellular contact sites. Knock-in mice (Cadm3Y170C) showed abnormal axonal organization including mislocalization of Kv1.2 channels and Caspr, supporting a disease mechanism involving disrupted axon-glia interaction.

citation: Differential Contribution of Cadm1-Cadm3 Cell Adhesion Molecules to Peripheral Myelinated Axons. (PMID: 33397712)
summary: Genetic ablation studies in mice showed that Cadm3 is the primary axonal ligand for glial Cadm4, as triple knockout of Cadm1/2/3 phenocopied Cadm4 null abnormalities in Caspr and Kv1 channel distribution. Double mutants lacking Cadm3 with either Cadm2 or Cadm1 also showed defects, but Cadm1/Cadm2 double knockouts did not, establishing a hierarchical adhesion code with Cadm3 at the apex. Cadm2 and Cadm1 can compensate for Cadm3 loss in combination but not individually.

citation: Cadm3 (Necl-1) interferes with the activation of the PI3 kinase/Akt signaling cascade and inhibits Schwann cell myelination in vitro. (PMID: 27658374)
summary: shRNA-mediated knockdown of axonal Cadm3 in DRG neurons promoted Schwann cell myelination in vitro, while Cadm3 overexpression nearly abolished myelin segment formation. The extracellular domain of Cadm3 dose-dependently inhibited ErbB3 activation and the pro-myelinating PI3K/Akt pathway without affecting Mek/Erk1/2 signaling. These results identify Cadm3 as a negative regulator of PNS myelination acting through selective modulation of PI3K/Akt signaling in Schwann cells.

citation: Clinical significance of low expression of CADM3 in breast cancer and preliminary exploration of related mechanisms. (PMID: 38515057)
summary: CADM3 expression was significantly lower in breast cancer tissues than adjacent normal tissues, and high CADM3 correlated with better prognosis and was an independent prognostic factor. Overexpression of CADM3 in breast cancer cell lines notably reduced cell proliferation and migration in clonal formation, CCK-8, scratch, and Transwell assays. Mechanistically, high CADM3 was associated with inhibition of ERK1/2 and JNK1 phosphorylation, implicating the MAPK pathway.

citation: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcomas with PRDM10 fusions have a distinct gene expression profile. (PMID: 31313299)
summary: RNA-seq of PRDM10-rearranged tumors (PRT) identified CADM3 as one of the most consistently and highly upregulated genes compared to high-grade undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcomas and other soft tissue tumors. Conditional expression of the CITED2-PRDM10 fusion in fibroblasts also induced high CADM3 expression, and ATAC-seq showed enrichment of PRDM10 binding sites near CADM3, suggesting CADM3 is a direct transcriptional target of PRDM10. CADM3 protein expression was confirmed by immunohistochemistry.

citation: The peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonist rosiglitazone specifically represses tumour metastatic potential in chromatin inaccessibility-mediated FABP4-deficient gastric cancer. (PMID: 35198079)
summary: In gastric cancer, FABP4 binding to PPAR-γ facilitated nuclear translocation of PPAR-γ, which transcriptionally activated CADM3 to suppress metastasis. FABP4 depletion reduced PPAR-γ-mediated CADM3 transcription, promoting metastatic behavior in vitro and in vivo. The PPAR-γ agonist rosiglitazone restored CADM3 expression in FABP4-deficient cells and reversed metastatic properties in multiple mouse models.

citation: Localization of Cadm2a and Cadm3 proteins during development of the zebrafish nervous system. (PMID: 21456004)
summary: Subtype-specific antibodies revealed that cadm3 is broadly expressed throughout the nervous system of larval zebrafish, with particularly striking and largely non-overlapping expression compared to cadm2a in the developing retina and spinal cord. In vitro binding assays showed cadm3 binds heterophilically and preferentially to cadm4, consistent with tetrapod Cadm binding preferences. This study establishes cadm3 protein localization as a prerequisite for understanding its diverse functions during vertebrate nervous system development.

citation: Circ004463 promotes fibroblast proliferation and collagen I synthesis by sponging miR-23b and regulating CADM3/MAP4K4 via activation of AKT/ERK pathways. (PMID: 36502948)
summary: In pig skin fibroblasts, the circRNA circ0044633 acts as a sponge for miR-23b, thereby upregulating CADM3 and MAP4K4 expression and activating downstream AKT and ERK pathways to promote fibroblast proliferation, myofibroblast transition, and collagen I synthesis. Overexpression of circ004463 increased mouse skin thickness and collagen I content in vivo. This identifies a circ0044633-miR-23b-CADM3/MAP4K4 axis as a regulator of skin thickness development.

citation: Peptidomic analysis of CSF reveals new biomarker candidates for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. (PMID: 40681694)
summary: Mass-spectrometry-based peptidomic analysis of CSF identified CADM3-derived peptides as significantly downregulated in ALS patients compared to non-neurodegenerative controls in both discovery and validation cohorts. CADM3 peptide levels were not altered in other neurodegenerative diseases (Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, Parkinson's disease), suggesting ALS-specific relevance. A logistic regression model combining CADM3 peptides with other candidates achieved an AUC of 98% for discriminating ALS from controls.

citation: Regulators of PP2C phosphatase activity function as abscisic acid sensors (PMID: 19407143)
summary: ABI2 (a type 2C protein phosphatase) was identified as a negative regulator of ABA responses in Arabidopsis. RCAR1 was shown to bind ABA and mediate ABA-dependent inactivation of ABI2 in vitro, and other RCARs also mediated ABA-dependent regulation of ABI2, consistent with combinatorial assembly of receptor complexes.

citation: The ABI1 and ABI2 protein phosphatases 2C act in a negative feedback regulatory loop of the abscisic acid signalling pathway (PMID: 11208021)
summary: ABI2 encodes a protein serine/threonine phosphatase 2C (PP2C) that acts as a negative regulator of ABA signaling in Arabidopsis. A reduction-of-function allele (abi2-1R1) with ~100-fold lower phosphatase activity, combined with a loss-of-function ABI1 allele, produced plants more responsive to ABA than either single mutant. PP2C activity of ABI2 increases in response to ABA, indicating ABI2 acts in a negative feedback regulatory loop.

citation: ABI INSENSITIVE 2 promotes flowering by inhibiting OST1/ABI5-dependent FLOWERING LOCUS C transcription in Arabidopsis (PMID: 38280208)
summary: ABI2 is the only phosphatase from the ABA-signaling core that positively regulates flowering transition in Arabidopsis; loss-of-function abi2-2 mutants show significantly delayed flowering under both long and short day conditions. ABI2 promotes flowering by dephosphorylating ABI5, reducing its stability and capacity to induce FLC expression. OST1 and ABI5 loss-of-function mutations are epistatic to abi2-2, rescuing the late-flowering phenotype.

citation: Phytocytokine signalling reopens stomata in plant immunity and water loss (PMID: 35508659)
summary: SCREW peptides sensed by the NUT receptor kinase trigger NUT-dependent phosphorylation of ABI2 (and ABI1), increasing ABI2 phosphatase activity toward OST1 kinase and reducing S-type anion channel activity, thereby promoting stomatal reopening. This places ABI2 as a key node linking immune phytocytokine signaling to ABA-mediated stomatal regulation.

citation: Ethylene antagonizes ABA responses in stomatal movement and seed germination by upregulating ABI1 and ABI2 at both the transcript and protein levels (PMID: 40811817)
summary: Ethylene upregulates ABI2 gene expression and protein accumulation in the presence of ABA via the EIN2-EIN3 signaling pathway, with ethylene-responsive factors directly regulating ABI2 transcription. Ethylene also enhances ABI2 protein stability by inhibiting ABA-induced degradation. Loss-of-function abi2 mutants demonstrate that ABI2 is a principal PP2C mediating ethylene-ABA crosstalk in stomatal movement and seed germination.

citation: PIM1 phosphorylates ABI2 to enhance actin dynamics and promote tumor invasion (PMID: 37042842)
summary: In prostate cancer cells, ABI2 (Abl-interactor 2) was identified as a PIM1 kinase substrate via unbiased proteomics; phosphorylation of ABI2 at Ser183 by PIM1 increased ABI2 protein levels and enhanced Wave Regulatory Complex (WRC) formation, resulting in increased protrusive activity and cell motility. Cell protrusion induced by hypoxia and/or PIM1 was dependent on ABI2, and in vivo smooth muscle invasion assays showed PIM1 overexpression increased tumor invasion depth.

citation: ABI2-deficient mice exhibit defective cell migration, aberrant dendritic spine morphogenesis, and deficits in learning and memory (PMID: 15572692)
summary: Homozygous deletion of murine Abi2 caused defective secondary lens fiber migration, cell migration defects in the neocortex and hippocampus, abnormal dendritic spine morphology and density, and severe deficits in short- and long-term memory. Abi2 localizes to adherens junctions and dendritic spines, and its loss correlated with downregulation of the Wave actin-nucleation promoting factor, supporting a role in cytoskeletal dynamics critical for intercellular connectivity and cognitive function.

citation: Inhibition of ABI2 ubiquitination-dependent degradation suppresses TNBC cell growth via down-regulating PI3K/Akt signaling pathway (PMID: 38937761)
summary: ABI2 is expressed at low levels in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) tumors and functions as a tumor suppressor by controlling cell cycle and inhibiting TNBC cell migration, invasion, and proliferation. E3 ligase CBLC promotes ubiquitination-dependent degradation of ABI2, and ABI2 inhibits the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway through interaction with Rho GTPase RAC1. FDA-approved drug Colistimethate sodium was identified as suppressing TNBC proliferation by targeting ABI2.

citation: Downregulation of ABI2 expression by EBV-miR-BART13-3p induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition of nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells through upregulation of c-JUN/SLUG signaling (PMID: 31907338)
summary: EBV-miR-BART13-3p directly targets ABI2 in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) cells, reducing ABI2 expression and driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) via activation of c-JUN/SLUG signaling. Silencing ABI2 phenocopied EBV-miR-BART13-3p overexpression (increased migration and invasion), while reconstitution of ABI2 reversed these effects. ABI2 expression levels in NPC tissue samples correlated with N stages of NPC patients.

citation: ASHG 2010 - GxG interactions potentially account for the blood pressure linkage peak on chromosome 2 in the Old Order Amish (Montasser et al.)
significance: LOD score reduced by up to 34% per pair; combination reduced LOD by 85%
summary: In a fine-mapping study of a diastolic blood pressure QTL on chromosome 2q31-34 in 762 Old Order Amish individuals, intronic SNPs in ABI2 were among 19 SNPs showing gene-by-gene interaction evidence. A combination of 6 SNP pairs (including the ABI2 intronic SNP) accounted for 18% of total DBP variation and reduced the linkage LOD score by 85%.

citation: A role for ATF2 in regulating MITF and melanoma development (PMID: 21203491)

phenotype: Atf2 upregulated in brains of doxorubicin-treated mice compared to controls; Gene expression changes associated with neuronal transmission and oxidative stress in doxorubicin-related cognitive impairment

phenotype: Atf2 evaluated as candidate gene for alcohol preference QTL on chromosome 2 but not confirmed for a definitive role in regulation of alcohol preference

citation: ATF2 orchestrates macrophage differentiation and activation to promote antibacterial responses (PMID: 37403209)
summary: ATF2 expression and activity are precisely regulated during human monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation, and its activation is linked to M1 polarization and antibacterial responses. Genetic deletion of ATF2 in THP-1 cells caused abnormal macrophage morphology, while overexpression produced round M1-like morphology with increased MHC-II, IL-1β, and IP-10 production, enhanced phagocytosis, and improved control of intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis. ATF2 overexpression or stimuli-induced activation also reprogrammed macrophage metabolism toward glycolysis during M1 polarization or bacterial infection.

citation: Increased ATF2 expression predicts poor prognosis and inhibits sorafenib-induced ferroptosis in gastric cancer (PMID: 36473315)
summary: ATF2 is significantly upregulated in gastric cancer tissues and predicts poor clinical prognosis. ATF2 knockdown promoted sorafenib-induced ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells, while overexpression inhibited it; ChIP-Seq and RNA-Seq identified HSPH1 as a direct ATF2 transcriptional target that stabilizes SLC7A11 protein to suppress ferroptosis. In vivo xenograft experiments confirmed that ATF2 knockdown enhances sorafenib sensitivity.

citation: MG53 protects against septic cardiac dysfunction by ubiquitinating ATF2 (PMID: 40107350)
summary: MG53 physically interacts with ATF2 and promotes its ubiquitination, leading to reduced ATF2-mediated transcriptional activation of TLR4 in cardiomyocytes. In a mouse LPS-induced septic cardiac dysfunction model, MG53 overexpression or exogenous administration reduced TLR4 expression, cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and inflammatory cytokine levels. This identifies ATF2 as an essential transcription factor for TLR4 expression in the heart.

citation: Identification of a lipid oxygen radical defense pathway and its epigenetic control (PMID: 41372219)
summary: ATF2 is a component of a repressive epigenetic complex (with ZNF354A, KAP1/TRIM28, and SETDB1) that silences the Lipid Oxygen Radical Defense (LORD) pathway under basal conditions. Upon lipid peroxide accumulation, p38- and JNK-dependent phosphorylation of ATF2 leads to disassembly of this complex and activation of protective genes including NRF2 targets. This positions ATF2 as a key sensor-effector in the cellular response to oxidative stress and ferroptosis.

citation: TRAF6-p38/JNK-ATF2 axis promotes microglial inflammatory activation (PMID: 30763583)
summary: In LPS-induced neuroinflammation, ATF2 is upregulated, phosphorylated, and translocates to the nucleus in microglia, co-localizing with microglia in inflamed mouse brain. Inhibiting ATF2 decreased pro-inflammatory factor expression in LPS-treated BV2 microglia and reduced neuronal apoptosis caused by conditioned medium from activated microglia. TRAF6 knockdown suppressed LPS-induced ATF2 expression and phosphorylation via reduced p38/JNK signaling, establishing the TRAF6-p38/JNK-ATF2 axis as a pro-inflammatory pathway in the CNS.

citation: OGT-Mediated O-GlcNAcylation of ATF2 Protects Against Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy by Inhibiting Microglial Pyroptosis (PMID: 40411666)
summary: OGT-mediated O-GlcNAcylation of ATF2 at Ser44 inhibits ATF2 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, thereby suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and inflammatory cytokine production in microglia. OGT deficiency augmented microglial pyroptosis and worsened sepsis-associated encephalopathy in mice, while OGT inhibition impaired cognitive function. This reveals a post-translational modification of ATF2 that modulates its activity and downstream neuroinflammatory signaling.

citation: Stimulus-Dependent Expression of Bdnf Is Mediated by ATF2, MYT1L, and EGR1 Transcription Factors (PMID: 39947922)
summary: ATF2 directly binds to Bdnf promoters in cultured rat neurons and in vivo, as demonstrated by chromatin immunoprecipitation assays, and functionally regulates Bdnf gene expression. ATF2 participates in Bdnf regulation specifically after BDNF-TrkB signaling (as part of the AP1 family response), and competes with CREB and other AP1 family members at Bdnf promoter cis-elements. This identifies ATF2 as a novel regulator of stimulus-dependent Bdnf transcription in neurons.

citation: MAP4K4 and WT1 mediate SOX6-induced cellular senescence by synergistically activating the ATF2-TGFβ2-Smad2/3 signaling pathway in cervical cancer (PMID: 38383842)
summary: ATF2 acts as a downstream transcriptional effector of both the MAP4K4-MAPK (JNK/ERK/p38) and WT1 pathways to promote TGFB2 gene expression, which in turn activates the TGFβ2-Smad2/3-p53-p21-Rb senescence pathway in cervical cancer cells. SOX6-induced cellular senescence in cervical cancer is dependent on this MAP4K4/WT1-ATF2-TGFβ2 axis. Senescent cells induced through this pathway are resistant to cisplatin but sensitive to senolytics ABT-263 and ABT-199.

citation: SIRT6 Lysine-Demyristoylates ATF2 to Ameliorate Vascular Injury via PRKCD/VE-Cadherin Pathway Regulating Vascular Endothelial Barrier (PMID: 40810740)
summary: SIRT6 demyristoylates ATF2 at lysine K296, regulating its nucleoplasmic translocation; decreased nuclear ATF2 results in reduced PRKCD expression, establishing a SIRT6/Myr-ATF2/PRKCD/VE-Cadherin pathway that enhances endothelial barrier integrity. These findings were validated in gene overexpression/knockdown cell lines and in SIRT6 knockout/double-transgenic mice. This identifies lysine myristoylation as a novel post-translational modification controlling ATF2 localization and vascular function.

citation: ATF2/BAP1 Axis Mediates Neuronal Apoptosis After Subarachnoid Hemorrhage via P53 Pathway (PMID: 38965653)
summary: ATF2 regulates BAP1 expression by directly binding to the BAP1 promoter in neurons, as demonstrated by luciferase and co-immunoprecipitation assays in a subarachnoid hemorrhage model. BAP1 overexpression enhanced P53 activity and stability by reducing proteasome-mediated P53 degradation, promoting neuronal apoptosis. Inhibition of the neuronal BAP1/P53 axis significantly reduced neurological deficits and neuronal apoptosis in mice after SAH, identifying ATF2 as an upstream transcriptional regulator of this pro-apoptotic cascade.
