citation: Disrupting the phase separation of KAT8-IRF1 diminishes PD-L1 expression and promotes antitumor immunity (PMID: 36894639)
summary: In response to IFNγ, KAT8 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation with IRF1 to form biomolecular condensates that upregulate PD-L1 expression. KAT8-IRF1 condensation promotes IRF1 K78 acetylation and its binding to the CD274 (PD-L1) promoter, enriching the transcription apparatus. A blocking peptide (2142-R8) that disrupts KAT8-IRF1 condensate formation inhibits PD-L1 expression and enhances antitumor immunity in vitro and in vivo.

citation: KAT8-mediated H4K16ac is essential for sustaining trophoblast self-renewal and proliferation via regulating CDX2 (PMID: 38961108)
summary: Trophoblast-specific deletion of Kat8 in mice caused extraembryonic ectoderm abnormalities and embryonic lethality. In trophoblast stem cells, KAT8 regulates transcriptional activation of the stemness marker CDX2 via H4K16 acetylation, and CDX2 overexpression partially rescues Kat8 knockout defects. Reduced KAT8, CDX2, and H4K16ac expression were associated with recurrent pregnancy loss in clinical samples.

citation: Stabilization of MOF (KAT8) by USP10 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma proliferation and metastasis through epigenetic activation of ANXA2/Wnt signaling (PMID: 38317006)
summary: KAT8 (MOF) is highly expressed in ESCC tumors and its depletion impedes tumor growth and metastasis in vitro and in vivo; catalytically inactive KAT8 (E350Q mutant) fails to promote ESCC progression, indicating acetyltransferase activity is essential. USP10 deubiquitinates KAT8 at K410 to prevent its proteasomal degradation, and stabilized KAT8 promotes H4K16ac enrichment at the ANXA2 promoter to activate ANXA2 transcription and downstream Wnt/β-catenin signaling.

citation: CHI-KAT8i5 suppresses ESCC tumor growth by inhibiting KAT8-mediated c-Myc stability (PMID: 39772391)
summary: KAT8 is identified as a prognostic and therapeutic biomarker in ESCC; esophageal-tissue-specific KAT8 deletion in mice reduced tumor burden after 4-NQO-induced tumorigenesis. KAT8 directly binds c-Myc to regulate its protein stability, and a specific KAT8 inhibitor (CHI-KAT8i5) significantly attenuates tumor growth in CDX and PDX models in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Mitochondrial MOF regulates energy metabolism in heart failure via ATP5B hyperacetylation (PMID: 39392752)
summary: KAT8 (MOF) is upregulated in mitochondria during heart failure, and overexpression of mitochondria-targeted MOF in mouse models causes mitochondrial dysfunction, cardiac remodeling, and heart failure. KAT8 acetylates ATP5B at K201, co-regulated with SIRT3, impairing mitochondrial respiration and energy metabolism. These findings reveal a non-histone, mitochondrial role for KAT8 in cardiac pathology.

citation: KAT8 is upregulated and recruited to the promoter of Atg8 by FOXO to induce H4 acetylation for autophagy under 20-hydroxyecdysone regulation (PMID: 38309506)
summary: In the lepidopteran insect Helicoverpa armigera, the transcription factor FOXO promotes KAT8 expression and recruits KAT8 to the Atg8 promoter to increase H4K16ac and enable autophagy during metamorphosis. RNAi knockdown of Kat8 delayed pupation, repressed midgut autophagy, and decreased H4K16ac levels, while KAT8 overexpression promoted autophagy. KAT8 also acetylates FOXO at K180/K183 to further promote autophagy gene transcription.

citation: Targeting KAT8 alleviates self-RNA-driven skin inflammation by modulating histone H4 lysine 16 acetylation in psoriasis (PMID: 40691280)
summary: H4K16ac levels are significantly elevated in macrophages of lesional skin from psoriasis patients and mice, positively correlating with self-RNA accumulation and disease pathology. KAT8 is responsible for self-RNA/TLR7-driven H4K16ac modification and is selectively recruited to promoters of pathogenic chemokines (Cxcl2, Ccl3) via interaction with the AP-1 transcription complex. KAT8 deficiency in macrophages or pharmacological inhibition restricted pro-inflammatory chemokine secretion and ameliorated experimental psoriasis and arthritis.

citation: ASHG 2019 - Variant-to-gene mapping for Alzheimer's disease using 3D genomics in an activated microglia human cell line (ASHG 2019)
summary: Using Capture C chromatin conformation and ATAC-seq in IFNγ-activated human microglia (HMC3), a chromatin loop was identified connecting an AD GWAS locus to the KAT8 promoter, implicating KAT8 as a candidate effector gene for an Alzheimer's disease GWAS signal. This interaction was only observed in activated (not resting) microglia, suggesting context-dependent regulatory relevance. Follow-up functional studies were noted as required to validate this finding.

citation: Lysine butyrylation of HSP90 regulated by KAT8 and HDAC11 confers chemoresistance (PMID: 37460462)
summary: KAT8 acts as the writer enzyme for lysine butyrylation (Kbu) of HSP90 at K754 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, cooperating with HDAC11 as the eraser to regulate this modification. Kbu of HSP90 K754 leads to HSP90 overexpression and contributes to 5-FU chemoresistance, with elevated levels in relapse samples predicting poor prognosis. This identifies KAT8 as a writer for a non-acetyl acylation mark on a non-histone substrate linked to drug resistance.

citation: A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome (PMID: 41290615)
variant_detail: p.Tyr654Ser
phenotype: delayed speech development; joint contractures; dysmorphic features; dysmotility of the gut; multisystem disorder
diagnostic_reason: de novo heterozygous variant in two unrelated individuals with the same variant; functional evidence showing elevated deacetylase activity due to displacement of conserved auto-inhibitory loop; reciprocal gene expression changes in patient fibroblasts compared to MiDAC-degraded cell line; variant located in conserved region revealed by cryoEM structure

citation: The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure. (PMID: 32591534)
phenotype: Embryonic lethality during late embryogenesis; Heart malformation; Haematopoietic failure; Perturbations in gene expression; Identical phenotype to DNTTIP1 knockout

citation: Structural and functional characterization of a cell cycle associated HDAC1/2 complex reveals the structural basis for complex assembly and nucleosome targeting. (PMID: 25653165)
summary: MIDEAS is identified as a corepressor protein in a novel histone deacetylase complex upregulated during mitosis and associated with cyclin A, conserved from nematodes to humans. DNTTIP1 interacts with and mediates assembly of the HDAC1:MIDEAS complex, with DNTTIP1 acting as a dimeric chromatin binding module within this corepressor complex. The complex contains HDAC1/2, MIDEAS, and DNTTIP1.

citation: The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure. (PMID: 32591534)
summary: Mice lacking MIDEAS die with identical phenotypes to DNTTIP1 knockout mice during late embryogenesis due to perturbations in gene expression resulting in heart malformation and haematopoietic failure. MiDAC is important for chromosome alignment during mitosis in cancer cell lines. CryoEM structure reveals four copies of HDAC1 positioned at the periphery with outward-facing active sites, suggesting the complex may target multiple nucleosomes in a processive deacetylase function.

citation: The histone deacetylase complex MiDAC regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program to control neurite outgrowth. (PMID: 32297854)
summary: MiDAC (containing MIDEAS) functions as a modulator of a neurodevelopmental gene expression program, upregulating pro-neural genes such as SLIT3 and NETRIN1 via H4K20ac removal on promoters and enhancers, while inhibiting negative regulators of neurogenesis by reducing H3K27ac. Loss of MiDAC results in neurite outgrowth defects that can be rescued by supplementation with SLIT3 and/or NTN1. These findings establish a crucial role for MiDAC in regulating ligands of the SLIT3 and NTN1 signaling axes for proper neurite development.

citation: A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome. (PMID: 41290615)
summary: MIDEAS is a scaffold protein that mediates assembly of the MiDAC histone deacetylase complex, and a de novo heterozygous missense variant (p.Tyr654Ser) in two unrelated individuals causes a multisystem disorder with delayed speech development, joint contractures, dysmorphic features, and gut dysmotility. CryoEM structure reveals that Tyr654 is located in a conserved auto-inhibitory loop covering the deacetylase active site, and the variant likely causes loop displacement leading to elevated deacetylase activity. Reciprocal gene expression changes in patient fibroblasts compared to MiDAC-degraded cell lines support a gain-of-function mechanism, establishing MIDEAS as a dominant monogenic disease gene.

citation: Mitotic deacetylase complex (MiDAC) recognizes the HIV-1 core promoter to control activated viral gene expression. (PMID: 38781120)
summary: MIDEAS, as a subunit of the MiDAC complex, was identified via DNA-affinity chromatography as selectively recognizing the TASHET sequence of the HIV-1 core promoter. Co-immunoprecipitation assays confirmed that DNTTIP1 interacts with MIDEAS and HDAC1/2. Gene silencing of MIDEAS revealed a functional role in HIV expression in cellulo, identifying MIDEAS as a cell cycle-regulated host cell transcription factor controlling activated HIV gene expression and a potential drug target for HIV cure strategies.

citation: Mutations on the surface of HDAC1 reveal molecular determinants of specific complex assembly and their requirement for gene regulation. (PMID: 40966515)
summary: Comparative structural analysis of MTA1:HDAC1 and MIDEAS:HDAC1 identified critical binding residues on the surface of HDAC1, with Y48 interacting with ELM2/SANT domain-containing proteins including MIDEAS. The HDAC1-E63R mutation shows markedly reduced binding to MiDAC (and NuRD) complexes, indicating E63 is important for MIDEAS interaction. In mouse embryonic stem cells, HDAC1 was found distributed across six complexes including MiDAC, with the full repertoire of complexes required for appropriate transcriptome regulation.

citation: DNA methylation in peripheral blood leukocytes in late onset Alzheimer's disease. (PMID: 40343304)
summary: Differential methylation analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from Alzheimer's disease patients versus controls identified MIDEAS among differentially methylated genes. This finding suggests potential epigenetic dysregulation of MIDEAS in the context of systemic peripheral inflammation associated with Alzheimer's disease. The study proposes DNA methylation patterns including MIDEAS as potential blood-based biomarkers for AD.

citation: Zebrafish MAP2K7 Simultaneously Enhances Host IRF7 Stability and Degrades Spring Viremia of Carp Virus P Protein via Ubiquitination Pathway (PMID: 37367226)
phenotype: map2k7-/- is lethal (homozygous knockout is lethal); map2k7+/- zebrafish showed higher lethality upon SVCV infection; more pronounced tissue damage in major immune organs; more viral proteins in major immune organs; weaker antiviral capacity compared to controls

citation: HER2-driven breast cancer suppression by the JNK signaling pathway (PMID: 36656864)
phenotype: JNK pathway deficiency (including Map2k7 ablation) promotes HER2+-driven breast cancer; Accelerated tumor development in mammary epithelial cells; Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly earlier tumor onset with JNK pathway deficiency

citation: Mice haploinsufficient for Map2k7, a gene involved in neurodevelopment and risk for schizophrenia, show impaired attention, a vigilance decrement deficit and unstable cognitive processing in an attentional task: impact of minocycline (PMID: 27774567)
phenotype: Impaired attentional function in five-choice serial reaction time task (5-CSRTT); Increased number of missed responses; More pronounced decrement in performance over time; Elevated intra-individual reaction time variability; Inability to sustain attention; Cognitive impairment pattern suggestive of schizophrenia-like deficits; Partial improvement in attentional performance with minocycline treatment

citation: Evolution of a New Testis-Specific Functional Promoter Within the Highly Conserved Map2k7 Gene of the Mouse (PMID: 35069705)
phenotype: Deletion of newly evolved promoter region of Map2k7 testis-specific transcript; Impaired sperm motility; Altered spermatid transcriptome

citation: Inactivation of KLF4 promotes T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and activates the MAP2K7 pathway (PMID: 27872496)
phenotype: Loss of KLF4 in NOTCH1-induced T-ALL mouse model leads to aberrant activation of MAP2K7; Activation of downstream effectors JNK and ATF2; Enhanced G1-to-S transition in leukemic cells; Expansion of leukemia-initiating cells; Accelerated development of T-ALL

citation: Cross-species analysis of transcriptome emphasizes a critical role of TNF-α in mediating MAP2K7/AKT2 signaling in zearalenone-induced apoptosis (PMID: 37549580)
phenotype: MAP2K7 knockout in mouse granulosa cells confirmed TNF-α-mediated MAP2K7/AKT2 axis as guiding signal in ZEN-induced apoptosis; Disruption of MAP2K7/AKT2 signaling in ovarian granulosa cells; Increased apoptosis in granulosa cells upon zearalenone exposure

citation: Inhibition of MKK7-JNK by the TOR signaling pathway regulator-like protein contributes to resistance of HCC cells to TRAIL-induced apoptosis (PMID: 22841785)
phenotype: Knockdown of tiprl (not MAP2K7 directly) in zebrafish led to large amounts of apoptosis throughout embryos; Prolonged activation/phosphorylation of MKK7 (MAP2K7) and JNK following TIPRL knockdown

citation: Inactivation of KLF4 promotes T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and activates the MAP2K7 pathway (PMID: 27872496)
summary: KLF4 transcriptionally represses MAP2K7; loss of KLF4 via DNA methylation in pediatric T-ALL leads to aberrant MAP2K7 activation and downstream JNK/ATF2 signaling, promoting leukemia-initiating cell expansion. JNK inhibitors reduced leukemia cell expansion in cell-based and patient-derived xenograft models, validating MAP2K7 as a therapeutic target.

citation: Inhibition of the MAP2K7-JNK pathway with 5Z-7-oxozeaenol induces apoptosis in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 34504651)
summary: The small molecule 5Z-7-oxozeaenol (5Z7O) induces dose-dependent cytotoxicity in T-ALL cell lines primarily through inhibition of the MAP2K7-JNK pathway, causing G2/M checkpoint dysregulation and apoptosis. Anti-leukemic effects were confirmed in two mouse T-ALL models and patient-derived xenograft cells, and synergy was observed with dexamethasone.

citation: Map2k7 Haploinsufficiency Induces Brain Imaging Endophenotypes and Behavioral Phenotypes Relevant to Schizophrenia (PMID: 31219577)
summary: Map2k7+/- mice display schizophrenia-relevant brain metabolic and connectivity alterations, including hippocampal/mesolimbic hypermetabolism and prefrontal hypometabolism. Behavioral studies showed attenuated d-amphetamine responses but preserved ketamine responses, implicating MAP2K7 in monoamine neurotransmitter system function relevant to schizophrenia.

citation: The EEF1AKMT3/MAP2K7/TP53 axis suppresses tumor invasiveness and metastasis in gastric cancer (PMID: 35753528)
summary: EEF1AKMT3 methyltransferase catalyzes monomethylation of MAP2K7 at K296, which decreases MAP2K7 phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and degradation, thereby stabilizing TP53 and suppressing gastric cancer invasiveness. EEF1AKMT3, p-MAP2K7, and TP53 protein levels were positively correlated in gastric cancer tissues.

citation: Zebrafish MAP2K7 Simultaneously Enhances Host IRF7 Stability and Degrades Spring Viremia of Carp Virus P Protein via Ubiquitination Pathway (PMID: 37367226)
summary: Zebrafish MAP2K7 protects against viral infection through two mechanisms: it stabilizes host IRF7 via K63-linked polyubiquitination and promotes degradation of SVCV P protein via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. map2k7+/- zebrafish showed higher lethality, more tissue damage, and greater viral burden than controls, demonstrating an antiviral role beyond canonical kinase signaling.

citation: miR-128-3p suppresses tumor growth and enhances chemosensitivity in tongue squamous cell carcinoma through MAP2K7 targeting (PMID: 39476205)
summary: miR-128-3p directly targets MAP2K7 (validated by luciferase reporter assay), and its overexpression inhibits TSCC cell migration, proliferation, and EMT by suppressing MAP2K7-mediated JNK/c-Jun signaling. Increased miR-128-3p also enhanced cisplatin sensitivity by reducing ABC transporter gene expression downstream of MAP2K7/JNK1/2.

citation: JNK pathway suppression mediates insensitivity to combination endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibition in ER+ breast cancer (PMID: 40826108)
summary: Genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screens identified MAP2K7 loss as a key driver of resistance to tamoxifen plus palbociclib in ER+ breast cancer cells. MAP2K7 knockout in MCF-7 and T-47D cells increased metastatic burden in vivo, impaired JNK-mediated stress responses, reduced senescence entry, and attenuated AP-1/c-JUN activity; low pJNK activity correlated with poorer clinical outcomes.

citation: Circular RNA ACTA1 Acts as a Sponge for miR-199a-5p and miR-433 to Regulate Bovine Myoblast Development through the MAP3K11/MAP2K7/JNK Pathway (PMID: 35234473)
summary: MAP2K7 functions as a component of the MAP3K11/MAP2K7/JNK signaling cascade in bovine myoblast development. circACTA1 sponges miR-199a-5p and miR-433 to relieve suppression of MAP3K11 and MAPK8, activating MAP2K7-mediated JNK signaling to regulate myocyte proliferation, apoptosis, and differentiation.

citation: Expression and Clinical Significance of MAPK8, MAPK9, MAP2K4, and MAP2K7 Genes in Colorectal Cancer (PMID: 41515982)
significance: statistically significant elevation in higher-grade tumors
summary: MAP2K7 gene expression was significantly elevated in colorectal cancer tumor specimens with higher histological grades, and bioinformatics analysis confirmed MAP2K7 promotes tumor aggressiveness and metastasis. This was assessed by quantitative PCR in 55 intraoperatively collected CRC tissue fragments.

citation: Small Extracellular Vesicles From Brown Adipose Tissue Mediate Exercise Cardioprotection (PMID: 35387487)
summary: MAP2K7 is a direct target of exercise-induced BAT-derived miRNAs (miR-125b-5p, miR-128-3p, miR-30d-5p) that cooperatively suppress the proapoptotic MAPK pathway in cardiomyocytes. BAT sEV delivery into hearts suppressed MI/R-related MAPK pathway activation including Map2k7, and this cardioprotective effect was abolished by combined BAT miRNA inhibition.

citation: Fast-twitch myofibrils grow in proportion to Mylpf dosage in the zebrafish embryo (PMID: 39345555)
phenotype: mylpfa-/- mutant: severely reduced fast-twitch myofibrils; mylpfa-/- mutant: loss of high-speed movement; mylpfa-/- mutant: persistent slow movement, swims as far as wild-type over time; mylpfb-/- mutant: normal myofibrils; mylpfa-/-;mylpfb-/- double mutant: complete failure of myofibril formation; Myofibril width restored by transgenic mylpfa-GFP, mylpfb-GFP, and human MYLPF-GFP proportional to GFP brightness; DA-causing MYLPF alleles reduce myofibril size in proportion to protein abundance

citation: Mutations in MYLPF Cause a Novel Segmental Amyoplasia that Manifests as Distal Arthrogryposis (PMID: 32707087)
phenotype: mylpfa-/- mutant: reduced trunk contractile force; mylpfa-/- mutant: complete pectoral fin paralysis; mylpfa-/- mutant: reduced myosin activity; mylpfa-/- mutant: fiber degeneration; Muscle weakness most pronounced in appendicular muscle (pectoral fin)

citation: Myosin light chain proteins cooperatively promote sarcomere growth in fast-twitch muscle (PMID: 42243126)
phenotype: mylpfa-/- and mylpfb-/- mutations cause full mRNA and protein loss; Loss of sarcomere formation in fast-twitch muscle; Degree of sarcomere reduction predicted by Mylpf protein dosage via high-slope Hill equation; Impaired thick filament localization in mylpfa-/-; Obliterated thick filament localization in mylpfa-/-;mylpfb-/-; Slow-twitch muscle spared and becomes larger and more active in mutants; mylpfa-/- defects rescued by Mylpfa-GFP, Mylpfb-GFP, and human MYLPF-GFP; DA-causing MYLPF protein variant fails to rescue mylpfa-/- defects

citation: Fast skeletal muscle regulatory light chain is required for fast and slow skeletal muscle development (PMID: 17356007)
phenotype: Homozygous RLC-f null (Mylpf-/-): complete absence of both fast and slow skeletal muscle; Diaphragm lacks skeletal muscle leading to respiratory failure; Death immediately after birth; Body weight of newborn null mice decreased 30% compared to heterozygous or WT; No effect on development of other organs including heart; Heterozygotes (RLC-/+): approximately half RLC-f mRNA, histologically normal muscles in adults and neonates; RLC-v/s not expressed in WT mice until after birth but expressed normally in embryonic heart

citation: ASHG 2015 - Mutations in MYLPF cause a novel segmental amyoplasia manifest as distal arthrogryposis (ASHG 2015)
phenotype: Mylpf null mice are 30% smaller than wild-type or heterozygous counterparts; Lack skeletal muscle throughout the whole body; Die immediately after birth due to respiratory failure caused by lack of skeletal muscle in the diaphragm; Mouse model recapitulates human phenotype of segmental amyoplasia

citation: Mutations in MYLPF Cause a Novel Segmental Amyoplasia that Manifests as Distal Arthrogryposis (PMID: 32707087)
sample_size: 10 affected individuals in 8 families; zebrafish model
summary: Loss-of-function and dominant/recessive variants in MYLPF cause distal arthrogryposis with congenital contractures and segmental amyoplasia (complete absence of skeletal muscle in distal limb). Zebrafish mylpfa knockout showed reduced trunk contractile force, complete pectoral fin paralysis, reduced myosin activity, and fiber degeneration, demonstrating that MYLPF is essential for limb muscle function and that partial loss leads to muscle degeneration.

citation: Fast-twitch myofibrils grow in proportion to Mylpf dosage in the zebrafish embryo (PMID: 39345555)
summary: Zebrafish mylpfa and mylpfb are exclusively expressed in fast-twitch muscle, with mylpfa producing ~6x more mRNA and protein than mylpfb. Combined Mylpf protein dosage is necessary for and proportionate to fast-twitch myofibril growth; double knockout (mylpfa-/-;mylpfb-/-) causes complete failure of myofibril formation, while mylpfa-/- alone severely reduces myofibrils and high-speed movement. Transgenic rescue with human MYLPF-GFP restores myofibril width proportionally, and disease-causing DA alleles reduce myofibril size in proportion to protein abundance.

citation: Molecular cloning, sequence identification and expression analysis of novel caprine MYLPF gene (PMID: 23277391)
summary: MYLPF mRNA is highly expressed in skeletal muscles (longissimus dorsi, gastrocnemius, abdominal muscle) of goats, with low expression in liver, spleen, lung, and kidney. MYLPF protein was detected only in muscle tissues, not in liver, spleen, lung, or kidney. Temporal analysis showed MYLPF expression decreases gradually with age in skeletal muscle, consistent with its role in early muscle growth.

citation: Identification of Potential Biomarkers for Ryanodine Receptor 1 (RYR1) Mutation-Associated Myopathies Using Bioinformatics Approach (PMID: 35692882)
summary: MYLPF was identified as one of four skeletal muscle tissue-specific hub genes (alongside MYH1, TNNT3, ATP2A1) differentially expressed in RYR1 mutation-associated myopathy patients versus healthy controls, with an AUC of 0.786 for diagnostic prediction. The transcription factor MYF6 was predicted as a key upstream regulator of MYLPF. MYLPF expression was downregulated in RYR1 myopathy muscle biopsies.

citation: DNA methyltransferase inhibitor CDA-II inhibits myogenic differentiation (PMID: 22627135)
summary: Treatment of C2C12 murine myoblasts with CDA-II (a DNA methyltransferase inhibitor) repressed expression of MYLPF (myosin light chain) along with other muscle structural proteins (Myh3, MCK) and transcription factors (Myogenin, Mef2c) in a dose-dependent manner. This demonstrates that MYLPF expression is regulated during myogenic differentiation and is sensitive to epigenetic modulation.

citation: EPA and DHA Inhibit Myogenesis and Downregulate the Expression of Muscle-related Genes in C2C12 Myoblasts (PMID: 30669396)
summary: RNA-sequencing of C2C12 myoblasts treated with EPA or DHA (50 µM) showed significant downregulation of MYLPF along with IGF-2, Tnnt3, Mb, and Myh3. EPA and DHA suppressed C2C12 differentiation and decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and Akt, suggesting MYLPF downregulation is linked to inhibition of PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signaling during myogenesis.

citation: The Expression Profiles of mRNAs and lncRNAs in Buffalo Muscle Stem Cells Driving Myogenic Differentiation (PMID: 34306003)
summary: Interference with MYLPF expression in buffalo muscle stem cells (MuSCs) significantly inhibited their differentiation, directly demonstrating a functional role for MYLPF in myogenic differentiation. MYLPF was identified among functionally important genes in mRNA/lncRNA expression profiling during MuSC proliferation and differentiation phases.

citation: Polymorphisms in the regulatory region of the porcine MYLPF gene are related to meat quality traits in the Large White breed (PMID: 26638021)
summary: Five SNPs in the promoter region of porcine MYLPF were genotyped in Large White, Duroc, and Pietrain pigs. In Large White pigs, SNP g.-1314A>G and linked SNPs (g.-871T>G, g.-566T>C, g.-403C>G) were significantly associated with ultimate pH and drip loss (meat quality traits), identifying MYLPF as a functional candidate gene for meat quality.

citation: Quantitative proteomic and phosphoproteomic analysis of chicken skeletal muscle during embryonic development (PMID: 34236285)
sample_size: Chicken leg muscle at E7, E12, E17, D3
summary: Phosphorylated MYLPF was identified as a differentially expressed phosphoprotein during chicken embryonic skeletal muscle development (E7 to D3 post-hatch). PPI analysis showed phosphorylated MYLPF interacts with TNNC1, TNNC2, TNNT2, and TNNT3 in pathways related to muscle contraction, and focal adhesion was the only pathway significantly enriched in the integrated proteome/phosphoproteome analysis.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Unsupervised learning revealed metabolic syndrome sub-groups with differing phenotypic and genotypic traits (A. Lim et al.)
summary: GWAS of metabolic syndrome subgroup C1 (non-descriptive, n=33,707) in UK Biobank identified a novel association at MYLPF (rs8054556), with MYLPF expression noted to be specific to skeletal muscle. MYLPF was unique to the C1 subgroup and was not associated with other MetS clusters, suggesting a distinct skeletal muscle-related genetic component in this metabolic syndrome subtype.

citation: PPP6R3-mediated dephosphorylation regulates mRNA translation during spermatogonial differentiation (PMID: 40721635)
phenotype: Abnormal spermatogonial differentiation; Male infertility; Translation inhibition in KIT+ spermatogonia; Decreased non-phosphorylated EIF3C and EIF4G1 levels; Increased phosphorylation and degradation of EIF3C and EIF4G1; Upregulated phosphorylation at EIF3CS39 and EIF4G1S1217; Reduced enrichment of differentiation-associated mRNAs on translation machinery

citation: Role of ppp6r3 in zebrafish gonadal differentiation and gametogenesis (PMID: 40962474)
phenotype: All mutant fish develop as male (sex ratio skewed to all-male); Male infertility - unable to fertilize wild-type eggs; Blocked transition of spermatocytes to mature sperm; Disrupted spermatogenesis; Defects in gonadal differentiation and gametogenesis

citation: Removal of developmentally regulated microexons has a minimal impact on larval zebrafish brain morphology and function (PMID: 41252186)
phenotype: Mild neural phenotypes in ppp6r3 microexon mutants; Altered larval brain activity (specific region not detailed beyond mild phenotype)

citation: The protein phosphatase PP6 promotes RIPK1-dependent PANoptosis (PMID: 38807188)
summary: PPP6R3, along with PPP6R1 and PPP6R2, acts as a regulatory subunit of the PP6 holoenzyme with redundant roles in regulating TAK1 inhibitor-induced PANoptosis; combined depletion of all three regulatory subunits was required to block cell death. Mechanistically, PPP6R3 and its paralogs promoted pro-death S166 auto-phosphorylation of RIPK1 and reduced pro-survival S321 phosphorylation. These findings were identified through a cell death-based CRISPR screen.

citation: Transcriptome-wide association study and eQTL colocalization identify potentially causal genes responsible for human bone mineral density GWAS associations (PMID: 36416764)
summary: PPP6R3 was identified as the gene with the strongest support from combined TWAS and eQTL colocalization analysis for bone mineral density (BMD) GWAS associations, and was not previously implicated in BMD regulation. Ppp6r3 deletion in mice decreased BMD, providing in vivo functional validation. This study demonstrates PPP6R3 as a putatively causal BMD GWAS gene.

citation: Role of ppp6r3 in zebrafish gonadal differentiation and gametogenesis (PMID: 40962474)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9-generated ppp6r3 mutant zebrafish developed exclusively as males, indicating a role in gonadal sex determination. In the testes of mutants, the transition from spermatocytes to mature sperm was blocked, disrupting spermatogenesis. This establishes PPP6R3 as a regulator of germ cell differentiation and sex determination in zebrafish.

citation: Interactome analysis of the influenza A virus transcription/replication machinery identifies protein phosphatase 6 as a cellular factor required for efficient virus replication (PMID: 25187537)
summary: PPP6R3 was identified as one of three PP6 subunits (along with PPP6C and PPP6R1) that co-purified with the influenza A virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP) in infected human cells via affinity purification and mass spectrometry. PP6 was found to interact directly with the PB1 and PB2 subunits of the viral RdRP. siRNA-mediated knockdown of the PP6 catalytic subunit reduced viral RNA accumulation and attenuated virus growth.

citation: Meta-Analysis of Genomewide Association Studies Reveals Genetic Variants for Hip Bone Geometry (PMID: 30888730)
summary: A SNP near PPP6R3 (rs7102273) at chromosome 11q13 reached genome-wide significance for femoral neck geometry phenotypes in a meta-analysis of up to 18,719 individuals. The same SNP was associated with any-type fracture (p=7.5×10⁻⁵) and was identified as an eQTL for PPP6R3 expression in bone transcriptome data (p=0.0007). This implicates PPP6R3 in hip bone geometry and fracture risk.

citation: Bivariate genome-wide association meta-analysis of pediatric musculoskeletal traits reveals pleiotropic effects at the SREBF1/TOM1L2 locus (PMID: 28743860)
summary: A variant in the PPP6R3/LRP5 locus was identified as one of eight loci with pleiotropic effects on both total-body lean mass and total-body bone mineral density in a bivariate GWAS meta-analysis of 10,414 children. This locus was among seven established BMD loci showing shared genetic effects on lean mass. The finding highlights PPP6R3 as a candidate gene at this locus influencing musculoskeletal traits.

citation: PPP6R3-USP6 amplification: Novel oncogenic mechanism in malignant nodular fasciitis (PMID: 27113271)
summary: A novel PPP6R3-USP6 gene fusion was identified in a case of malignant nodular fasciitis with multiple recurrences and metastatic behavior over 10 years. Amplification of this fusion resulted in transcriptional upregulation of USP6 mRNA, supporting an oncogenic role. This represents the first documented case of PPP6R3 involvement in a gene fusion driving malignant mesenchymal neoplasia.

citation: AKIRIN1: A Potential New Reference Gene in Human Natural Killer Cells and Granulocytes in Sepsis (PMID: 31075840)
summary: PPP6R3 was identified as a candidate reference gene in natural killer (NK) cells from patients with SIRS and sepsis, based on stable expression across disease conditions in microarray discovery and branched DNA assay validation. Its stable expression in NK cells under inflammatory conditions suggests constitutive expression in immune cell types. PPP6R3 was among several genes (AKIRIN1, TAX1BP1, ADRBK1) validated as potential reference genes in this context.

citation: Removal of developmentally regulated microexons has a minimal impact on larval zebrafish brain morphology and function (PMID: 41252186)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of a microexon in ppp6r3 in zebrafish resulted in mild neural phenotypes in larval brain activity or morphology assessments. This finding was part of a systematic screen of 45 microexons, with ppp6r3 being one of several genes showing subtle but notable phenotypes. The result suggests that the PPP6R3 microexon contributes to brain development or function in zebrafish.

citation: ASHG 2012 - The PPP6R3/LRP5 locus influences lean mass in children of different ethnic background and highlights pleiotropic effects on muscle-bone interactions
summary: PPP6R3 is described as a gene of unknown function that is ubiquitously expressed across tissues, including bone and muscle. A GWAS SNP at the PPP6R3/LRP5 locus was genome-wide significantly associated with total body lean mass (p=2.9×10⁻⁸) and nominally with BMD in 4,096 children. The authors note the difficulty in distinguishing whether the signal arises from PPP6R3 or LRP5 due to high regional LD.

citation: Loss of CTLH component MAEA impairs DNA repair and replication and leads to developmental delay. (PMID: 41420108)

citation: E3 ligase MAEA-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of PHD3 promotes glioblastoma progression. (PMID: 36882523)
summary: MAEA acts as an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets prolyl hydroxylase domain 3 (PHD3) at K159 for K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation, thereby stabilizing HIF-1α and upregulating CD133 to promote stemness, TMZ resistance, proliferation, and invasion in glioblastoma. High MAEA expression correlates with recurrence and poor prognosis in glioma. Knockdown of MAEA inhibited GBM xenograft tumor growth in vivo.

citation: Maea expressed by macrophages, but not erythroblasts, maintains postnatal murine bone marrow erythroblastic islands. (PMID: 30674470)
summary: Conditional knockout of Maea in macrophages (using Csf1r-Cre or CD169-Cre) caused severe reductions in bone marrow macrophages, erythroblasts, and erythroblastic island formation, while deletion in the erythroid lineage had no such phenotype, establishing a dominant macrophage-specific role for Maea in bone marrow erythropoiesis. Postnatal Maea deletion or antibody-mediated inhibition also impaired BM erythropoiesis. These results indicate Maea regulates macrophage maintenance and macrophage-erythroblast interactions.

citation: MAEA is an E3 ubiquitin ligase promoting autophagy and maintenance of haematopoietic stem cells. (PMID: 33947846)
summary: MAEA is a membrane-associated E3 ubiquitin ligase subunit highly expressed in haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs); its deletion in mice severely impairs HSC quiescence and causes a lethal myeloproliferative syndrome. Mechanistically, MAEA loss stabilizes cytokine receptors (MPL, FLT3) on the cell surface, prolonging their signaling and impairing autophagy flux specifically in HSCs. Autophagy-inducing compounds or receptor kinase inhibitors rescue the functional defects of Maea-deficient HSCs.

citation: Pathogenic variants in MAEA disrupt DNA replication fork stability and are associated with developmental abnormalities in humans. (PMID: 40880485)
summary: MAEA, as a core component of the CTLH E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, regulates the homologous recombination pathway by mediating ubiquitylation of Ku80 to enable its removal from replication fork ends and facilitate RAD51 loading; loss of MAEA impairs RAD51 recruitment and increases sensitivity to replication stress. Pathogenic MAEA variants (R34C, E349G, Y394D, M396R) are associated with a human developmental disorder involving microcephaly, craniofacial abnormalities, ocular defects, and heart malformations. Functional assays confirmed these disease-linked variants are defective in replication stress response.

citation: maea affects head formation through ß-catenin degradation during early Xenopus laevis development. (PMID: 36444483)
summary: In Xenopus laevis embryos, maea transcripts are ubiquitously expressed in early development, and maea.S overexpression at the anterior dorsal region enlarged head structures while Maea knockdown interfered with head formation. Mechanistically, Maea.S promotes ubiquitination and degradation of β-catenin (including at novel lysine residues), thereby suppressing canonical Wnt target genes (nodal3.1, sia1) and modulating axis/head formation.

citation: The CTLH ubiquitin ligase substrates ZMYND19 and MKLN1 negatively regulate mTORC1 at the lysosomal membrane. (PMID: 41315365)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen identified multiple CTLH E3 ligase subunits, including the catalytic MAEA subunit, as top hits that synergistically block EBV-associated gastric carcinoma proliferation with PI3K inhibition. MAEA knockout caused accumulation of substrates MKLN1 and ZMYND19, which associate with lysosomal membranes to inhibit mTORC1 by blocking its interaction with Rheb and substrates S6K and 4E-BP1. This places MAEA in the PI3K/mTOR pathway as a regulator of mTORC1 activity via ubiquitin/proteasome-mediated substrate degradation.

citation: Adenovirus vector-mediated macrophage erythroblast attacher (MAEA) overexpression in primary mouse hepatocytes attenuates hepatic gluconeogenesis. (PMID: 28955747)
summary: Adenovirus-mediated overexpression of MAEA in primary mouse hepatocytes reduced expression of gluconeogenesis genes and suppressed HNF-4α mRNA, suggesting MAEA attenuates hepatic gluconeogenesis. In vivo, Ad-MAEA-treated mice showed comparable blood glucose and insulin levels to controls, but the hepatocyte data suggest a potential role in improving type 2 diabetes. This study was motivated by genetic evidence linking the MAEA locus to T2D susceptibility in East Asians.

citation: The E3 ubiquitin ligase MAEA promotes macrophage phagocytosis and inhibits gastrointestinal cancer progression by mediating PARP1 ubiquitination and degradation. (PMID: 39990651)
summary: MAEA mediates K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of PARP1 in gastrointestinal cancer cells, impairing tumor proliferation and chemoresistance in vitro and in xenograft models. Additionally, MAEA suppresses M2 macrophage polarization and enhances macrophage phagocytic activity. Reduced MAEA expression in GIC patients correlates with worse disease-free and overall survival.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Comprehensive evaluation of type 2 diabetes susceptibility in the Japanese population by genome-wide imputation analysis using the 1000 Genomes Project data. (K. Hara et al.)
summary: SNPs in the CTBP1/MAEA region (rs730831, rs4974585, rs4974586) were identified as associated with type 2 diabetes in a Japanese GWAS with genome-wide significance after replication in an independent sample. Combined p-values ranged from P=5×10⁻⁸ (OR=1.18) to P=1×10⁻¹⁰ (OR=1.25). Conditional analyses identified rs730831 in CTBP1 as the lead SNP, though the MAEA locus was implicated in T2D susceptibility.

citation: Exploring the genomic and transcriptomic profiles of glycemic traits and drug repurposing. (PMID: 40399988)
summary: A genome-wide meta-analysis of glycemic traits (HbA1c and fasting glucose) in a Taiwanese cohort identified MAEA as a novel gene locus associated with glycemic traits, in addition to validating known loci. The study integrated genetics, transcriptomics, and pathway analyses, and a higher polygenic risk score including MAEA was associated with increased T2D risk. This finding extends the genetic association of MAEA with glucose regulation to the Taiwanese Han population.

citation: Astrocytic LRP1 enables mitochondria transfer to neurons and mitigates brain ischemic stroke by suppressing ARF1 lactylation (PMID: 38906140)
summary: Astrocytic LRP1 suppresses glucose uptake, glycolysis, and lactate production, thereby reducing lactylation of ARF1 and promoting astrocyte-to-neuron mitochondria transfer. Suppression of astrocytic LRP1 in a mouse ischemia-reperfusion model worsened stroke injury and reduced mitochondria transfer to damaged neurons. CSF lactate was elevated in human stroke patients and inversely correlated with astrocytic mitochondria levels.

citation: Low-density-lipoprotein-receptor-related protein 1 mediates Notch pathway activation (PMID: 34626540)
summary: LRP1 was identified as a key regulator of the Notch signaling pathway through a protein interaction landscape analysis. LRP1 mediates ubiquitination chain linkage switching of Delta ligands, affecting ligand recycling, membrane localization, and stability. LRP1 inhibition led to Notch signaling inhibition and decreased tumorigenesis in leukemia cell models.

citation: Heterozygous LRP1 deficiency causes developmental dysplasia of the hip by impairing triradiate chondrocytes differentiation due to inhibition of autophagy (PMID: 36067312)
summary: Whole-exome sequencing identified likely pathogenic LRP1 variants in two DDH families and seven sporadic patients. Heterozygous Lrp1 knockout mice and Lrp1 knockin mice with a human DDH-associated missense variant (R1783W) recapitulated DDH phenotypes. Mechanistically, Lrp1 deficiency impaired chondrogenic differentiation by decreasing autophagy and upregulating β-catenin signaling.

citation: Skeletal progenitor LRP1 deficiency causes severe and persistent skeletal defects with Wnt pathway dysregulation (PMID: 39865089)
summary: LRP1 is abundantly expressed in skeletal progenitor cells from mouse embryonic stage E10.5, especially in the perichondrium. Lrp1 deficiency in skeletal progenitors caused joint fusion, cartilage/bone malformation, and severe skeletal defects resembling Wnt signaling pathway phenotypes. LRP1 directly binds Wnt5a, facilitates its endocytic degradation and recycling, and regulates non-canonical Wnt/PCP components Wnt5a and Vangl2 in developing limbs.

citation: LRP1 Repression by SNAIL Results in ECM Remodeling in Genetic Risk for Vascular Diseases (PMID: 39355906)
summary: Multitrait colocalization analyses identified rs11172113 as the most likely causal variant at the LRP1 locus for fibromuscular dysplasia, migraine, pulse pressure, and spontaneous coronary artery dissection, with the T allele associated with higher LRP1 expression. In iPSC-derived smooth muscle cells, LRP1 knockout decreased proliferation and migration, enhanced TGF-β/SMAD2/3 signaling, and remodeled the extracellular matrix. The transcription factor SNAIL was found to repress LRP1 expression through an allele-specific mechanism involving the disease risk allele.

citation: Genome-wide CRISPR screening identifies LRP1 as an entry factor for SFTSV (PMID: 40301361)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen identified LRP1 as a host entry factor for Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV). Knockdown or knockout of LRP1 significantly attenuated SFTSV infection in mouse embryonic fibroblasts, and co-IP and surface plasmon resonance revealed direct interaction between SFTSV glycoprotein Gn and LRP1 via CLI and CLII domains. LRP1 antagonists and neutralizing antibodies reduced viral load and improved survival in a lethal mouse model.

citation: Schwann cell LRP1 regulates remak bundle ultrastructure and axonal interactions to prevent neuropathic pain (PMID: 23536074)
summary: LRP1 is expressed in Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system, where it is essential for normal axon myelination and ensheathment of axons in Remak bundles. Schwann cell-specific LRP1 deletion (scLRP1-/-) in mice caused mechanical allodynia even without nerve injury, accelerated degeneration after crush injury, and impaired remyelination. Central sensitization markers including p38MAPK activation and microglial activation were elevated in the spinal cord of scLRP1-/- mice.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Regulation of HDL-c levels via ABCA1: A role for LRP1 (ASHG 2016)
summary: Two missense mutations in LRP1 (p.Val3244Ile and p.Glu3983Asp) were identified in individuals with extremely low HDL-c levels, and the LRP1 locus was strongly associated with HDL-c and ApoA1 levels in a large Danish cohort. Mutant LRP1 proteins were reduced by 40-60% in stability, and ABCA1 cell surface localization was decreased by 60-70% in carrier fibroblasts and LRP1-deficient cells. LRP1 was found to regulate intracellular trafficking of ABCA1 to the plasma membrane via modulation of lysosomal enzyme Cathepsin D and Prosaposin levels.

citation: Meta-analysis of genome-wide association data of 20,000 migraine cases identifies two novel gene loci and supports several biologically relevant mechanisms (ASHG 2011)
summary: A large-scale GWAS meta-analysis of approximately 20,000 migraine cases and 90,000 controls identified LRP1 (rs11172113 at 12q13.3) as one of the genome-wide significant loci associated with migraine susceptibility. This finding was replicated across multiple clinic- and population-based cohorts from three continents. Subsequent Bayesian conditional analysis further strengthened the LRP1 association signal (p-value improving from 3.94×10⁻¹⁹ to 1.41×10⁻²⁶) and identified multiple independent signals at this locus.

citation: MiR-4649-5p acts as a tumor-suppressive microRNA in triple negative breast cancer by direct interaction with PIP5K1C, thereby potentiating growth-inhibitory effects of the AKT inhibitor capivasertib. (PMID: 37803350)

citation: The phosphorylation status of PIP5K1C at serine 448 can be predictive for invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. (PMID: 30555634)

citation: ASHG 2016 - De novo alterations in KLF7 are a novel cause of intellectual disability, psychiatric and neuromuscular issues. (ASHG 2016)
summary: Three unrelated individuals with de novo missense variants in KLF7 (p.T137M, p.P139S, p.D264N) presented with intellectual disability, abnormal muscle tone, feeding/swallowing issues, psychiatric features, and neuromuscular issues. Two variants fall in the F-box motif involved in protein-protein interactions and ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis; one variant is in the zinc finger DNA-binding domain. KLF7 is implicated in neurogenesis including axon guidance in hippocampus, olfactory bulbs, and cortex.

citation: KLF7 orchestrates hippocampal development through neurogenesis and Draxin-mediated neuronal migration. (PMID: 40762575)
summary: Conditional knockout of KLF7 in hippocampal progenitors (Emx1-Cre;Klf7F/F mice) caused hippocampal shrinkage, disrupted neurogenesis, neuronal differentiation and migration, and led to anxiety/depression-like behaviors and memory impairments. Transcriptomic profiling identified Draxin, a neural chemorepellent, as a key downstream transcriptional target of KLF7. Overexpression of Draxin rescued dentate gyrus granule cell migration defects in KLF7 mutant mice.

citation: KLF7-transfected Schwann cell graft transplantation promotes sciatic nerve regeneration. (PMID: 27826105)
summary: KLF7 overexpression in Schwann cells via AAV2 promoted SC proliferation, enhanced DRG neurite outgrowth, and improved sciatic nerve regeneration in a mouse acellular nerve allograft model. KLF7-overexpressing SCs showed increased expression of NGF, GAP43, TrkA, and TrkB, suggesting involvement of neurotrophin signaling pathways. These findings confirm KLF7 as a transcription factor that stimulates axonal regeneration after peripheral nerve injury.

citation: HMGB1-mediated elevation of KLF7 facilitates hepatocellular carcinoma progression and metastasis through upregulating TLR4 and PTK2. (PMID: 37554278)
summary: KLF7 overexpression promotes HCC metastasis by directly transactivating TLR4 and PTK2 promoters. HMGB1 upregulates KLF7 via the TLR4/RAGE-PI3K-AKT-NF-κB pathway, forming a positive feedback loop. Genetic depletion of KLF7 via AAV gene therapy impeded HMGB1-mediated HCC progression and metastasis in orthotopic xenograft and DEN/CCl4-induced HCC models.

citation: KLF7 promotes adipocyte inflammation and glucose metabolism disorder by activating the PKCζ/NF-κB pathway. (PMID: 37342904)
summary: KLF7 directly binds the PKCζ promoter to upregulate its transcription, thereby activating the NF-κB signaling pathway and promoting IL-6 expression in adipocytes. In high-fat diet mice, KLF7, PKCζ, p-IκB, p-p65, and IL-6 were all elevated in epididymal white adipose tissue, while fat-conditional KLF7 knockout reduced these markers. This identifies a KLF7/PKCζ/NF-κB axis linking KLF7 to adipocyte inflammation and insulin resistance.

citation: KLF7 promotes progression of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma by remodeling tumor immune microenvironment. (PMID: 41482204)
summary: KLF7 acts as an oncogenic transcription factor in HNSCC that directly transcriptionally activates LOX, driving extracellular matrix crosslinking and stiffening to recruit tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and suppress CD8+ T cell-mediated killing. In vitro and in vivo experiments showed KLF7 governs both autonomous malignant behaviors and macrophage recruitment in the tumor microenvironment. The KLF7/LOX/TAM signaling axis was validated as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.

citation: Histone marks identify novel transcription factors that parse CAR-T subset-of-origin, clinical potential and expansion. (PMID: 39333103)
summary: Analysis of histone methylation marks in CAR-T products from a clinical lymphoma trial (NCT01865617) identified KLF7 activity as associated with in vivo CAR-T accumulation in patients. Overexpression of KLF7 in CAR-T cells increased in vitro proliferation and IL-2 production. This represents a novel functional role for KLF7 in T cell biology beyond its known roles in neural and cancer contexts.

citation: Knockdown of KLF7 inhibits the differentiation of both intramuscular and subcutaneous preadipocytes in goat. (PMID: 34890305)
summary: KLF7 knockdown in goat intramuscular and subcutaneous preadipocytes inhibited lipid droplet accumulation and reduced expression of adipogenic markers (C/EBPα, SREBP1), demonstrating KLF7 as a positive regulator of adipogenesis. KLF7 expression changed dynamically during preadipocyte-to-adipocyte differentiation, and KLF7 transcriptional binding sites were identified in the promoters of multiple KLF family members and adipogenic markers. This contrasts with some prior reports and identifies KLF7 as a novel regulator of adipogenesis in a livestock model.

citation: KLF7 Blocks MKNK2/HIF-1 Pathway-Mediated M1 Microglia Polarization to Ameliorate Ischemic Stroke-Induced Neurological Injury. (PMID: 40923147)
summary: KLF7 expression is downregulated in ischemic stroke (MCAO/R rat model and OGD/R microglia), and KLF7 overexpression ameliorated brain damage and neurological injury by repressing MKNK2 transcription, thereby inhibiting HIF-1 signaling and M1 microglia polarization while promoting M2 polarization. ChIP and dual-luciferase assays confirmed direct KLF7-mediated repression of the MKNK2 promoter. MKNK2 overexpression reversed the neuroprotective effects of KLF7 overexpression in vivo.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Cardiovascular comorbidity influence genetic association studies results. (ASHG 2016)
summary: A genetic association study of cardiovascular disease comorbidity identified a KLF7 polymorphism as associated with a combination of multiple cardiovascular diseases including ischemic heart disease, arterial hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypercholesterolemia (disease syntropy phenotype). KLF7 was not associated with isolated ischemic heart disease or the two-disease combination, suggesting its variant is specific to the multi-disease comorbidity context. Approximately 1,400 polymorphic variants were analyzed across patient groups.

citation: MARK2 phosphorylates KIF13A at a 14-3-3 binding site to polarize vesicular transport of transferrin receptor within dendrites (PMID: 38709923)

Knockout of MARK2 leads to axonal missorting of TfR-containing vesicles, demonstrating MARK2's role in polarized dendritic vesicle transport.

citation: ER-phagy restrains inflammatory responses through its receptor UBAC2 (PMID: 39284914)

Dimerized UBAC2 interacts more strongly with GABARAP, facilitating selective ER degradation. This MARK2-UBAC2 axis regulates ER-phagy and restrains inflammatory responses including acute ulcerative colitis in mice.

citation: MARK2 regulates chemotherapeutic responses through class IIa HDAC-YAP axis in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 35780183)

MARK2 directly phosphorylates HDAC4, which promotes YAP activation and controls expression of YAP target genes induced by paclitaxel. MARK2, HDACs, and YAP expression levels are upregulated and positively correlated in PDAC patients.

citation: MARK2 regulates Golgi apparatus reorientation by phosphorylation of CAMSAP2 in directional cell migration (PMID: 40333320)

Inducible whole-body deletion of Map4k4 in adult mice was tolerated under homeostatic conditions.

citation: RAP2 mediates mechanoresponses of the Hippo pathway (PMID: 30135582)
summary: MAP4K4 (along with MAP4K6 and MAP4K7) was identified as a direct binding partner and downstream effector of the GTPase RAP2 in mechanotransduction. At low ECM stiffness, active RAP2 binds to and stimulates MAP4K4, resulting in activation of LATS1/2 and inhibition of YAP/TAZ, placing MAP4K4 in the Hippo signaling pathway as a mechanosensitive kinase. This defines a mechanosignaling pathway from ECM stiffness through RAP2-MAP4K4-LATS1/2 to the nucleus.

citation: Cooperation of Striatin 3 and MAP4K4 promotes growth and tissue invasion (PMID: 35941177)
summary: MAP4K4 was found to interact with striatin 3 and 4 (STRN3/4), with STRN3 coupling MAP4K4 to protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) to inactivate growth-repressing activities of MAP4K4. STRN3 also enables MAP4K4-mediated direct phosphorylation of VASP at S157 via its CNH domain interaction with striatins, which is necessary for efficient cell invasion in medulloblastoma. Depletion of either STRN3 or MAP4K4 reduces invasion, while loss of both abrogates tumor cell growth in cerebellar tissue.

summary: Using A431 carcinoma cells, MAP4K4 was identified as a central regulator of collective cell migration, with its inactivation blocking cluster migration and overexpression decreasing cluster cohesion. citation: Histone lactylation-derived LINC01127 promotes the self-renewal of glioblastoma stem cells via the cis-regulating the MAP4K4 to activate JNK pathway (PMID: 38084701)

citation: MAP4K4 aggravates microvascular anomalies in diabetic retinopathy in a YTHDF2-dependent manner (PMID: 40072537)

citation: MAP4K4 promotes ovarian cancer metastasis through diminishing ADAM10-dependent N-cadherin cleavage (PMID: 36922678)
summary: Transcriptomic sequencing of paired primary ovarian tumors and metastases revealed MAP4K4 is highly expressed at metastatic sites, with higher expression associated with poorer survival and more advanced disease stage. TUGUL-modified KIF5B then carries GLUT4 storage vesicles and other cargoes to the cell surface, linking KIF5B to the insulin-regulated glucose uptake pathway. This mechanism is cell-type specific, occurring in fat and muscle but not fibroblasts.

summary: KIF5B-RET fusion cells showed increased expression of RET and downstream signaling molecules (p-BRAF, p-ERK, p-AKT) and elevated nuclear p-STAT5A and FOXA2, with FOXA2 expression being much higher in RET-rearranged NSCLC (94.4%) than in RET wild-type NSCLC (45.0%). FOXA2 siRNA knockdown in KIF5B-RET fusion cells reduced TGF-β1 mRNA but increased Twist1 and Snail, indicating FOXA2 regulates downstream oncogenic transcriptional programs.

This identifies KIF5B as a motor protein involved in the spatial organization of the ERGIC during non-canonical secretory pathway activity. The study places KIF5B in a Rab2A-dependent regulatory axis distinct from conventional ER-to-Golgi trafficking.

citation: m6A-modified circCCAR1 promotes malignant proliferation by enhancing KIF5B expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 40696234)

CircCCAR1 also binds PTBP1 to stabilize KIF5B mRNA, resulting in significantly elevated KIF5B expression in HCC cell lines compared to normal hepatic cells. Silencing circCCAR1 suppressed HCC proliferation and tumor growth in xenograft models, effects partially reversed by KIF5B overexpression.

citation: DNA double-strand break-capturing nuclear envelope tubules drive DNA repair (PMID: 38632359)
summary: KIF5B, together with KIF13B, collaborates with the LINC complex, NUP153, nuclear lamina, DDR kinases, and ATAT1-acetylated cytoplasmic microtubules to generate DSB-capturing nuclear envelope tubules (dsbNETs) that localize to DNA double-strand breaks and promote their repair. dsbNETs are reversed by kinesin KIFC3, indicating KIF5B drives their formation. These structures are hyper-induced in cells expressing the aging-linked lamin A mutant progerin and are co-opted during PARP inhibition in BRCA1-deficient breast cancer cells.

citation: Identification of Variant-Specific Functions of PIK3CA by Rapid Phenotyping of Rare Mutations (PMID: 26627007)
summary: High-throughput functional assessment of PIK3CA tail mutations using in vitro and in vivo cell growth and transformation assays differentiated driver from passenger mutations. PIK3CA variants above 5% mutation frequency were significantly more oncogenic than wild-type in all assays, while variants at 0.07–5.0% showed variable oncogenic activity. Proteomic profiling revealed variant-specific activation of PI3K signaling and the MEK1/2 module of the MAPK pathway.

citation: Organismal metabolism regulates the expansion of oncogenic PIK3CA mutant clones in normal esophagus (PMID: 39169259)
summary: Expression of heterozygous Pik3ca H1047R in transgenic mice drives clonal expansion in normal esophageal epithelium by tilting cell fate toward proliferation via the PI3K-mTOR pathway. Metabolic conditions such as type 1 diabetes or diet-induced obesity enhanced the competitive fitness of Pik3ca H1047R cells, while metformin reduced mutant cell advantage in vivo and in vitro. Higher density of PIK3CA gain-of-function mutations was found in the esophagus of individuals with high BMI compared to normal weight.

citation: Oncogenic PIK3CA corrupts growth factor signaling specificity (PMID: 39706867)
summary: Using live-cell imaging of PI3K/AKT activity reporters and CyTOF measurements, dose-dependent expression of PIK3CA H1047R in human cervical cancer and iPSCs was found to corrupt the fidelity of growth factor-induced information transfer rather than acting as a simple constitutive activator. PIK3CA H1047R preferentially amplified EGFR signaling responses compared to IGF1 and insulin receptor signaling, and also enhanced signaling heterogeneity. This demonstrates that oncogenic PIK3CA H1047R corrupts information transfer in a growth factor-dependent manner.

citation: Oncogenic PIK3CA recruits myeloid-derived suppressor cells to shape the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in luminal breast cancer through the 5-lipoxygenase-dependent arachidonic acid pathway (PMID: 37965796)
summary: PIK3CA mutant luminal breast cancer cells induce an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment by recruiting myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and excluding cytotoxic T cells via the arachidonic acid metabolism pathway. Mechanistically, PIK3CA mutations activate transcription of 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) in a STAT3-dependent manner, leading to high LTB4 production that binds BLT2 on MDSCs and promotes their infiltration. Targeted therapy against the PI3K/5-LOX/LTB4 axis combined with immune checkpoint blockade achieved dramatic tumor shrinkage in vivo.

citation: PIK3CA Mutations Downregulate PPT1 to Promote Adipogenesis by Suppressing P300 Depalmitoylation and Phase Separation (PMID: 41610323)
summary: PIK3CA mutations transcriptionally repress PPT1 via PI3K-AKT-c-JUN signaling in facial infiltrating lipomatosis (FIL), leading to enhanced palmitoylation of the transcriptional coactivator P300 at C1176. This palmitoylation stabilizes P300 by impairing its chaperone-mediated lysosomal degradation and inhibits P300 phase separation, thereby preserving its histone acetyltransferase activity and promoting chromatin accessibility and expression of adipogenic genes. This establishes a novel 'palmitoylation-phase separation-epigenetic regulation' axis linking PIK3CA mutation to excessive adipogenesis.

citation: BEX2 regulates autophagy by inhibiting PIK3CA-p85 interaction in non-small-cell lung cancer cells (PMID: 41398291)

This BEX2-PIK3CA interaction promotes autophagic flux through suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. The regulatory role of BEX2 on autophagy was confirmed to be dependent on the presence of PIK3CA.

citation: miR-29a Downregulates PIK3CA Expression and Inhibits Cervical Cancer Cell Dynamics: A Comparative Clinical Analysis (PMID: 39590348)
summary: miR-29a was shown to bind the 3'-UTR region of PIK3CA, leading to reduction in PIK3CA expression at both RNA and protein levels in PIK3CA-overexpressing cervical cancer cell lines (SiHa, C33A, HeLa). Transfection of miR-29a into HeLa cells reduced cell division and migration as demonstrated by wound healing and cell migration assays. Clinical biopsy samples from cervical cancer patients showed correlation between miR-29a concentration and disease progression.

citation: Neddylation as a target in PIK3CA-mutated head and neck cancer (PMID: 40154000)
summary: CRISPRi-based genome-wide screening in an HPV-positive HNSCC cell line (UM-SCC-47) engineered to express the canonical E545K PIK3CA mutant identified 34 genes co-dependent on PIK3CA E545K mutation, including 5 genes in the neddylation pathway (NEDD8, NEDD8-MDP-1, NAE1, USP8, UBA3). Validation experiments confirmed the essential role of NEDD8, NEDD8-MDP-1, and NAE1, indicating a novel regulatory mechanism in PIK3CA E545K-mutated HNSCC. These findings suggest PIK3CA mutation may serve as a predictive biomarker for neddylation inhibitor therapy.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Dual inhibition of mTORC1 and mTORC2 activation effectively rescues hyperproliferative lymphatic sprouting in a cell-based model system of complex lymphatic anomalies (M. Battig et al.)
summary: Expression of PIK3CA H1047L in human dermal lymphatic endothelial cells resulted in significantly greater lymphangiogenic sprouting compared to wild-type controls (cumulative sprout length 2666 µm vs. 1381 µm, p=0.029), with immunoblotting revealing over-activation of mTORC1 and mTORC2 targets. Dual mTORC1/mTORC2 inhibition with OSI-027 rescued the hyperproliferative phenotype caused by PIK3CA H1047L to basal levels. These findings demonstrate that somatic activating PIK3CA mutations drive lymphangiogenesis through over-activation of AKT/mTOR signaling.

PIK3CA was nominated as a putative risk gene near one of the novel loci using summary-based Mendelian randomization with multi-omic data. This represents a genetic association of PIK3CA with Parkinson's disease risk across ancestrally diverse populations.

summary: Using functional rescue experiments in cultured hippocampal neurons lacking all endogenous neuroligins, Nlgn2 was shown to selectively restore inhibitory synaptic transmission. Chimeric Nlgn1-Nlgn2 constructs revealed that the extracellular domain confers inhibitory synapse specificity, while the cytoplasmic sequences of Nlgn2—including its Gephyrin-binding motif—are essential for its synaptic function at inhibitory synapses but dispensable for Nlgn1 at excitatory synapses.

citation: Synaptic deficits in iPSC-derived cortical interneurons in schizophrenia are mediated by NLGN2 and rescued by N-acetylcysteine. (PMID: 31780643)
summary: iPSC-derived cortical interneurons from schizophrenia subjects showed significantly reduced levels of NLGN2 and gephyrin, along with reduced synaptic puncta density. NLGN2 overexpression rescued synaptic puncta deficits in schizophrenia neurons, while NLGN2 knockdown in healthy neurons reduced synaptic puncta density. The antioxidant N-acetylcysteine increased NLGN2 expression and rescued synaptic deficits, implicating oxidative stress as a regulator of NLGN2 expression.

citation: Functional Neuroligin-2-MDGA1 interactions differentially regulate synaptic GABAARs and cytosolic gephyrin aggregation. (PMID: 39284869)
summary: Nlgn2 interacts with MDGA1 at GABAergic synapses in hippocampal area CA1; loss of MDGA1 ameliorated the abnormal cytosolic gephyrin aggregation, reduced inhibitory synaptic transmission, and exacerbated anxiety-related behaviour seen in Nlgn2 knockout mice. Combined Nlgn2 and MDGA1 deletion caused an exacerbated layer-specific loss of gephyrin puncta, indicating that MDGA1 modulates Nlgn2 function at inhibitory synapses. These findings suggest cytosolic gephyrin aggregation as a potential therapeutic target linked to the Nlgn2-MDGA1 interaction.

citation: Physical Interactions and Functional Relationships of Neuroligin 2 and Midbrain Serotonin Transporters. (PMID: 26793096)
summary: Proteomic analysis of mouse midbrain identified NLGN2 as a component of SERT (serotonin transporter) complexes; reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation confirmed SERT/NLGN2 associations along with α-neurexin and gephyrin in a Ca2+-independent manner. Loss of NLGN2 in Nlgn2 null mice produced significant reductions in midbrain and hippocampal SERT expression and function, reduced excitability of dorsal raphe 5-HT neurons, loss of GABAA receptor-mediated IPSCs, and increased 5-HT1A autoreceptor sensitivity. These interactions were localized to somatodendritic compartments of raphe neurons, not axons.

citation: Neuroligin 2 deletion alters inhibitory synapse function and anxiety-associated neuronal activation in the amygdala. (PMID: 26142252)
summary: In Nlgn2 knockout mice, NLGN2 was found at the majority of inhibitory synapses in the basal amygdala; its deletion specifically affected postsynaptic structures at perisomatic sites and impaired inhibitory synaptic transmission. Following exposure to an anxiogenic environment, Nlgn2 KO mice showed exacerbated cFOS expression in CaMKII-positive projection neurons but not in parvalbumin- or somatostatin-positive interneurons. These results indicate that Nlgn2 deletion reduces inhibitory drive onto projection neurons, leading to their excessive activation under anxiogenic conditions.

citation: Neuroligin-2 shapes individual slow waves during slow-wave sleep and the response to sleep deprivation in mice. (PMID: 38570872)
summary: Nlgn2 knockout mice exhibited greater slow-wave amplitude and density during slow-wave sleep, with SW density being the main contributor to altered 24-h dynamics of delta activity. Absence of Nlgn2 accelerated paradoxical sleep recovery following sleep deprivation and caused profound alterations in ECoG activity across vigilance states. RNA sequencing in wild-type mice confirmed that sleep deprivation decreases cortical expression of Nlgn2 and related GABAergic transcripts.

citation: Expression alteration of Neuroligin family gene in attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder and autism spectrum disorder. (PMID: 37285744)
summary: Quantitative PCR of peripheral blood from 450 ASD patients, 450 ADHD patients, and 490 controls showed that NLGN2 mRNA was significantly down-regulated in both ASD and ADHD groups compared to controls. NLGN2 was significantly more down-regulated in ASD subjects compared to ADHD subjects. These findings suggest NLGN2 expression changes in peripheral blood may reflect its role in the etiology of both neurodevelopmental disorders.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Targeted sequencing of postsynaptic protein genes associated with schizophrenia: A role for multiple rare risk mutations in schizophrenia susceptibility. (M. Cheng et al.)
summary: Targeted sequencing of 18 postsynaptic protein genes in 98 schizophrenia patients identified a rare missense mutation NLGN2:p.R309Q absent in 1517 healthy controls. Immunoblot analysis in HEK293 cells showed that the NLGN2 R309Q mutant had decreased protein expression compared to wild-type. Genotyping in an independent sample of 500 cases and 500 controls confirmed this mutation was schizophrenia-specific.

citation: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants. (PMID: 35468861)
summary: Integrative analysis of de novo SNVs in 41,165 NDD individuals and de novo CNVs in 3,675 NDD individuals identified NLGN2 as one of 11 high-confidence candidate NDD genes with >90% true-positive probability based on deep learning similarity to known NDD genes. NLGN2 achieved statistical significance (5% FDR) for enrichment of de novo deleterious variants. Its validity was supported by similarity in function and gene expression patterns to established NDD genes.

citation: A meiosis-specific cyclin regulated by splicing is required for proper progression through meiosis (PMID: 16024772)
summary: Rem1 is a fission yeast (S. pombe) B-type cyclin expressed exclusively during meiosis. Cells lacking Rem1 show impaired meiotic recombination and require Rem1 for premeiotic DNA synthesis when Cig2 is absent. rem1 expression is regulated at both transcription and splicing levels, with Mei4 as a positive and Cig2 as a negative splicing factor.

citation: Promoter-driven splicing regulation in fission yeast (PMID: 18815595)
summary: rem1 expression in S. pombe is regulated at both transcription and splicing levels, encoding two proteins with different functions depending on intron retention. The rem1 promoter is sufficient to confer meiotic-specific splicing regulation to heterologous intron-containing genes. Forkhead transcription factors Mei4 and Fkh2 control this regulation: Mei4 induces both transcription and splicing, while Fkh2 causes intron retention during vegetative growth and pre-meiotic S phase.

citation: A dominant role for meiosis-specific 3' RNA processing in controlling expression of a fission yeast cyclin gene (PMID: 22647846)
summary: Cleavage/polyadenylation is a key regulatory mechanism for rem1 expression in fission yeast meiosis, with polyadenylation of rem1 transcripts restricted to meiosis by a splicing-independent mechanism. A negative control region (NCR) upstream of the rem1 transcription start site blocks 3' RNA processing in proliferating cells. A second 3' processing site within the intron is activated during meiosis, revealing a novel regulatory interplay between splicing and polyadenylation.

citation: Negative control contributes to an extensive program of meiotic splicing in fission yeast (PMID: 15893732)
summary: rem1 is one of 12 transcripts identified in S. pombe that retain introns until specific times during meiotic differentiation, establishing regulated splicing as a major mechanism for meiotic gene expression control. Splicing of rem1 is regulated by sequences outside the coding regions, far from the target introns. Gene chimera analyses indicate splicing is prevented in mitotically growing cells via inhibition rather than positive activation.

citation: Adrenergic signaling controls RGK-dependent trafficking of cardiac voltage-gated L-type Ca2+ channels through PKD1 (PMID: 22076634)
summary: Rem1 (mammalian RGK family GTPase) is strongly and specifically expressed in cardiac tissue. Activation of protein kinase D1 downstream of α1-adrenergic signaling leads to direct phosphorylation of Rem1 at Ser18, releasing its inhibition of voltage-gated L-type calcium channels (VLCCs) and increasing channel activity and transverse-tubule expression in cardiomyocytes.

citation: RASSF effectors couple diverse RAS subfamily GTPases to the Hippo pathway (PMID: 33051258)
summary: The tumor suppressor RASSF1A was demonstrated to form complexes with the RAS-related GTPase REM1 (along with GEM, REM2, and RASL12). Interactions between RASSFs and RAS GTPases including REM1 blocked YAP1 nuclear localization, linking REM1 to Hippo pathway regulation.

citation: Ras associated with diabetes may play a role in fracture nonunion development in rats (PMID: 31830958)
summary: Rem1 expression was examined in rat fracture callus and fibrous tissue from standard healing fractures and nonunions at multiple post-fracture time points by real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry. Immunolocalization of Rem1 protein was similar to that of Rad in both fracture types at post-fracture days 14 and 21, suggesting co-expression in fracture healing tissue.

citation: Biochemical and structural characterization of the gem GTPase (PMID: 17107948)
summary: REM1 is identified as a member of the RGK protein family (along with Rad, Gem, and Rem2), a branch of the Ras superfamily characterized by atypical nucleotide binding motifs and large N- and C-terminal extensions. RGK proteins including Rem1 are regulated at the transcriptional level and function as inhibitors of voltage-gated calcium channels.

citation: Rapid Oligo-Galacturonide Induced Changes in Protein Phosphorylation in Arabidopsis (PMID: 26811356)
summary: The Arabidopsis REM1.3 protein (a remorin scaffold protein) was identified as a phosphoprotein in a quantitative phosphoproteomic screen for OG (oligo-galacturonide)-induced signaling. Null mutants in REM1.3 enhance a dominant WAK allele phenotype, and REM1.3 is implicated as a membrane-associated scaffold in the WAK-dependent cell wall stress signaling pathway.

citation: Spontaneous mitotic recombination in yeast: the hyper-recombinational rem1 mutations are alleles of the RAD3 gene (PMID: 2840336)
summary: The rem1 mutations in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which confer enhanced spontaneous mitotic recombination and mutation, were identified as alleles of the RAD3 gene by genetic mapping, complementation, and DNA hybridization. Double mutants of rem1 with recombination-repair pathway defects are inviable, and rem1 strains show smaller DNA size than wild type, suggesting rem1/RAD3 mutations cause DNA damage that requires recombination-repair for survival.

citation: Pathogenic de novo variants in PPP2R5C cause a neurodevelopmental disorder within the Houge-Janssens syndrome spectrum. (PMID: 39978342)
summary: De novo missense variants in PPP2R5C (encoding the PP2A regulatory B56γ subunit) cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, epilepsy, behavioral problems, and macrocephaly. Variants affect substrate binding, C-subunit binding, or both, and variably impair PP2A catalytic activity. A dominant-negative mechanism on substrate dephosphorylation is proposed as the pathogenic mechanism.

citation: Growth arrest of PPP2R5C and PPP2R5D double knockout mice indicates a genetic interaction and conserved function for these PP2A B subunits. (PMID: 35415460)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9n knockout of both B56δ (PPP2R5D) and B56γ (PPP2R5C) in mice causes fetal developmental arrest around embryonic day E12, with hearts displaying a single outflow vessel instead of separate aorta and pulmonary artery. Individual knockouts of B56γ alone are viable, indicating a strong genetic interaction between B56δ and B56γ specifically required for heart development. This suggests B56γ and B56δ form a functional subfamily within the B56 family.

citation: Activation of ERK/IER3/PP2A-B56γ-positive feedback loop in lung adenocarcinoma by allelic deletion of B56γ gene. (PMID: 26986830)
summary: Allelic deletion of PPP2R5C was found in 4 of 8 informative lung adenocarcinoma cases (50%), and PPP2R5C deletion or EGFR mutation together accounted for IER3/pERK overexpression in at least 67% of cases. PPP2R5C loss is proposed to activate an ERK/IER3/PP2A-B56γ positive feedback loop driving sustained ERK phosphorylation in adenocarcinoma. This is the first report of high-frequency PPP2R5C deletion in human carcinomas.

citation: Differential gene expression profiles of PPP2R5C-siRNA-treated malignant T cells. (PMID: 23941244)
summary: siRNA-mediated knockdown of PPP2R5C in Molt-4 and Jurkat T-cell leukemia lines significantly reduced proliferation without inducing apoptosis. Global gene expression profiling revealed 963 differentially expressed genes, with changes in TCR, Wnt, calcium, MAPK, and p53 signaling pathway genes; notably GSK-3β, ATM, and MDM2 were altered. This implicates PPP2R5C in multiple oncogenic signaling networks in T-cell malignancy.

citation: Proliferation inhibition and apoptosis induction of imatinib-resistant chronic myeloid leukemia cells via PPP2R5C down-regulation. (PMID: 24004697)
sample_size: 4 cell lines + primary CML patient cells
summary: PPP2R5C siRNA knockdown in imatinib-sensitive (K562, 32D-Bcr-Abl WT) and imatinib-resistant (K562R, 32D-Bcr-Abl T315I) CML cell lines and primary CML patient cells significantly reduced proliferation and induced apoptosis at 72 hours. Imatinib-resistant K562R cells showed significantly greater proliferation inhibition and apoptosis induction than sensitive K562 cells upon PPP2R5C knockdown. These results suggest PPP2R5C as a potential therapeutic target for imatinib-resistant CML.

citation: LincR-PPP2R5C Promotes Th2 Cell Differentiation Through PPP2R5C/PP2A by Forming an RNA-DNA Triplex in Allergic Asthma. (PMID: 38262392)

LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency suppressed PP2A phosphatase activity and reduced Th2 polarization, airway hyperresponsiveness, and inflammation. This establishes PPP2R5C/PP2A as a key axis in CD4+ T-cell Th2 differentiation downstream of a lncRNA regulatory mechanism.

The affinity of Nrl binding to the Ppp2r5c promoter is dynamically regulated during mouse photoreceptor development. This identifies Ppp2r5c as a transcriptional target of Nrl during retinogenesis.

These findings suggest PPP2R5C influences osteosarcoma metastasis via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

citation: Prognostic Impact of PPP2R5C Gene Expression in Adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia Patients with Normal Cytogenetics. (PMID: 32158086)

High PPP2R5C expression correlated with unfavorable response to induction chemotherapy and significantly worse overall survival and progression-free survival. PPP2R5C overexpression was identified as an adverse prognostic factor in cytogenetically normal AML.
