citation: Gene therapy with phosphodiesterases 2A and 4B ameliorates heart failure and arrhythmias by improving subcellular cAMP compartmentation (PMID: 38776406)
summary: AAV9-mediated overexpression of PDE2A3 in a mouse pressure-overload heart failure model attenuated cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and contractile decline. Live cell imaging with targeted cAMP biosensors showed PDE2A overexpression restored altered cAMP compartmentation in caveolin-rich plasma membrane microdomains, accompanied by ameliorated caveolin-3 decline and antiarrhythmic effects under isoproterenol stimulation.

citation: Activation of PDE2A moderates pathologically high cAMP/PKA responses to dopamine in dyskinetic mice (PMID: 40412662)
summary: In the 6-OHDA mouse model of Parkinson's disease, cAMP and PKA signaling were markedly upregulated in striatal neurons. Stimulation of cGMP signaling by a NO donor (DEANO) efficiently down-regulated these hypersensitive cAMP/PKA responses via PDE2A activation, demonstrating that cGMP-stimulated PDE2A activity can moderate excessive D1 receptor-driven cAMP/PKA signaling in the striatum.

citation: miR-139/PDE2A-Notch1 feedback circuit represses stemness of gliomas by inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling (PMID: 34512162)
summary: PDE2A overexpression in patient-derived glioma stem-like cells suppressed stemness by inhibiting cAMP accumulation and GSK-3β phosphorylation, thereby reducing Wnt/β-catenin signaling and self-renewal. Both PDE2A and its co-transcribed miR-139 were inversely correlated with glioma stem cell stemness and associated with better prognosis in clinical samples. Targeted delivery of PDE2A via OCP liposomes significantly repressed stemness and decelerated glioma progression in orthotopic xenograft models.

citation: Defects in AMPAR trafficking and microglia activation underlie socio-cognitive deficits associated to decreased expression of phosphodiesterase 2A (PMID: 38154608)
summary: Pde2a+/- mice (homozygous knockouts are non-viable) displayed sex-dependent socio-cognitive deficits, with males showing severe deficits throughout life and females showing milder adult-onset cognitive impairment. In males, these phenotypes were associated with microglia activation, elevated glutathione levels, and increased GluR1 externalization in CA1, producing reduced mGluR-dependent long-term depression, revealing PDE2A-dependent molecular targets underlying socio-cognitive performance.

citation: PDE2A Inhibition Enhances Axonal Sprouting, Functional Connectivity, and Recovery after Stroke (PMID: 36163142)
summary: Pharmacological inhibition of PDE2A in a mouse cortical stroke model enhanced functional recovery of the contralateral forelimb, increased axonal projections in peri-infarct cortex, and improved functional connectivity of motor system excitatory neurons as measured by two-photon in vivo imaging. PDE2A inhibition did not affect angiogenesis, gliogenesis, neurogenesis, or inflammatory responses, suggesting its pro-recovery effects are specifically mediated through neuronal connectivity mechanisms.

citation: Phosphodiesterases PDE2A and PDE10A both change mRNA expression in the human brain with age, but only PDE2A changes in a region-specific manner with psychiatric disease (PMID: 32119913)
sample_size: Stanley Foundation Neuropathology Consortium postmortem cohort
summary: Using autoradiographic in situ hybridization on postmortem brain tissue, PDE2A mRNA was found to be reduced in the amygdala of patients with schizophrenia, MDD, and bipolar disorder, while frontal cortical reductions were specific to schizophrenia and hippocampal/striatal reductions were most pronounced in bipolar disorder. PDE2A mRNA expression increased across brain development, and its region- and disorder-specific changes implicate it as a potential diagnostic biomarker or therapeutic target in psychiatric disease.

citation: PDE2A Is Indispensable for Mouse Liver Development and Hematopoiesis (PMID: 32326334)
summary: PDE2A knockout mice are embryonic lethal, and at E14.5 their livers are extremely reduced in size with loss of niche integrity, compromised hematopoietic function, and apoptosis in hepatoblasts and endothelial/stromal compartments. Increased intracellular cAMP and upregulation of the inducible cAMP early repressor (ICER) in PDE2A-/- livers likely impairs development by downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl2, establishing PDE2A as essential for liver niche integrity and hematopoiesis.

citation: Critical role of phosphodiesterase 2A in mouse congenital heart defects (PMID: 29409032)
summary: PDE2A knockout embryos exhibited cardiac defects including absence of atrial trabeculation, interventricular septum defects, hypertrabeculation, myocardial wall thinning, and occasionally overriding aorta and valve defects. Loss of PDE2A caused increased intracellular cAMP, upregulation of ICER, downregulation of Tbx transcription factors, reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation, and increased apoptosis, demonstrating a direct role for PDE2A-mediated cAMP regulation in cardiac development.

citation: Involvement of Phosphodiesterase 2A Activity in the Pathophysiology of Fragile X Syndrome (PMID: 30137253)
summary: PDE2A enzymatic activity is increased in the brain of Fmr1-KO mice (a Fragile X Syndrome model), leading to decreased cAMP and cGMP levels, as PDE2A mRNA is a prominent target of FMRP. Pharmacological inhibition of PDE2A in Fmr1-KO mice rescued dendritic spine maturity, hippocampal mGluR-dependent LTD, and social/communicative deficits in both mouse and rat models, with chronic neonatal inhibition followed by washout rescuing adolescent social behavior.

citation: Differential expression of the cyclic GMP-stimulated phosphodiesterase PDE2A in human venous and capillary endothelial cells (PMID: 10375378)
summary: Using selective monoclonal antibodies, PDE2A protein was detected in cerebellum, neocortex, heart, kidney, lung, pulmonary artery, and skeletal muscle. Immunocytochemical analysis revealed PDE2A expression specifically in venous and capillary endothelial cells but not in arterial endothelial cells of cardiac and renal tissue, with expression also present in microvascular endothelial cells of renal glomerulus, skin, brain, and liver, suggesting a role in modulating cyclic nucleotide effects on endothelial barrier function.

citation: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism (PMID: 40166812)
summary: RAB3A encodes a small GTP-binding protein abundant in brain synaptic vesicles, crucial for neurotransmitter release and synaptic plasticity. Heterozygous variants, including the recurrent p.Arg83Trp, cause autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia; variants in the GAP-binding domain reduce GAP-dependent GTP hydrolysis. Co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry revealed differential changes in variant-specific interactions with known RAB3A regulatory and effector proteins.

citation: RAB3 phosphorylation by pathogenic LRRK2 impairs trafficking of synaptic vesicle precursors (PMID: 38512027)
summary: Hyperphosphorylation of RAB3A by pathogenic LRRK2-p.R1441H in iPSC-derived human neurons disrupts anterograde axonal transport of synaptic vesicle precursors, causing sequestration of synaptophysin and synaptobrevin-2 in the soma. RAB3A phosphorylation disrupts binding to the motor adaptor MADD, preventing formation of the RAB3A-MADD-KIF1A/1Bβ transport complex, and also disrupts interactions with RAB3GAP and RAB-GDI1.

citation: Molecular and functional interactions of alpha-synuclein with Rab3a (PMID: 35809645)
summary: Alpha-synuclein interacts with GTP-bound Rab3a via its C-terminus in a manner similar to its interaction with Rab8a, with the interaction strengthened on lipid membrane surfaces. Alpha-synuclein inhibits GTP hydrolysis by Rab3a, and this inhibition is more potent on membrane surfaces. Phosphorylation of alpha-synuclein at Ser129, associated with Parkinson's disease pathology, enhances its interaction with Rab3a and increases inhibition of Rab3a GTP hydrolysis.

citation: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism (PMID: 40166812)
summary: In a Drosophila Rab3 loss-of-function model, the two missense variants p.Arg83Trp and p.Tyr91Cys failed to rescue a synaptic phenotype, consistent with partial loss-of-function. Overexpression of Rab3 variants in a Drosophila wild-type background did not cause an obvious phenotype, making a dominant negative effect unlikely.

citation: zDHHC9 Regulates Cardiomyocyte Rab3a Activity and Atrial Natriuretic Peptide Secretion Through Palmitoylation of Rab3gap1 (PMID: 37325411)
summary: The Golgi S-acyltransferase zDHHC9 palmitoylates Rab3gap1, causing its spatial segregation from Rab3a, elevation of Rab3a-GTP levels, formation of Rab3a-positive peripheral vesicles, and impairment of exocytosis that limits atrial natriuretic peptide release in cardiomyocytes. This identifies a novel regulatory pathway linking palmitoylation to Rab3a GTP-loading state and cardiomyocyte exocytosis.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Identification of interactions in the MADD PTPRN RAB3 complex with type 2 diabetes in multiple populations
summary: Gene-gene interactions among MADD, PTPRN/PTPRN2, and RAB3A/RAB3C were identified in association with type 2 diabetes across eight independent multi-ethnic studies totaling 15,502 participants. MADD acts as a GDP/GTP exchange factor for RAB3A/RAB3C to provide energy for moving insulin-containing dense core secretory vesicles to the membrane for insulin release. Single-gene analyses did not find significant associations, highlighting the importance of the protein complex interaction.

citation: Rab3A mediates vesicle delivery at photoreceptor ribbon synapses (PMID: 22593061)
summary: Fluorescently labeled Rab3A binds to and dissociates from synaptic ribbons in tiger salamander photoreceptors in a GTP hydrolysis-dependent manner. A GTPase-deficient Rab3A mutant blocks synaptic release in an activity-dependent manner in paired recordings from photoreceptors and OFF-bipolar cells. These findings suggest Rab3A plays a crucial role in delivering vesicles to Ca²⁺-dependent release sites at ribbon synapses.

citation: Rab3A interacts with spastin to regulate neurite outgrowth in hippocampal neurons (PMID: 36587525)
summary: Rab3A physically interacts with spastin in rat brain lysates and co-localizes with spastin in cultured hippocampal neurons. Rab3A overexpression induces lysosomal and ubiquitin-mediated degradation of spastin, abolishing spastin-mediated microtubule severing. Overexpression of Rab3A inhibits neurite outgrowth while knockdown promotes it, with the inhibitory effect reversed by co-transfection of spastin.

citation: Association of variants in the KIF1A gene with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (PMID: 36284339)
summary: ALS-associated KIF1A variants in the C-terminal cargo-binding region preferentially enhanced binding of synaptic vesicle precursors containing RAB3A, VAMP2, and synaptophysin. Expression of disease-related KIF1A mutants in cultured mouse cortical neurons led to enhanced colocalization of RAB3A with the KIF1A motor, suggesting dysregulated RAB3A-containing vesicle transport in ALS pathogenesis.

citation: Rab3a attenuates spinal cord injury by mediating vesicle release (PMID: 38253132)
summary: Rab3a was significantly downregulated in a rat spinal cord injury (SCI) model, and Rab3a overexpression promoted SCI repair. Rab3a knockdown in neuronal cells inhibited secretion of neuronal cell-derived extracellular vesicles and promoted M1 macrophage polarization and neuronal apoptosis. STXBP1 was identified as a binding protein of Rab3a, and their interaction promoted neuronal cell-derived EV secretion; METTL2b was found to regulate Rab3a protein expression.

phenotype: Decreased level of DIO2 protein in oligodendrocyte lineage cells; Decreased T3 (active thyroid hormone) levels in CNS; Impaired oligodendrocyte differentiation; Hypomyelination; Motor deficits in both sexes; Defective OL differentiation rescued by T3 or T3 analog but not T4

citation: The expression of essential selenoproteins during development requires SECIS-binding protein 2-like. (PMID: 35210313)
summary: CRISPR knockout of secisbp2l in zebrafish showed that secisbp2l-/- embryos retain the full complement of selenoproteins (unlike sbp2-/- embryos which lose a subset), but double knockout of both sbp2 and secisbp2l completely prevents selenoprotein synthesis, causing juvenile death at 14 days post fertilization. SECISBP2L is proposed to promote essential selenoprotein synthesis when SBP2 activity is compromised, acting as a functional paralog of SBP2 in the selenocysteine incorporation machinery.

citation: SECISBP2L-Mediated Selenoprotein Synthesis Is Essential for Autonomous Regulation of Oligodendrocyte Differentiation. (PMID: 35760530)
summary: SECISBP2L is highly expressed in differentiating oligodendrocytes (OLs) and is required for DIO2 (deiodinase 2) translation. Conditional knockout of Secisbp2l in OL lineage in mice resulted in decreased DIO2 and active thyroid hormone T3 levels, impaired OL differentiation, hypomyelination, and motor deficits, establishing a SECISBP2L-DIO2-T3 pathway for autonomous regulation of myelination.

citation: SECISBP2L-Mediated Selenoprotein Synthesis Is Essential for Autonomous Regulation of Oligodendrocyte Differentiation. (PMID: 35760530)
summary: SECISBP2L is specifically and highly expressed in differentiating oligodendrocytes in the CNS, distinguishing it from SBP2 and suggesting a cell-type-specific role in selenoprotein translation during myelin development.

summary: A large GWAS of 29,266 lung cancer cases and 56,450 controls identified new susceptibility loci, and eQTL analysis in 1,425 normal lung tissue samples highlighted SECISBP2L as a candidate gene at one of the associated loci, suggesting that genetic variants influencing lung cancer risk may act through regulation of SECISBP2L expression.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Defining the genetic architecture of lung cancer etiology. (C.I. Amos et al.)
summary: In the largest GWAS of lung cancer susceptibility (29,863 cases, 55,586 controls), eQTL analysis in normal lung tissue identified a consistent cis-acting effect of variant rs77468143 on SECISBP2L expression, implicating SECISBP2L as a functional candidate gene at a lung cancer susceptibility locus.

citation: Cross-Trait Genetic Analyses Indicate Pleiotropy and Complex Causal Relationships between Headache and Thyroid Function Traits. (PMID: 36672757)

citation: Construction and Validation of Prognostic Regulation Network Based on RNA-Binding Protein Genes in Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma. (PMID: 34931870)

citation: Rab5c-mediated endocytic trafficking regulates hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell development via Notch and AKT signaling (PMID: 32275659)
summary: Rab5c is essential for hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) specification in zebrafish embryos through endocytic trafficking of Notch ligands/receptor and AKT signaling. Rab5c deficiency caused defects in HSPC production, and its interaction with Appl1 in endosomes was required for hemogenic endothelium survival. Both loss and overactivation of Rab5c disrupted HSPC production, demonstrating a dosage-sensitive role in endolysosomal trafficking.

citation: The endosomal RIN2/Rab5C machinery prevents VEGFR2 degradation to control gene expression and tip cell identity during angiogenesis (PMID: 33983539)
summary: RIN2/Rab5C prevents lysosomal degradation of internalized VEGFR2 in human endothelial cells, sustaining VEGF signaling through ERK and PI3-K pathways and enabling tip cell specification and sprouting angiogenesis. Knockdown and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated editing of Rab5C disrupted VEGFR2 stabilization, impaired immediate VEGF target gene expression, and blocked developmental angiogenesis in zebrafish in vivo. This identifies an endosomal feedforward mechanism linking receptor trafficking to cell fate determination.

citation: RAB5c controls the assembly of non-canonical autophagy machinery to promote phagosome maturation and microbicidal function of macrophages (PMID: 40196584)
summary: RAB5c is necessary for LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) in macrophages by regulating phagosome recruitment of PI(3)P- and ROS-generating complexes and facilitating V-ATPase translocation required for ATG16L1 binding and LC3 conjugation. RAB5c depletion impaired macrophage elimination of Aspergillus fumigatus, and disruption of the V-ATPase-ATG16L1 axis increased susceptibility in vivo. This identifies RAB5c as a specific isoform controlling non-canonical autophagy machinery assembly at phagosomes.

citation: RAB5C Increases Endothelial Release of VWF by Regulating Vesicle Trafficking (PMID: 41537263)
summary: RAB5C regulates von Willebrand Factor (VWF) exocytosis from human endothelial cells; silencing decreased VWF release while overexpression or constitutively active RAB5C increased it. Proximity labeling and mass spectrometry identified 147 RAB5C-proximal proteins involved in vesicle trafficking, with SNAP29 (a SNARE-associated protein) identified as a key RAB5C interactor mediating VWF exocytosis. Two GWAS-identified variants (rs9915255 and rs9912088) were shown to regulate RAB5C expression in stem cell-derived endothelial cells.

citation: Rab5 isoforms orchestrate a 'division of labor' in the endocytic network; Rab5C modulates Rac-mediated cell motility (PMID: 24587345)
summary: Among the three Rab5 isoforms, only Rab5C silencing reduced membrane ruffle formation, cell migration in scratch wound and Transwell assays, and EGF-stimulated Rac1 and Akt activation in HeLa and U937 cells. Rab5C-depleted cells had significantly fewer focal adhesion foci and reduced peripheral GFP-Rac1 localization. This demonstrates isoform-specific roles, with Rab5C selectively coupling growth factor signaling to Rac-mediated cell motility.

citation: Rab5C enhances resistance to ionizing radiation in rectal cancer (PMID: 30968159)
sample_size: Stage II/III rectal adenocarcinoma patient biopsies
summary: Rab5C protein expression was significantly increased in rectal adenocarcinoma biopsy specimens after neoadjuvant chemoradiation and in a radiotherapy-resistant cell line generated in vitro. Rab5C was found to modulate EGFR internalization and its nuclear relocalization in response to irradiation, which in turn regulated expression of DNA repair proteins Ku70 and Ku80 and conferred radioresistance. These findings identify Rab5C as a potential target for sensitizing rectal cancer cells to radiotherapy.

citation: Regulation of RAB5C is important for the growth inhibitory effects of MiR-509 in human precursor-B acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 25368993)
summary: A genome-wide gain-of-function miRNA screen identified miR-509 as an inhibitor of B-ALL cell growth, and RAB5C was validated as a direct target of miR-509 in NALM6 cells. Enforced miR-509 expression reduced RAB5C mRNA and protein levels, decreased proliferating cells, and increased apoptosis; RAB5C knockdown alone recapitulated these effects. Re-expression of RAB5C ORF without its 3'UTR rescued the growth-inhibitory phenotype, establishing RAB5C as an oncogenic regulator of B-ALL cell growth.

citation: S100P is a ferroptosis suppressor to facilitate hepatocellular carcinoma development by rewiring lipid metabolism (PMID: 39779666)
summary: RAB5C directs ACC1 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha) to the lysosome via P62-dependent selective autophagy, mediating S100P-induced lysosomal degradation of ACC1 in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Knockdown of RAB5C abrogated S100P-induced ACC1 degradation and restored ferroptotic sensitivity of HCC cells. This places RAB5C in an anti-ferroptosis pathway linking selective autophagy to lipid metabolism regulation.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Coronary artery disease-associated splicing variants in vascular smooth muscle cells (N. Perry et al.)
summary: A splicing QTL analysis of 151 aortic smooth muscle cell donors identified RAB5C as one of six genes containing SNPs both within CAD GWAS loci and highly predicted to affect SMC-specific alternative splicing events. Long-read PacBio sequencing confirmed the splicing predictions, suggesting RAB5C may contribute to CAD susceptibility through altered splicing in vascular smooth muscle cells.

citation: SLC18A3 variants lead to fetal akinesia deformation sequence early in pregnancy (PMID: 31059209)
phenotype: lethal phenotype; fetal akinesia (inferred from reference to VAChT knockout mice showing lethal phenotype consistent with human FADS presentation)

citation: Vesicular acetylcholine transporter defect underlies devastating congenital myasthenia syndrome (PMID: 28188302)
summary: A homozygous missense mutation SLC18A3 c.1078G>C (p.Gly360Arg) was identified in two brothers with severe congenital myasthenic syndrome featuring hypotonia, arthrogryposis, and respiratory failure. Stable transfection of mutant VAChT into PC12A123.7 neuronal-like cells showed similar mRNA levels but undetectable mutant protein, indicating post-translational degradation. This established SLC18A3/VAChT loss-of-function as a presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome.

citation: SLC18: Vesicular neurotransmitter transporters for monoamines and acetylcholine (PMID: 23506877)
summary: SLC18A3 encodes the vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT), which actively transports acetylcholine from the neuronal cytoplasm into synaptic vesicles for exocytotic release. It is a member of the Drug:H+ Antiporter-1 Family (DHA1) within the Major Facilitator Superfamily (MFS). This is its core molecular function enabling cholinergic neurotransmission.

citation: SLC18A3 promoted renal cancer development through acetylcholine/cAMP signaling (PMID: 36225635)
sample_size: Renal cancer patient samples; A498 mouse xenograft model
summary: SLC18A3 is upregulated in renal cancer patients and enhances uptake of acetylcholine, which activates the PKA/CREB pathway to promote cancer cell proliferation and invasive migration. SLC18A3 overexpression in A498-bearing mice caused sustained tumor growth and increased lung metastases. This study identifies SLC18A3 as a driver of renal cancer spread via ACh/PKA/CREB-dependent signaling.

citation: Arsenic Impairs Differentiation of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells into Cholinergic Motor Neurons (PMID: 37624150)
summary: RNA sequencing of human iPSC-derived early motor neurons exposed to 0.5 µM arsenic showed downregulation of SLC18A3 transcript levels as part of impaired cholinergic synapse pathway. SLC18A3 was identified alongside CHAT, SLC5A7, and ACHE as a key gene in acetylcholine synthesis and transport that is disrupted by arsenic exposure. This demonstrates SLC18A3's role in cholinergic function during human motor neuron differentiation.

citation: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of human paravertebral sympathetic chain ganglia reveals diabetes-induced neuroplasticity (PMID: 40667173)
summary: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of human lumbar sympathetic chain ganglia identified a distinct cholinergic neuronal population defined by SLC18A3 expression, distinguishing it from two noradrenergic populations defined by tyrosine hydroxylase. In diabetic SCGs, cholinergic neurons showed a phenotypic shift toward a noradrenergic identity, suggesting SLC18A3-expressing neurons are vulnerable to diabetes-induced neuroplasticity. This establishes SLC18A3 as a marker of cholinergic neurons in human autonomic ganglia.

citation: Gene expression profiles in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of Asian obstructive sleep apnea patients (PMID: 24732660)
summary: SLC18A3 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) was significantly differentially expressed in patients with severe obstructive sleep apnea (RDI > 30) compared to controls. SLC18A3 was identified as a potential biomarker for severe OSA in Asian populations. This represents an unexpected non-neuronal expression context for SLC18A3.

citation: The cholinergic system in rat testis is of non-neuronal origin (PMID: 21482687)
summary: SLC18A3/VAChT mRNA was detected in non-neuronal cells of rat testicular parenchyma, including spermatogonia, spermatocytes, and Sertoli cells, in regions completely lacking innervation as confirmed by absence of PGP9.5 labeling. This demonstrates that SLC18A3 is expressed as part of a non-neuronal cholinergic system in the testis, suggesting a role in germ cell differentiation. ACh was confirmed present in testicular tissue by HPLC.

citation: Transcriptome-scale spatial gene expression in rat arcuate nucleus during puberty (PMID: 35063020)
sample_size: Female Sprague-Dawley rats at postnatal days 25, 35, and 45
summary: SLC18A3 was identified as a unique membrane surface biomarker selectively expressed by kisspeptin neurons in the arcuate nucleus (ARC) of female rats, enabling their isolation by flow cytometry. SLC18A3 expression distinguished one of four neuronal subclusters in the ARC across pubertal stages (postnatal days 25, 35, and 45). This finding reveals an unexpected role for SLC18A3 as a cell-surface marker for kisspeptin neurons involved in hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis regulation.

citation: Identifying genetic variants for heart rate variability in the acetylcholine pathway (PMID: 25384021)
significance: No significant associations after multiple testing correction
summary: 443 common genetic variants in eight acetylcholine pathway genes including SLC18A3 were tested for association with heart rate variability (RMSSD) in a two-stage study of individuals of European descent. No statistically significant associations were found for SLC18A3 or other pathway genes with RMSSD after correction for multiple testing. This is the largest candidate gene study of the acetylcholine pathway and heart rate variability to date.

citation: Effects of cylindrospermopsin, chlorpyrifos and their combination in a SH-SY5Y cell model concerning developmental neurotoxicity (PMID: 38091671)
summary: Exposure of differentiating SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells to the EC20 concentration of cylindrospermopsin (0.097 µM) for 6 days downregulated SLC18A3 (vesicular acetylcholine transporter) expression along with four other genes important for neuronal development. SLC18A3 downregulation was identified as part of a transcriptomic signature of developmental neurotoxicity in this cholinergic cell model. This implicates SLC18A3 as a sensitive marker of cholinergic disruption during neuronal differentiation.

citation: Identifying the Fourth Patient With Spastic Paraplegia 90, Extending the Phenotype Spectrum (PMID: 40533086)
variant_detail: p.Thr51Ile
phenotype: global developmental delay; inability to walk; axial hypotonia; extremity spasticity; dystonia; distal renal tubular acidosis; recurrent urinary tract infections; nephrolithiasis; neurogenic bladder; primary polydipsia
diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous pathogenic variant identified by exome sequencing; recurrent variant previously detected in two other reported patients with SPG90

citation: SPTSSA variants alter sphingolipid synthesis and cause a complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (PMID: 36718090)
summary: SPTSSA encodes an activating subunit of serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT), the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo sphingolipid synthesis. Two pathogenic variants in SPTSSA (missense p.Thr51Ile and a frameshift) impaired negative regulation of SPT by ORMDL proteins, leading to excessive sphingolipid synthesis. This caused a complex hereditary spastic paraplegia with progressive motor disturbance, variable sensorineural hearing loss, and language/cognitive dysfunction in three children.

citation: ASHG 2022 - SPTSSA variants alter sphingolipid synthesis and cause a complex form of hereditary spastic paraplegia
summary: Overexpression of human SPT in Drosophila caused excessive sphingolipid synthesis, severe motor defects, and shortened lifespan. Co-expression of human ORMDL3 rescued phenotypes in flies expressing wild-type SPT but failed to rescue flies expressing the SPTSSA p.Thr51Ile variant, confirming that this variant abrogates ORMDL regulation of SPT in vivo. Elevated sphingolipids were also confirmed in serum and fibroblasts from patients.

citation: Structural insights into the assembly and substrate selectivity of human SPT-ORMDL3 complex (PMID: 33558762)
summary: Cryo-EM structures of the human SPT complex revealed that SPTSSA (SPTssa) participates in acyl-CoA coordination, stimulating SPT activity and regulating substrate selectivity. SPTSSA is a component of the SPT complex alongside SPTLC1 and SPTLC2, and its structural role in acyl-CoA binding was directly visualized. ORMDL3 is located at the center of the complex and stabilizes SPT assembly, with SPTSSA Thr51 residing in close association with ORMDL3.

citation: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen reveals that the aryl hydrocarbon receptor stimulates sphingolipid levels (PMID: 32029474)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 loss-of-function screen in HeLa cells identified SPTSSA as required for globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) biosynthesis. The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) was found to bind and activate the SPTSSA gene promoter, upregulating its expression and thereby stimulating de novo sphingolipid synthesis. AHR knockout cells showed reduced Gb3 and decreased SPTSSA expression, and Ahr knockout mouse sciatic nerve showed reduced ceramide content and myelin thickness.

citation: Human Rhinovirus Infection of the Respiratory Tract Affects Sphingolipid Synthesis (PMID: 34851798)
summary: Rhinovirus (RV) infection in mice shifted lung sphingolipid synthesis gene expression to a pattern resembling genetic SPT deficiency, including decreased expression of Sptssa, particularly in lung epithelial (EpCAM+) cells. This pattern was reproduced in human bronchial epithelial cells infected with RV, but RV did not affect Sptssa expression in lung CD45+ immune cells. RV exacerbated SPT deficiency-associated airway hyperreactivity, linking Sptssa downregulation to asthma-relevant pathophysiology.

citation: SPTSSA facilitates gastric cancer progression with modulating PD-L1 in immunomicroenvironment through Wnt/β-catenin pathway (PMID: 40498284)
summary: SPTSSA overexpression enhanced malignant phenotypes of gastric cancer cells in vitro and in vivo, mechanistically by facilitating β-catenin accumulation and PD-L1 transcription through the Wnt signaling pathway. Elevated SPTSSA expression was associated with reduced CD8+ T cell infiltration, increased M2 macrophage infiltration, and increased PD-L1 expression in patient tumors. SPTSSA protein was markedly elevated in GC tissues and peripheral venous blood compared to controls.

citation: SPTSSA Is a Prognostic Marker for Glioblastoma Associated with Tumor-Infiltrating Immune Cells and Oxidative Stress (PMID: 36062185)
summary: SPTSSA expression was significantly upregulated in diffuse glioma compared to normal brain tissues and was associated with poor survival in GEPIA and CGGA databases. GSEA identified enrichment of SPTSSA-associated genes in oxidative stress-related GO terms. SPTSSA expression was significantly correlated with tumor-infiltrating immune cell populations as assessed by CIBERSORT, TIMER, and confirmed by IHC/IF.

citation: SPTSSA in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Prognostic Significance and Implications for Gene- and Cell-Based Therapy (PMID: 42051093)
summary: SPTSSA expression was significantly higher in HNSCC tissues than in non-tumoral tissues, and overexpression of SPTSSA in HNSCC cell lines enhanced cell proliferation in vitro, supporting a pro-tumorigenic function. In tumor tissues, SPTSSA protein expression correlated with CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and CD56+ NK cells, indicating immune remodeling in the TME. Elevated circulating SPTSSA protein in patient blood was proposed as a non-invasive diagnostic biomarker.

citation: Decreased SPTLC1 expression predicts worse outcomes in ccRCC patients (PMID: 31512789)
summary: Bioinformatics co-expression analysis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma identified SPTSSA as one of 10 genes significantly co-regulated with SPTLC1, placing SPTSSA within the sphingomyelin metabolism network. SPTSSA was identified alongside SPTLC2, SPTLC3, SPTSSB, and ORMDL1-3 as part of the serine palmitoyltransferase complex gene network relevant to cancer biology. This supports SPTSSA's membership in the sphingolipid biosynthesis pathway with potential roles in cancer progression.

citation: Development and Validation of Ischemic Events Related Signature After Carotid Endarterectomy (PMID: 35372347)
summary: SPTSSA was identified as one of eight genes in a predictive model for ischemic events after carotid endarterectomy, derived from weighted gene co-expression network analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The eight-gene model including SPTSSA achieved ROC-AUCs of 0.891 (train), 0.826 (validation), and 0.792 (independent cohort). High-risk patients defined by this model showed enhanced immune signatures, suggesting SPTSSA's expression in peripheral immune cells may be relevant to vascular disease outcomes.

diagnostic_reason: De novo dominant mutation identified by whole-exome sequencing; functional studies in zebrafish models and patient cell lines showed aberrant MEK/ERK signaling and disruption of F-actin polymerization

phenotype: Bleeding defect due to defective platelet function; Reduced platelet aggregation in response to GPCR-linked and GPCR-independent agonists; Decreased activation of integrin alphaIIbbeta3; Impaired signaling downstream from integrin alphaIIbbeta3; Protection from arterial thrombosis in vivo

citation: Dapagliflozin activates the RAP1B/NRF2/GPX4 signaling and promotes mitochondrial biogenesis to alleviate vascular endothelial ferroptosis. (PMID: 40280228)
phenotype: Blocked inhibitory effects of dapagliflozin on atherosclerotic plaque formation in Apoe-/-;Rap1b-/- double-knockout mice; Blocked inhibitory effects of dapagliflozin on ferroptosis activation; Impaired dapagliflozin-mediated upregulation of GPX4 and mitochondrial biogenesis factors

citation: Somatic RAP1B gain-of-function variant underlies isolated thrombocytopenia and immunodeficiency. (PMID: 39225097)
summary: RAP1B acts as a molecular switch regulating cell signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, cell trafficking, and integrin activation in platelets and lymphocytes. Gain-of-function variants G12E, G12V, and G60R increased RAP1B activation, talin recruitment, and integrin activation, modifying platelet activation, T cell proliferation, and migration. A somatic heterozygous de novo G12E variant caused neonatal thrombocytopenia, combined immunodeficiency, neutropenia, and monocytopenia, fully reversed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

citation: Dapagliflozin activates the RAP1B/NRF2/GPX4 signaling and promotes mitochondrial biogenesis to alleviate vascular endothelial ferroptosis. (PMID: 40280228)
sample_size: HUVECs in vitro; Apoe-/-;Rap1b-/- mouse model
summary: RAP1B upregulates NRF2 and promotes its nuclear translocation, activating the xCT/GPX4 signaling pathway to inhibit lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis in vascular endothelial cells. Dapagliflozin upregulates RAP1B (identified by RNA sequencing), and RAP1B also mediates mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation. In vivo, Apoe-/-;Rap1b-/- double-knockout mice showed that Rap1b knockout blocked dapagliflozin's inhibitory effects on atherosclerotic plaque formation and ferroptosis.

citation: Hepatocyte-specific RAP1B deficiency ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity and liver inflammation in mice. (PMID: 40083059)
sample_size: LKO and OE mice fed HFD for 18 weeks; RAP1B-knockdown AML12 cells
summary: Liver-specific RAP1B knockout (LKO) mice on a high-fat diet showed reduced body weight, fat mass, hepatic lipid accumulation, macrophage infiltration, and oxidative stress, with downregulation of MAPK(p38) and NF-κB signaling. Conversely, RAP1B overexpression (OE) mice showed increased liver weight, aggravated lipid accumulation, worsened insulin resistance, and elevated inflammation. RAP1B-knockdown AML12 hepatocytes were used for in vitro validation, and transcriptome/metabolome analyses identified key metabolic shifts.

citation: Targeting Rap1b signaling cascades with CDNF: Mitigating platelet activation, plasma oxylipins and reperfusion injury in stroke. (PMID: 39256999)
sample_size: Rat ischemic stroke model; hemorrhagic stroke patient platelets
summary: CDNF (cerebral dopamine neurotrophic factor) acts as an endogenous antagonist that interferes with GTP binding to Rap1b, reducing Rap1b activation and downregulating the Rap1b-MAPK-PLA2 signaling pathway, which decreases thromboxane A2 release and platelet aggregation. Subcutaneous CDNF administration in a rat ischemic stroke model significantly reduced platelet activation, aggregation, lipid mediator production, infarct volume, and neurological deficits. Studies used platelets from hemorrhagic stroke patients and animal models.

citation: Host Cell Rap1b mediates cAMP-dependent invasion by Trypanosoma cruzi. (PMID: 36897926)
summary: Pull-down experiments detecting active Rap1b-GTP and infection assays using cells transfected with constitutively active Rap1b-G12V demonstrated that Rap1b mediates cAMP/Epac-dependent host cell invasion by Trypanosoma cruzi. Fluorescence microscopy showed relocalization of Rap1b to the parasite entry site during infection. PKA-dependent phosphorylation of Rap1b had an antagonistic effect on invasion, and MEK/ERK signaling was identified downstream of cAMP/Epac/Rap1b.

citation: Myeloperoxidase-anchored ENO1 mediates neutrophil extracellular trap DNA to enhance Treg differentiation via IFITM2 during sepsis. (PMID: 40892462)
sample_size: Mouse sepsis model; CD4+ T cell experiments
summary: IFITM2 acts as a DNA receptor that senses NET-DNA and activates intracellular RAP1B and its downstream ERK signaling pathway to promote Treg differentiation and function in CD4+ T cells during sepsis. ENO1 inhibition significantly attenuated NET-induced Treg differentiation and alleviated sepsis in mice. The IFITM2-RAP1B-ERK axis was identified as a key regulatory mechanism for sepsis-induced immunosuppression.

citation: Fibronectin 1 Aggravates Colon Cancer Metastasis by Regulating RAP1B Protein Stability Through Akt/CREB Signalling Pathway. (PMID: 40638546)
sample_size: In vitro colon cancer cell lines; nude mouse xenograft model
summary: FN1 interacts with RAP1B and suppresses the interaction between RAP1B and the E3 ligase PARK2, relieving RAP1B ubiquitination and improving RAP1B protein stability. FN1-RAP1B activates the Akt signaling pathway, leading to CREB phosphorylation and activation, which in turn transcriptionally upregulates FN1 and TIMP1, forming a positive feedback loop promoting colon cancer metastasis. FN1 promoted liver and lung metastasis of colon cancer in nude mice through RAP1B.

citation: A novel DCSTAMP antagonist impedes preosteoclast fusion via modulation of RAP1B-RAC1-mediated cytoskeletal remodeling. (PMID: 41423555)
sample_size: In vitro osteoclast cultures; ovariectomy mouse model
summary: A previously uncharacterized DCSTAMP signaling cascade involving direct DCSTAMP-RAP1B interaction was identified, which activates RAP1-RAC1 signaling-dependent cytoskeletal reorganization during osteoclastogenesis. A novel small molecule E8431 inhibits the DCSTAMP-RAP1B molecular interface, impeding preosteoclast fusion and bone resorption. E8431 administration attenuated ovariectomy-induced bone loss in murine models.

citation: ICP4-Associated Activation of Rap1b Facilitates Herpes Simplex Virus Type I (HSV-1) Infection in Human Corneal Epithelial Cells. (PMID: 37515145)
summary: HSV-1 immediate early gene ICP4 inhibits PKA phosphorylation to induce Rap1b activation, which promotes viral infection through cytoskeletal rearrangement mediated by CDC42 and RAC1 in human corneal epithelial cells. siRNA knockdown of Rap1b showed a dose-dependent decrease in viral infection levels, and Rap1b activation and membrane enrichment were observed from early stages of HSV-1 infection. PKA agonist Forskolin disturbed Rap1b activation and decreased viral infection in a dose-dependent manner.

citation: Sonic hedgehog-heat shock protein 90β axis promotes the development of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis in mice. (PMID: 38342927)
sample_size: NASH mouse model; NASH patient serum samples
summary: miR-28-5p, enriched in exosomes secreted by hepatocytes under the SHH-HSP90β axis, directly targets and decreases Rap1b levels in macrophages, which in turn promotes NF-κB transcriptional activity and stimulates expression of inflammatory factors. Delivery of miR-28-5p to macrophages in mouse liver impaired NASH symptomatic development, and miR-28-5p was markedly elevated in NASH patient sera. This identifies Rap1b as a downstream effector in the SHH-HSP90β-miR-28-5p axis regulating hepatic inflammation.

diagnostic_reason: Truncating mutation segregating with syndromic and nonsyndromic intellectual disability in the same family; autosomal recessive inheritance; functional studies in mouse model (jc/jc) supporting pathogenicity

citation: Sobp modulates the transcriptional activation of Six1 target genes and is required during craniofacial development. (PMID: 34414417)
summary: Co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence experiments demonstrate that Sobp binds to and colocalizes with Six1 in the cell nucleus. Luciferase assays show that Sobp interferes with the transcriptional activation of Six1+Eya1 target genes, indicating Sobp acts as a modulator of Six1 transcriptional activity. Sobp is thus identified as a potential co-factor in the Six1/Eya1 pathway relevant to Branchio-oto-renal syndrome.

citation: Sobp modulates the transcriptional activation of Six1 target genes and is required during craniofacial development. (PMID: 34414417)
summary: In Xenopus embryos, knockdown or overexpression of Sobp disrupts formation of ectodermal domains at neural plate stages, impairs otic vesicle development, and causes craniofacial cartilage defects. Expression of a Xenopus Sobp construct carrying a human disease variant disrupts the pre-placodal ectoderm similarly to full-length Sobp but with distinct additional changes. These results establish Sobp as required for vertebrate craniofacial development and as a candidate gene for Branchio-oto-renal syndrome.

citation: SOBP is mutated in syndromic and nonsyndromic intellectual disability and is highly expressed in the brain limbic system. (PMID: 21035105)
summary: In situ RNA expression studies in postnatal mouse brain showed strong SOBP expression in the limbic system during the period of active synaptogenesis, a pattern unusual among genes mutated in intellectual disability. SOBP encodes a nuclear zinc finger protein, and its expression in limbic circuits suggests a role in learning, memory, and affective behavior.

citation: SOBP is mutated in syndromic and nonsyndromic intellectual disability and is highly expressed in the brain limbic system. (PMID: 21035105)
summary: A truncating mutation in SOBP was identified as the cause of both syndromic (MRAMS syndrome with anterior maxillary protrusion and strabismus) and nonsyndromic intellectual disability with psychosis in the same family. Proteomic comparison of +/jc versus jc/jc mouse brains identified 24 proteins with >1.5-fold expression differences, including dynamin and pacsin1, implicating SOBP in neuronal protein networks. One patient also exhibited subclinical cochlear hearing loss, consistent with SOBP's known role in cochlear development.

citation: Jxc1/Sobp, encoding a nuclear zinc finger protein, is critical for cochlear growth, cell fate, and patterning of the organ of corti. (PMID: 18579736)
summary: The mouse Jxc1/Sobp gene encodes a nuclear protein with two FCS-type zinc finger domains and nuclear localization signals; wild-type protein localizes to the nucleus while mutant isoforms are mislocalized to the cytoplasm. In jc (Jackson circler) mutant mice, cochlear duct growth arrests at E13.5, and the organ of Corti shows supernumerary hair cells, mirror-image duplications, and ectopic vestibular-like hair cells. These findings establish Jxc1/Sobp as critical for cochlear growth, cell fate determination, and patterning of the organ of Corti.

citation: Jxc1/Sobp, encoding a nuclear zinc finger protein, is critical for cochlear growth, cell fate, and patterning of the organ of corti. (PMID: 18579736)
summary: Jxc1/Sobp mRNA was detected in inner ear sensory hair cells, supporting cells, and acoustic ganglia in mice. Expression was also found in the developing retina, olfactory epithelium, trigeminal ganglion, and hair follicles, indicating broad expression in sensory organs during development.

citation: Recurrent intragenic exon rearrangements of SOBP and AUTS2 in non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma. (PMID: 31686349)
summary: Intragenic exon rearrangements (IERs) involving SOBP exons 2 and 3 (at chromosomal locus 6q21) were identified as tumor-specific molecular lesions in non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma (B-NHL). These SOBP IERs were frequently detected across multiple B-NHL samples, suggesting they may contribute to tumorigenesis and serve as potential genetic biomarkers for B-NHL.

citation: Identification of MEG8/miR-378d/SOBP axis as a novel regulatory network and associated with immune infiltrates in ovarian carcinoma by integrated bioinformatics analysis. (PMID: 33742531)
summary: Integrated bioinformatics analysis of ovarian cancer datasets identified lower SOBP expression as an independent prognostic factor for inferior prognosis. Downregulation of SOBP was associated with enhanced infiltration of B cells, CD8+ T cells, macrophages, neutrophils, and dendritic cells, and GSEA linked low SOBP to activation of immune-related pathways. A novel MEG8/miR-378d/SOBP regulatory axis was proposed, whereby this lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network affects ovarian cancer progression through cytokine pathway regulation.

citation: Chicken sine oculis binding protein homolog (sobp), a novel gene that may regulate feather development. (PMID: 22802190)
summary: In chickens, sobp mRNA (~5 kb) and SOBP protein (~96 kDa) are expressed in many tissues and continuously throughout embryonic development. Expression is higher in the dorsal skin and feather follicle of White Leghorn compared to Chinese Silky chickens, suggesting sobp may regulate distinct feather type development.

citation: Zmym2 Alters Expression of Key Craniofacial Genes. (PMID: 40448369)
summary: Zmym2 was identified based on sequence similarity to domains found in Sobp (sine oculis-binding protein), a bona fide Six1 co-factor. Unlike Sobp, Zmym2 did not co-immunoprecipitate with Six1 and did not affect Six1+Eya1 transcriptional activity in cultured cells, but overexpression in Xenopus embryos indirectly antagonized Six1 function during cranial placode development. This study contextualizes Sobp's unique role as a genuine Six1 interactor by contrast with the non-interacting Zmym2.

phenotype: Neural tube defects; Impaired ciliogenesis; Failure to adequately methylate septin2; Disrupted GTP binding activity of septin2; Disrupted formation of septin2-6-7 complex; Compromised neural tube closure

citation: S-Nitrosylation of Septin2 Exacerbates Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection by Coupling the TIAM1-RAC1 Axis in Macrophages (PMID: 38357802)
summary: S-nitrosylation of Septin2 at Cys111 in macrophages reduces its interaction with TIAM1, activating the TIAM1-RAC1 axis and downstream NF-κB signaling, leading to vascular inflammation and extracellular matrix degradation in aortic aneurysm and dissection. This was demonstrated in both human aortic dissection tissue and Apoe-/- mice infused with angiotensin II. Pharmacological blockade of RAC1 with R-Ketorolac or NSC23766 protected against disease progression.

citation: SEPTIN2 suppresses an IFN-γ-independent, proinflammatory macrophage activation pathway (PMID: 37978190)
summary: SEPTIN2 acts as a negative regulator of IFN-γ-independent macrophage autoactivation, identified by high-content screening. Mechanistically, ER stress induces SEPT2 expression, which balances acetylation versus ubiquitination of HSP5 at Lysine 327, alleviating ER stress and constraining M1-like polarization and proinflammatory cytokine release. Loss of this negative feedback leads to unfolded protein accumulation, excessive inflammation, and tissue damage.

citation: Septin2 mediates podosome maturation and endothelial cell invasion associated with angiogenesis (PMID: 31865373)
summary: Septin2 (along with Septin6 and Septin7) is required for maturation of nascent endothelial podosomes into matrix-degrading organelles. Septin2 localizes around the perimeter of podosomes near the basolateral plasma membrane, and its phosphoinositide-binding residues are required for podosome function. Septin2-mediated podosome regulation is critical for endothelial cell invasion during angiogenesis, making it a potential anti-angiogenesis target.

citation: Folate-dependent methylation of septins governs ciliogenesis during neural tube closure (PMID: 28432198)
summary: Methylation of septin2 is required for normal ciliogenesis and neural tube closure in animal models and cultured mammalian cells. Embryos with neural tube defects failed to adequately methylate septin2, and this methylation affects septin2's GTP binding activity and formation of the septin2-6-7 complex. Folic acid promotes normal neural tube closure partly by regulating septin2 methylation.

citation: Hypoxia exposure impairs male fertility via inhibiting Septin2-mediated spermatogonial proliferation (PMID: 40487848)
sample_size: 24 high-altitude residents, 6 pathological hypoxia patients, 19 healthy controls; mouse model n=5
summary: Hypoxia downregulates Sept2 transcription in spermatogonia by interfering with POLR2A binding to the Sept2 promoter, leading to stabilization of the PP2A B56γ regulatory subunit, enhanced AKT dephosphorylation, G1-S phase arrest, and impaired spermatogonial proliferation. Sept2 knockdown in normoxic mice phenocopied hypoxia-induced spermatogenesis defects, while Sept2 overexpression mitigated hypoxia-related proliferative defects. PP2A inhibitor okadaic acid restored reproductive competence in hypoxic mice.

citation: Septin2 regulates ARHGAP25-mediated suppression of lamellipodia formation and cell spreading (PMID: 40205813)
summary: Septin2 was identified as an interacting protein of ARHGAP25 (a GTPase-activating protein for Rac) in mammalian cells, with both proteins colocalizing at lamellipodia. Depletion of septin2 restored lamellipodia formation and cell spreading suppressed by ARHGAP25 overexpression, while forced septin2 expression enhanced ARHGAP25-mediated suppression. These results indicate septin2 controls cell morphology by modulating ARHGAP25 function.

citation: Repression of Septin9 and Septin2 suppresses tumor growth of human glioblastoma cells (PMID: 29724999)
summary: SEPT2 expression is elevated in glioma tissues and cell lines (A172, U87-MG), and knockdown of SEPT2 together with SEPT9 synergistically inhibits GBM cell proliferation, arrests cell cycle in S phase, decreases invasive capability, and impairs glioma xenograft growth in nude mice. The growth suppression involves two parallel signaling pathways: the p53/p21 axis and MEK/ERK activation. These findings were identified through integrated multi-omics analysis across transcriptomic and proteomic studies.

citation: Functional interdependence between septin and actin cytoskeleton (PMID: 15541171)
summary: Septin2 partially co-localizes with actin bundles in mammalian interphase cells, and its filament morphology depends on an intact actin cytoskeleton. FRAP experiments showed that all Septin2 assemblies are highly dynamic with constant exchange, independent of actin. RNAi and truncated Septin2 expression experiments demonstrated that Septin2 plays a significant role in stabilizing actin bundles and preventing actin turnover.

citation: Septin2 is modified by SUMOylation and required for chromosome congression in mouse oocytes (PMID: 20372094)
summary: Septin2 is modified by SUMO-1 in mouse oocytes and localizes along the entire spindle at metaphase and at the midbody during cytokinesis. Disruption of septin function with an inhibitor or siRNA caused failure of the metaphase I/anaphase I transition and chromosome misalignment, activating the spindle assembly checkpoint (BubR1 labeling). These results demonstrate septin2 plays an important role in chromosome congression and meiotic cell cycle progression in mouse oocytes.

citation: Association of Predicted Expression and Multimodel Association Analysis of Substance Abuse Traits (PMID: 36407771)
summary: SEPTIN2 was identified as one of 15 significant associations between predicted gene expression and addiction traits (family alcoholism, cannabis craving, alcohol, nicotine, and cannabis dependence) using a combined PrediXcan burden test and cross-phenotype association (CPASSOC) multimodel meta-analysis aggregated across 10 brain tissues. The study used low-pass whole genome sequencing in 1,640 participants from the UCSF Family Alcoholism Study. SEPTIN2 had prior associations with similar phenotypes in the GWAS Atlas.

citation: Identification of a novel human zinc finger gene, ZNF438, with transcription inhibition activity (PMID: 17669267)
summary: ZNF438 encodes a C2H2-type zinc finger protein of 828 amino acids with five zinc finger domains, mapped to human chromosome 10p11.2. Immunofluorescence showed exogenous Flag-tagged ZNF438 localizes to the nucleus of COS-7 cells. Dual luciferase assays demonstrated that ZNF438 functions as a transcriptional repressor.

citation: Identification of a novel human zinc finger gene, ZNF438, with transcription inhibition activity (PMID: 17669267)
summary: RT-PCR analysis of 18 human adult tissues showed that ZNF438 is ubiquitously expressed across all tissues examined, indicating broad expression without tissue-specific restriction.

citation: Study of FN1 and ZNF438 gene expression negatively regulated by androgen receptor in androgen-independent LNCaP cells (PMID: 27122218)
summary: ChIP-PCR in androgen-independent LNCaP-AI cells showed significant AR enrichment at the ZNF438 gene locus (6.843±0.078 vs. 1.000±0.014 in IgG control). DHT stimulation reduced ZNF438 mRNA and protein expression, while AR knockdown via lentivirus increased ZNF438 expression, establishing ZNF438 as a negatively regulated AR target gene in castration-resistant prostate cancer cells.

citation: Comprehensive Analysis of a Zinc Finger Protein Gene-Based Signature with Regard to Prognosis and Tumor Immune Microenvironment in Osteosarcoma (PMID: 35281811)
summary: ZNF438 was identified as one of seven prognosis-related ZNF genes in osteosarcoma; lower expression of ZNF438 was associated with high-risk classification and worse overall survival. The prognostic signature including ZNF438 was significantly associated with immune-related biological processes and differences in immune cell subpopulations (CD8+ T cells, neutrophils, Th1 cells, TILs) between risk groups.

citation: Investigating the shared genetic structure between rheumatoid arthritis and stroke (PMID: 39953635)
sample_size: 8,255 RA cases / 409,001 controls; 43,132 stroke cases / 43,132 controls
summary: Multi-trait GWAS analysis identified ZNF438 as one of five common risk genes shared between rheumatoid arthritis and stroke (alongside IRF5, RNASET2, UBE2LS, and SYNGR1). These shared genes are implicated in the immune-inflammatory pathway, and the RA-stroke genetic correlation was 0.3756 genome-wide.

citation: Type 1 Diabetes and Multiple Sclerosis Share General Autoimmunity Genetic Variation (PMID: 42194988)
sample_size: 18,942 T1D cases / 501,638 controls; 14,802 MS cases / 26,703 controls
summary: Bayesian colocalization analysis identified a shared genetic locus at ZNF438/ZEB1 as one of 26 colocalizing signals between type 1 diabetes and multiple sclerosis, representing a novel locus for T1D. This locus was classified among the general autoimmune susceptibility signals shared between the two diseases.

citation: Genome-wide DNA methylation investigation of glucocorticoid exposure within buccal samples (PMID: 30821055)
summary: A genome-wide significant differentially methylated CpG site was identified in or nearest to ZNF438 following high-dose dexamethasone (10 mg) administration in dental surgery patients, with DNAm change >10%. This finding suggests ZNF438 methylation is responsive to synthetic glucocorticoid exposure in buccal tissue.

citation: DNA methylation and cardiovascular disease in humans: a systematic review and database of known CpG methylation sites (PMID: 36991458)
summary: The CpG site cg01656216, located near ZNF438, was one of only two CpG sites referenced in 6 or more publications in a systematic review of DNA methylation and cardiovascular disease, associating ZNF438 methylation with vascular disease and epigenetic age. This makes ZNF438 one of the most consistently reported methylation loci in CVD research.

citation: Spatial Organization of Chromatin of ZEB1 Gene Promoter Region in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Cells (PMID: 41391024)
summary: 4C-seq chromatin conformation analysis in PDAC cell lines suggested that ZNF438 is a candidate transcriptional repressor of the ZEB1 gene, based on its known repressor activity and properties consistent with the observed chromatin contact patterns at the ZEB1 regulatory region. ZNF438 was proposed as a regulator of ZEB1 expression, a key driver of epithelial-mesenchymal transition in pancreatic cancer.

citation: Constructing a 10-core genes panel for diagnosis of pediatric sepsis (PMID: 33274532)
summary: WGCNA co-expression analysis of pediatric sepsis gene expression datasets identified ZNF438 among the top 20 hub genes in the blue module, which was significantly correlated with pediatric sepsis. Genes in this module were primarily enriched in neutrophil degranulation pathways, suggesting ZNF438 is aberrantly expressed in pediatric sepsis in an immune/inflammatory context.

citation: Cardiac ryanodine receptor calcium release deficiency syndrome (PMID: 33536282)
sample_size: Six families with linkage analysis; LOD score 11.479
summary: RyR2 loss-of-function (LOF) mutations were shown to cause a novel disease entity termed Ca2+ release deficiency syndrome (CRDS), distinct from CPVT. A RyR2 LOF mouse model exhibited cardiac electrophysiological remodeling and increased propensity for early afterdepolarizations, and a long-burst, long-pause, short-coupled pacing protocol reliably induced ventricular arrhythmias in both mice and humans with RyR2 LOF mutations. Treatment with quinidine and flecainide abolished induced arrhythmias in model mice.

citation: Heart failure-induced cognitive dysfunction is mediated by intracellular Ca2+ leak through ryanodine receptor type 2 (PMID: 37429912)
summary: RyR2 intracellular Ca2+ release channels were found to be expressed in hippocampal neurons of both humans and mice with heart failure, where they undergo post-translational modifications (PKA phosphorylation, oxidation, nitrosylation, calstabin2 depletion) leading to Ca2+ leak. Genetically engineered mice resistant to RyR2 Ca2+ leak (RyR2-p.Ser2808Ala) were protected against heart failure-induced cognitive dysfunction, demonstrating a role for RyR2 beyond cardiac muscle in neuronal function.

citation: Hippo-Yap Signaling Maintains Sinoatrial Node Homeostasis (PMID: 36317529)
summary: CUT&RUN sequencing data showed that the Hippo-Yap pathway effector Yap directly regulates Ryr2 expression in sinoatrial node (SAN) pacemaker cells. Lats1/2 conditional knockout mice showed decreased Ryr2 expression and dysregulated calcium handling in the SAN, linking RYR2 to the Hippo-Yap signaling pathway in cardiac pacemaker homeostasis.

citation: Astrocyte-derived SerpinA3N promotes neuroinflammation and epileptic seizures by activating the NF-κB signaling pathway in mice with temporal lobe epilepsy (PMID: 37422673)
summary: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that SerpinA3N physically interacts with RYR2 in the hippocampus of mice with kainic acid-induced temporal lobe epilepsy. SerpinA3N promotes RYR2 phosphorylation, suggesting a novel regulatory mechanism of RYR2 in neuroinflammation and seizure pathology.

citation: Ero1α-Dependent ERp44 Dissociation From RyR2 Contributes to Cardiac Arrhythmia (PMID: 35086342)
summary: ERp44 (endoplasmic reticulum protein 44) was identified as an intraluminal binding partner of RyR2, interacting via cysteine 4806 in a redox-sensitive manner. In a rat model of cardiac hypertrophy, Ero1α-mediated oxidation caused ERp44 dissociation from RyR2, increasing spontaneous Ca2+ release and arrhythmias; pharmacological Ero1α inhibition restored ERp44-RyR2 association and reduced arrhythmias.

citation: Foxp3-mediated blockage of ryanodine receptor 2 underlies contact-based suppression by regulatory T cells (PMID: 38099494)
summary: Foxp3 was shown to block transcription of RYR2 in regulatory T cells (Tregs), reducing basal Ca2+ oscillations and m-calpain activity, which prolongs DC engagement and suppresses antigen presentation. RYR2-deficient CD4+ T cells phenocopied Foxp3+ Tregs in multiple immune models (viral infection, asthma, colitis, tumor), and rescued systemic autoimmunity in scurfy mice lacking Foxp3, establishing RYR2-mediated Ca2+ signaling as a central effector mechanism of Treg immune suppression.

citation: The biophysical properties of TRIC-A and TRIC-B and their interactions with RyR2 (PMID: 37756589)
summary: Co-expression of mouse TRIC-A or TRIC-B with mouse RyR2 in HEK293 cells and subsequent bilayer electrophysiology demonstrated that both TRIC isoforms alter RyR2 gating behavior and its response to cytosolic Ca2+, with TRIC-A showing a greater ability to stimulate RyR2 opening. This indicates that TRIC channels directly and complementarily regulate RyR2 gating in addition to providing counter-ion currents.

citation: CPVT1 point mutations in RyR2 S5 and S6 segments and their Ca2+ signaling consequence (PMID: 40974955)
summary: Using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, two CPVT-associated RyR2 mutations (R4822H in the S5-S6 luminal loop and L4865V on S6) were introduced and studied by TIRF imaging. R4822H completely suppressed Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release (CICR) and ICa-triggered SR Ca2+ release, while L4865V did not suppress E-C coupling but showed spontaneous Ca2+ transients, demonstrating divergent phenotypes despite both mutations being in transmembrane segments.

citation: Dantrolene rescues aberrant N-terminus intersubunit interactions in mutant pro-arrhythmic cardiac ryanodine receptors (PMID: 25411383)
summary: The arrhythmia-associated RyR2 L433P mutation was shown by yeast two-hybrid, co-immunoprecipitation, chemical cross-linking, and sucrose density gradient centrifugation to disrupt N-terminal self-association and impair tetramerization of the full-length channel. Dantrolene treatment restored normal N-terminal intersubunit interactions and channel function, identifying the N-terminus as a critical structural determinant for RyR2 oligomerization and a therapeutic target.

summary: Whole-exome sequencing of 234 unexplained cardiac arrest (UCA) survivors identified a significant enrichment of rare missense RYR2 variants compared to gnomAD controls (combined allele frequency 4.1% vs. 2.0%). This supports RYR2 as a major genetic contributor to unexplained ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest in the absence of overt structural disease.

phenotype: Significant increase in vitreous chamber depth; Altered lens diameter; High myopia-like ocular morphology; Preserved physiological retinal function (ERG normal under high-myopia conditions)

citation: G9a and ZNF644 Physically Associate to Suppress Progenitor Gene Expression during Neurogenesis (PMID: 27546533)
summary: ZNF644 was identified as a G9a/GLP-interacting protein via unbiased affinity purification and mass spectrometry. In zebrafish, znf644a and znf644b orthologs play complementary roles in regulating G9a/H3K9me2-mediated gene silencing during neurogenesis, with non-overlapping requirements during retinal differentiation. ZNF644 is described as a critical co-regulator of G9a/GLP histone methyltransferase activity during neuronal differentiation.

citation: The zinc finger proteins ZNF644 and WIZ regulate the G9a/GLP complex for gene repression (PMID: 25789554)
summary: ZNF644 was identified as a core subunit of the G9a/GLP histone methyltransferase complex through unbiased protein affinity purification. ZNF644 interacts with the transcription activation domain of G9a and contains multiple zinc finger motifs that recognize consensus DNA sequences, targeting G9a to chromatin to mediate H3K9 methylation and gene repression. This study establishes ZNF644 as a key chromatin-targeting subunit of the G9a/GLP complex.

citation: Myopia disease mouse models: a missense point mutation (S673G) and a protein-truncating mutation of the Zfp644 mimic human disease phenotype (PMID: 30834109)
summary: Using TALEN technology, two mouse models were generated carrying either the disease-associated missense mutation Zfp644 S673G or a truncated form (Zfp644 Δ8). Both mutants showed significant differences in vitreous chamber depth and lens diameter consistent with high myopia, while retinal physiological function was preserved. These models confirm that ZNF644/Zfp644 mutations are causative for ocular changes associated with high myopia.

citation: miR-362 regulates the proliferation and apoptosis of porcine immature Sertoli cells through targeting the ZNF644 gene (PMID: 30021720)
summary: miR-362 was shown to directly target the 3'UTR of ZNF644 in porcine immature Sertoli cells, suppressing its expression as confirmed by dual luciferase reporter assay. Overexpression of miR-362 or knockdown of ZNF644 arrested cells in G1 and G2 phases, inhibited proliferation, and enhanced apoptosis. These results indicate ZNF644 plays a role in Sertoli cell survival and cell cycle progression during spermatogenesis.

citation: A Massively Parallel Screen of 5'UTR Mutations Identifies Variants Impacting Translation and Protein Production in Neurodevelopmental Disorder Genes (PMID: 37961498)
summary: A high-throughput assay screening 5'UTR patient mutations identified variants in ZNF644 that specifically alter translational activity in neurons in vivo. Patient-derived cell line studies confirmed that these 5'UTR mutations can alter ZNF644 protein production in individuals with autism. This implicates ZNF644 as a gene whose dysregulation via 5'UTR mutations may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders.

citation: Study of a US cohort supports the role of ZNF644 and high-grade myopia susceptibility (PMID: 22539872)
summary: Sanger sequencing of ZNF644 coding regions in 131 high-grade myopia cases identified two novel variants (c.725C>T, c.821A>T) not found in 672 ethnically matched controls. A rare variant (rs12117237) was present in 6 cases and 5 controls. The study supports a role for ZNF644 variants in myopia susceptibility in a US cohort including Caucasian and African American individuals.

citation: CD4 T-cell transcriptome analysis reveals aberrant regulation of STAT3 and Wnt signaling pathways in rheumatoid arthritis: evidence from a case-control study (PMID: 25880754)
summary: Whole-genome transcriptome profiling of CD4 T cells from 53 RA patients and 45 healthy controls identified ZNF644 as one of several differentially expressed zinc finger transcription factors confirmed in a validation cohort. ZNF644 expression was aberrant in RA patient CD4 T cells, suggesting it may be a potential pathogenic factor in rheumatoid arthritis. The study highlights ZNF644 alongside ZEB1 and ZNF292 as dysregulated zinc finger transcription factors in RA.

citation: Gene expression differences in PTSD are uniquely related to the intrusion symptom cluster: A transcriptome-wide analysis in military service members (PMID: 31039430)
sample_size: 39 PTSD participants, 22 with high intrusion symptoms
summary: Transcriptome-wide analysis of peripheral blood in military service members identified ZNF644 as one of 10 genes upregulated in participants with PTSD and high intrusion symptoms at baseline and downregulated following successful sleep-based treatment. ZNF644 upregulation was specifically associated with the intrusion symptom cluster rather than other PTSD symptom clusters. This positions ZNF644 as a potential molecular biomarker for PTSD intrusion symptoms and treatment response.

citation: Developing ZNF Gene Signatures Predicting Radiosensitivity of Patients with Breast Cancer (PMID: 34504527)
summary: Analysis of 976 breast cancer samples from TCGA revealed that high expression of ZNF644 was associated with radiosensitivity in breast cancer patients. A 4-gene ZNF signature including ZNF644 (high expression) and three other ZNF genes (low expression) predicted better overall survival following radiotherapy, validated in the METABRIC database. ZNF644 is proposed as a component of a radiosensitivity gene signature for breast cancer.

citation: The expanding role of the Ehmt2/G9a complex in neurodevelopment (PMID: 28596979)
summary: This review highlights ZNF644 as a recently characterized context-dependent binding partner of the Ehmt1/2 (G9a/GLP) complex that coordinates its activity during early neurodevelopment. ZNF644 is discussed as part of the mechanism by which the G9a/GLP complex achieves tissue- and temporal-specific H3K9 methylation and gene repression. The review frames ZNF644 as a key regulator of G9a/GLP function in the neurodevelopmental epigenetic landscape.

citation: CDK11 regulates pre-mRNA splicing by phosphorylation of SF3B1 (PMID: 36104565)
summary: CDK11 physically associates with SF3B1 and phosphorylates threonine residues at its N terminus during spliceosome activation. This phosphorylation is required for the association between SF3B1 and U5 and U6 snRNAs in the activated Bact spliceosome complex. Inhibition of CDK11 with OTS964 blocks this phosphorylation, preventing spliceosomal transition from the precatalytic B complex to the activated Bact complex and causing widespread intron retention.

citation: GPATCH8 modulates mutant SF3B1 mis-splicing and pathogenicity in hematologic malignancies (PMID: 38688280)
summary: Using synthetic introns responsive to mutant SF3B1, GPATCH8 was identified as a trans factor required for aberrant mutant SF3B1 splicing activity. Silencing of GPATCH8 corrected approximately one-third of mutant SF3B1-dependent splicing defects and improved dysfunctional hematopoiesis in SF3B1-mutant mice and primary human progenitors. GPATCH8 interacts with RNA helicase DHX15 and functionally opposes SUGP1, another G-patch protein implicated in SF3B1-mutant diseases.

citation: Exploring the mechanistic link between SF3B1 mutation and ring sideroblast formation in myelodysplastic syndrome (PMID: 36028755)
summary: HUDEP-2 erythroid progenitor cells stably expressing SF3B1K700E showed a higher proportion of ring sideroblasts compared to controls, demonstrating direct contribution of mutant SF3B1 to ring sideroblast formation. Mutant SF3B1 caused mis-splicing of ABCB7, leading to its downregulation along with ALAS2, and ABCB7 knockdown alone was sufficient to increase ring sideroblast frequency. RNA-seq of MDS clinical samples confirmed decreased ABCB7 expression associated with SF3B1 mutation.

citation: Vitamin B5 and succinyl-CoA improve ineffective erythropoiesis in SF3B1-mutated myelodysplasia (PMID: 36857430)
summary: SF3B1 mutations cause mis-splicing of coenzyme A synthase (COASY), leading to depletion of CoA and succinyl-CoA in MDS-RS patient cells, thereby impairing heme biosynthesis and erythropoiesis. Supplementation with vitamin B5 (COASY substrate) rescued CoA and succinyl-CoA concentrations in SF3B1-mutant cells and restored erythropoiesis differentiation in primary MDS-RS patient cells. COASY was shown to be upregulated during normal erythroid differentiation, and its silencing prevented erythroid colony formation and heme accumulation.

citation: Aberrant EVI1 splicing contributes to EVI1-rearranged leukemia (PMID: 35709354)
summary: Oncogenic SF3B1 mutations, present in >30% of inv(3)/t(3;3) myeloid neoplasm patients, promote mis-splicing of EVI1 by utilizing a cryptic branch point and aberrant 3' splice site within intron 12, generating an in-frame 6-amino-acid insertion isoform. Expression of this EVI1 splice variant enhanced hematopoietic stem cell self-renewal, and introduction of mutant SF3B1 in mice bearing the humanized inv(3)(q21q26) allele generated this novel EVI1 isoform and hastened leukemogenesis in vivo. The mutant SF3B1 spliceosome depends on an exonic splicing enhancer within EVI1 exon 13 to promote this aberrant splicing.

citation: H3B-8800, an orally available small-molecule splicing modulator, induces lethality in spliceosome-mutant cancers (PMID: 29457796)
summary: H3B-8800, an orally available modulator of the SF3b complex, potently and preferentially kills spliceosome-mutant (SF3B1, U2AF1, SRSF2) epithelial and hematologic tumor cells through direct interaction with the SF3b complex. The preferential killing of spliceosome-mutant cells is due to retention of short, GC-rich introns enriched for genes encoding spliceosome components. Drug-resistant cells bearing mutations in SF3b component-encoding genes showed loss of H3B-8800 activity, confirming on-target mechanism.

citation: Inhibition of SF3B1 improves the immune microenvironment through pyroptosis and synergizes with αPDL1 in ovarian cancer (PMID: 38012150)
summary: SF3B1 is overexpressed in ovarian cancer and is associated with low cytotoxic immune cell infiltration based on CPTAC and TCGA cohort analyses validated by tissue microarrays. Inhibition of SF3B1 with pladienolide B induces pyroptosis in ovarian cancer cells, releases mitochondrial DNA that activates macrophage M1 polarization, and increases cytotoxic immune cell infiltration in the ID8 mouse model. SF3B1 inhibition also upregulates PD-L1 expression, enhancing the antitumor effect of anti-PD-L1 therapy in combination treatment.

citation: Frequent pathway mutations of splicing machinery in myelodysplasia (PMID: 21909114)
summary: Whole-exome sequencing of 29 myelodysplasia specimens revealed that SF3B1, along with U2AF35, ZRSR2, and SRSF2, is recurrently mutated as part of the RNA splicing machinery pathway in myeloid neoplasms. Splicing pathway mutations were found in approximately 45-85% of myelodysplasia cases and were highly specific to myeloid neoplasms with dysplastic features. Most mutations, including those in SF3B1, occurred in a mutually exclusive manner and affected genes involved in 3'-splice site recognition during pre-mRNA processing, inducing abnormal RNA splicing and compromised hematopoiesis.

citation: ASHG 2014 - SF3B1 mutations in different cancer types cause recognition of sterically hindered cryptic splice-sites downstream of the branch point (C. DeBoever et al.)
summary: Analysis of transcriptome data from SF3B1-mutant CLL, uveal melanoma, and breast cancer revealed that mutant SF3B1 causes use of cryptic AG dinucleotide acceptors located 13-17 bp downstream of the branch point that are sterically hindered when SF3B1 is wild-type. Only 617 AG dinucleotides genome-wide met the specific sequence requirements for use as cryptic acceptors, and the same cryptic 3' splicing signature was observed across different cancer types only in samples with mutations in the SF3B1 HEAT 5-9 repeat hotspots. Three cancer-implicated genes (TTI1, MAP3K7, FXYD5) and four others showed cryptic acceptors consistently preferred over canonical acceptors in SF3B1-mutant CLL samples.

citation: ASHG 2013 - Functional characterization of mutations in the spliceosomal component SF3B1 in uveal melanoma (A. Bowcock et al.)
summary: Knockdown of SF3B1 in uveal melanoma cell lines from primary tumors resulted in differential regulation of several oncogenes with roles in cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and apoptosis. Transient overexpression of mutant SF3B1 forms (p.R625C, p.R625H, p.R625L, p.R625G) found in primary uveal melanomas led to upregulation of tumor-promoting transcripts including E2F3 and CLK4 (a kinase regulating splice-site recognition effectors). No overlap of differentially regulated transcripts was observed between knockdown and mutant-expressing lines, consistent with SF3B1 mutations being gain-of-function alterations.
