citation: Ferroptosis-induced SUMO2 lactylation counteracts ferroptosis by enhancing ACSL4 degradation in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 41057295)
summary: SUMO2-K11 lactylation (SUMO2-K11la) is the most prominently elevated lactylation modification in response to ferroptosis induction in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cells. SUMO2-K11la impairs the interaction between SUMO2 and ACSL4, facilitating ACSL4 degradation and thereby conferring ferroptosis resistance. A cell-penetrating peptide inhibiting SUMO2-K11la potentiated ferroptosis and sensitized LUAD to cisplatin in xenograft models.

citation: Targeting SUMO2 reverses aberrant epigenetic rewiring driven by SS18::SSX fusion oncoproteins and impairs sarcomagenesis (PMID: 40804185)
summary: CRISPR library screening identified SUMO2 as one of the strongest selective dependencies in synovial sarcoma (SySa) cells both in vitro and in vivo. SUMO2 inhibition with TAK-981 suppressed growth, reversed the SS18::SSX-driven gene expression program, and reduced chromatin occupancy of the fusion protein along with H2AK119 ubiquitination. This identifies SUMO2 as a novel, selective vulnerability in synovial sarcoma.

citation: Rbms1 promotes pulmonary fibrosis by stabilising Sumo2 mRNA to facilitate Smad4-SUMOylation and fibroblast activation (PMID: 40473311)
summary: RBMS1 binds to the Sumo2 3' untranslated region to enhance Sumo2 mRNA stability, increasing SUMO2 protein levels in lung fibroblasts following TGF-β1 stimulation. Elevated SUMO2 facilitates SUMOylation of Smad4 at lysine 158, promoting fibroblast activation and pulmonary fibrosis. Sumo2 knockdown alleviated the Rbms1-driven exacerbation of pulmonary fibrosis in mouse models.

citation: Induced proximity to PML protects TDP-43 from aggregation via SUMO-ubiquitin networks (PMID: 40246979)
summary: SUMO2 modification compartmentalizes TDP-43 in promyelocytic leukemia protein (PML) nuclear bodies and limits TDP-43 aggregation in response to proteotoxic stress. Exploiting this pathway through proximity-induced recruitment of TDP-43 to PML triggers a SUMOylation-ubiquitylation cascade that protects TDP-43 from stress-induced insolubility, mediated by ubiquitylation and the p97 disaggregase. This demonstrates a protective role for SUMO2 in preventing insoluble TDP-43 inclusions relevant to neurodegenerative disease.

citation: DHX9 SUMOylation is required for the suppression of R-loop-associated genome instability (PMID: 39019926)
summary: SUMOylation of RNA helicase DHX9 at lysine 120 is crucial for its function in resolving R-loops and maintaining genome stability. Wild-type DHX9 interacts with R-loop-associated proteins PARP1 and DDX21 via SUMO-interacting motifs, and fusion of SUMO2 to the non-SUMOylatable DHX9 K120R mutant restored these interactions, reduced R-loop accumulation, and alleviated cell survival defects. This demonstrates that SUMO2 mediates protein-protein interactions essential for R-loop homeostasis.

citation: Bone marrow stromal cells protect myeloma cells from ferroptosis through GPX4 deSUMOylation (PMID: 39653239)
summary: SUMO2 is conjugated to GPX4 at lysine 75, and SENP3-mediated de-conjugation of SUMO2 from GPX4 stabilizes the GPX4 protein, thereby consuming ROS and protecting multiple myeloma cells from ferroptosis. This mechanism was validated using SUMO2-KO mice, where loss of SUMO2 abrogated the protective effect of bone marrow stromal cells on myeloma ferroptosis resistance. The study places SUMO2 in a CD40/CD40L-SENP3-GPX4 axis regulating ferroptosis in the tumor microenvironment.

citation: LncRNA INHEG promotes glioma stem cell maintenance and tumorigenicity through regulating rRNA 2'-O-methylation (PMID: 37980347)
summary: SUMO2 E3 ligase TAF15 is induced by lncRNA INHEG to interact with and SUMOylate NOP58, a core component of the snoRNP complex that guides rRNA 2'-O-methylation. This SUMO2-mediated SUMOylation of NOP58 accelerates C/D box snoRNP assembly and enhances rRNA methylation, increasing translation of oncoproteins including EGFR, IGF1R, CDK6, and PDGFRB in glioma stem cells. This identifies SUMO2 as a regulator of ribosome biogenesis and oncogenic translation in glioblastoma.

citation: Sumoylation of methionine adenosyltransferase alpha 1 promotes mitochondrial dysfunction in alcohol-associated liver disease (PMID: 38100286)
summary: SUMO2 specifically SUMOylates MATα1 at lysine 48 (K47 in humans), depleting mitochondrial MATα1 and contributing to mitochondrial dysfunction in alcohol-associated liver disease. Mutation of MATα1 K48 prevented ethanol-induced mitochondrial membrane depolarization, MATα1 depletion, and triglyceride accumulation in primary hepatocytes and mouse models. CRISPR editing of MATα1 K48 in vivo protected mice from ethanol-induced fat accumulation, liver injury, and mitochondrial dysfunction.

citation: SUMOylation-Driven mRNA Circularization Enhances Translation and Promotes Lymphatic Metastasis of Bladder Cancer (PMID: 37991737)
summary: SUMO2 modification at lysine 108 of hnRNPA2B1 is mediated and recognized by DHCR24, fostering TBK1 mRNA circularization and eIF4F initiation complex assembly by enhancing hnRNPA2B1-eIF4G1 interaction. This SUMO2-dependent mechanism elevates TBK1 expression, activates PI3K/Akt signaling, promotes VEGFC secretion, and drives lymphangiogenesis and lymph node metastasis in bladder cancer. DHCR24 silencing significantly impeded bladder cancer lymphangiogenesis in a patient-derived xenograft model.

citation: ASHG 2022 - Maternally Inherited novel SUMO2 variant associated with a complex phenotype (D. Otohinoyi, C. Hicks, R. Zambrano)
summary: A novel maternally inherited heterozygous variant in exon 1 of SUMO2 (c.2T>A: p.Met1?) was identified by whole exome sequencing in a proband and his mother, both presenting with skeletal abnormalities including tibial agenesis, syndactyly, and clubfoot. In silico analysis and ACMG guidelines support a pathogenic classification for this variant. Animal studies showing that SUMO2 knockdown alters expression of CDX2, OCT4, and NANOG and results in embryonic lethality support the developmental importance of SUMO2.

citation: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels (PMID: 37543036)
summary: Cryo-EM structures of TMEM63B revealed a monomeric configuration with a single highly restricted pore, distinct from the homodimeric architecture of plant OSCA channels. Functional analyses confirmed TMEM63B is a bona fide mechanosensitive ion channel with small conductance and high activation thresholds. The intracellular linker IL2 mediates dimerization in OSCAs but drives monomeric assembly in TMEM63B, affecting mechanosensitivity.

citation: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration (PMID: 37421948)
summary: Six disease-associated TMEM63B variants (including recurrent p.Val44Met) were modeled in transfected Neuro2a cells, demonstrating inward leak cation currents under isotonic conditions and impaired responses to hypo-osmotic challenge, as well as disrupted Ca2+ transients. Ectopic expression of p.Val44Met and p.Gly580Cys variants in Drosophila caused early death. The study established TMEM63B-associated DEE as a clinicopathological entity with progressive neurodegeneration, early-onset epilepsy, and hematological abnormalities in 17 unrelated individuals.

citation: Mechanosensitive channels TMEM63A and TMEM63B mediate lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion (PMID: 38127458)
summary: Loss of TMEM63A/B in mice resulted in atelectasis and respiratory failure due to deficient pulmonary surfactant secretion. TMEM63A/B were predominantly localized at the limiting membrane of lamellar bodies in alveolar type 2 epithelial cells, and their activation during cell stretch facilitated surfactant and ATP release. Released ATP evoked Ca2+ signaling that potentiated further exocytic fusion of lamellar bodies.

citation: Phospholipid scrambling induced by an ion channel/metabolite transporter complex (PMID: 39217145)
summary: CRISPR sgRNA library screening identified TMEM63B as a phospholipid scrambling (PLS)-inducing factor upon Ca2+ stimulation. Biochemical screening revealed that TMEM63B forms a heterodimer with the thiamine transporter SLC19A2, and deletion of either gene decreased PLS activity. Human disease-related TMEM63B mutants induced constitutive PLS, and the Ca2+-activated K+ channel KCNN4 was identified as an additional PLS-regulating factor in this complex.

citation: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution (PMID: 39424995)
summary: TMEM63B functions as a membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase localized at the plasma membrane and lysosomes, activating bidirectional lipid translocation in response to changes in membrane curvature and thickness. TMEM63B deficiency alters phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin distributions in the plasma membrane. The disease-associated V44M substitution confers constitutive scramblase activity, disrupting plasma membrane phospholipid asymmetry; cryo-EM structures revealed open and closed conformations with a lipid translocation pathway.

citation: Expression and localization of the mechanosensitive/osmosensitive ion channel TMEM63B in the mouse urinary tract (PMID: 38724885)
summary: Using HA-tagged Tmem63b reporter mice and immunofluorescence confocal microscopy, TMEM63B protein was detected in proximal tubule epithelial cells, intercalated cells of the collecting duct, and thick ascending limb epithelial cells of the kidney. In the lower urinary tract, TMEM63B was expressed in urothelium lining the renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, and urethra, as well as in seminal vesicles, vas deferens, lateral prostate, and vaginal epithelium.

citation: A splicing-dependent ER retention signal regulates surface expression of the mechanosensitive TMEM63B cation channel (PMID: 36496074)
summary: Brain-specific alternative splicing of exon 4 in TMEM63B produces a short isoform (lacking exon 4) that is the major brain isoform and shows enhanced surface expression and stronger responses to hypoosmotic stimulation compared to the long isoform. Mutagenesis identified an RXR-type ER retention signal within exon 4 that mediates COPI retrieval, retaining the long isoform in the ER. Long and short TMEM63B isoforms can form heterodimers, with the long isoform reducing surface expression of the short isoform.

citation: Mechanical signaling through membrane tension induces somal translocation during neuronal migration (PMID: 39707024)
summary: Using the membrane tension sensor Flipper-TR and scanning ion conductance microscopy, leading process extension during neuronal migration was shown to increase plasma membrane tension, which activated Tmem63b and triggered Ca2+ influx. This Ca2+ influx led to actomyosin activation at the rear of the cell, driving somal translocation. Blockade of this Tmem63b-mediated signaling pathway inhibited neuronal migration in three-dimensional environments.

citation: The TMEM63B Channel Facilitates Intestinal Motility and Enhances Proliferation of Intestinal Stem Cells (PMID: 39513891)
summary: TMEM63B is expressed in intestinal stem cells and its deletion in these cells decelerated intestinal motility, impaired digestion, attenuated intestinal stem cell proliferation, and exacerbated DSS-induced colitis in mice. These findings identify TMEM63B as a mechanosensitive channel regulating gastrointestinal motility and intestinal stem cell homeostasis. The channel likely responds to osmotic pressure changes within the intestinal lumen.

citation: ASHG 2019 - Human and mouse essentiality screens as a resource for disease gene discovery (P. Cacheiro et al.)
sample_size: 163 developmental lethal genes screened; multiple independent disease sequencing consortia
summary: Integrating IMPC knockout mouse viability data with human intolerance-to-variation scores, TMEM63B was identified as a developmental lethal gene highly intolerant to variation. Screening of unsolved developmental disorder cases identified potentially pathogenic de novo variants in TMEM63B in multiple patients exhibiting intellectual disability and neurological/movement phenotypes partially modeled by the IMPC mouse knockout. This highlighted TMEM63B as a novel candidate gene for intellectual disability.

citation: Splicing Factor SRSF1 Promotes Pancreatitis and KRASG12D-Mediated Pancreatic Cancer (PMID: 37098965)
summary: SRSF1 is highly expressed in pancreatitis, PDAC precursor lesions, and tumors. Increased SRSF1 is sufficient to induce pancreatitis and accelerate KRASG12D-mediated PDAC by activating MAPK signaling partly through alternative-splicing-regulated upregulation of IL1R1. A negative feedback mechanism destabilizes SRSF1 protein in normal epithelial cells expressing KRASG12D, which is overcome by hyperactive MYC to facilitate tumorigenesis.

citation: Endothelial SRSF1 Promotes Ischemia-Induced Angiogenesis via ATF3-KLF2-S1PR1 Pathway (PMID: 41195527)
summary: SRSF1 expression is elevated in endothelial cells after ischemia and hypoxia. SRSF1 modulates alternative splicing of ATF3 pre-mRNA by direct binding, promoting full-length ATF3 over truncated ATF3Δzip2, which suppresses KLF2 and downstream S1PR1 signaling to enhance angiogenesis. Endothelial-specific SRSF1 knockout mice showed impaired blood flow recovery after hindlimb ischemia, while SRSF1 overexpression enhanced angiogenesis in vivo and in vitro.

citation: Targeting SRSF1 improves cancer immunotherapy by dually acting on CD8(+)T and tumor cells (PMID: 39837814)
summary: Depleting SRSF1 in CD8+ T cells improves antitumor immune function and glycolytic metabolism, enhancing adoptive T cell therapy efficacy. SRSF1 inactivation in tumor cells reduces transcription factors c-Jun, c-myc, and JunB, reprogramming glycolytic metabolism and restoring CD8+ T cell function. A small-molecule inhibitor TN2008 targeting SRSF1 boosted antitumor immune responses in mouse models.

citation: FAM120A couples SREBP-dependent transcription and splicing of lipogenesis enzymes downstream of mTORC1 (PMID: 37595559)
summary: mTORC1-activated SRPK2 phosphorylates SRSF1, enhancing its binding to FAM120A, which bridges newly transcribed lipogenic genes from RNA polymerase II to the SRSF1 and U1-70K-containing RNA-splicing machinery. This multi-protein complex promotes efficient splicing and stability of lipogenic transcripts, resulting in fatty acid synthesis and cancer cell proliferation. SRSF1 thus functions as a downstream effector of mTORC1-SRPK2 signaling in anabolic cell growth.

citation: Genomic Landscape Survey Identifies SRSF1 as a Key Oncodriver in Small Cell Lung Cancer (PMID: 27093186)
summary: SRSF1 DNA copy number gain and mRNA over-expression were strongly associated with poor survival in SCLC patients across discovery and validation cohorts of 99 Chinese patients. Functional studies in vitro and in vivo demonstrated that SRSF1 is important for tumorigenicity of SCLC and may play a key role in DNA repair and chemo-sensitivity. These results support SRSF1 as a prognostic biomarker in SCLC.

citation: SRSF1 Is Crucial for Maintaining Satellite Cell Homeostasis During Skeletal Muscle Growth and Regeneration (PMID: 39381961)
summary: SRSF1 knockout in satellite cells (via MyoD-Cre) caused early mortality and muscle atrophy in mice, with scRNA-seq revealing increased activated/proliferating myoblasts (28.68% to 77.06%) that underwent mitotic abnormalities, cell cycle arrest, and cellular senescence. SRSF1 regulates splicing of Fgfr1op2 to favor the full-length isoform crucial for mitotic spindle organization; its loss causes multipolar spindle formation. Adult satellite cells lacking SRSF1 fail to regenerate muscle after cardiotoxin injury due to impaired proliferation.

citation: Unearthing a novel function of SRSF1 in binding and unfolding of RNA G-quadruplexes (PMID: 38567732)
summary: SRSF1 was found to bind RNA G-quadruplexes (GQ) from ARPC2 mRNA using both its RRM domains and RS domain, with the RS domain preferring purine over pyrimidine. FRET and circular dichroism data revealed that SRSF1 unfolds the ARPC2 GQ, with RS leading unfolding and RRMs aiding, through Arg residues interacting specifically with guanine bases. Luciferase assays confirmed that SRSF1 alleviates the inhibitory effect of GQ on gene expression in cells, revealing a novel function beyond canonical splicing enhancer recognition.

citation: ASHG 2022 - SRSF1 haploinsufficiency is responsible for a syndromic developmental disorder with intellectual disability and variable marfanoid habitus
summary: Sixteen patients with germline SRSF1 variants (frameshift, nonsense, missense, and microdeletion of 17q22) presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, behavioral disorders, and skeletal/cardiac anomalies. Eye-specific overexpression of SF2 (the Drosophila ortholog of SRSF1) induced a severe developmental phenotype due to missplicing of key genes involved in eye development, and overexpression of human SRSF1 phenocopied this, demonstrating functional conservation. In vivo splicing assays in Drosophila supported pathogenicity of the identified variants.

citation: FOXA1 regulates alternative splicing in prostate cancer (PMID: 36170835)
summary: FOXA1 binds to the regulatory regions of splicing-related genes including SRSF1, controlling its expression as part of a cascade that rewires alternative splicing in prostate cancer across 500 primary and metastatic transcriptomes. FOXA1-controlled oncogene SRSF1 promotes inclusion of the NMD-determinant FLNA exon 30, which promotes cell growth in vitro and predicts disease recurrence. SRSF1 is thus positioned downstream of FOXA1 in a chromatin-to-splicing regulatory cascade.

citation: When SUMO met splicing (PMID: 29741121)
summary: SRSF1 was found to stimulate SUMO conjugation to several spliceosomal proteins during active splicing reactions. SUMOylation of spliceosomal components, modulated by SRSF1, is proposed to regulate spliceosome assembly and splicing efficiency. This identifies SRSF1 as a regulator of post-translational modification of the splicing machinery beyond its direct RNA-binding role.

citation: WNK4 kinase: from structure to physiology (PMID: 33491560)
summary: WNK4 is a serine-threonine kinase that acts as a positive regulator of the thiazide-sensitive NaCl cotransporter (NCC) in the distal convoluted tubule. Gain-of-function mutations in WNK4 cause familial hyperkalemic hypertension through increased activation of the SPAK/OSR1-NCC pathway, increasing salt reabsorption and impairing renal K+ secretion. The review covers WNK4 structure, functional domains, physiological functions from in vitro studies and genetically modified mouse models, and multiple levels of regulation.

citation: WNK4-SPAK modulates lipopolysaccharide-induced macrophage activation (PMID: 31786261)
summary: Using WNK4 knockout (WNK4-/-) and knockin (WNK4D561A/+) mice, the study demonstrated that WNK4 regulates NKCC1 phosphorylation and NF-κB activation in alveolar macrophages in response to LPS. WNK4 knockout attenuated LPS-induced macrophage activation and acute lung injury, while WNK4 knockin augmented the inflammatory response. This establishes a role for the WNK4-SPAK-NKCC1 cascade in modulating macrophage activation and lung inflammation outside the kidney.

citation: WNK4 kinase: role of chloride sensing in the distal convoluted tubule (PMID: 33394730)
summary: WNK4 functions as a physiological intracellular chloride sensor in the distal convoluted tubule (DCT), with the highest chloride sensitivity among WNK kinases and dominant expression in DCT. Chloride-insensitive WNK4 knockin mice developed hypertension and increased NCC activity, proving that WNK4 is inhibited by physiological intracellular chloride concentrations. The chloride-sensing mechanism of WNK4 is responsible for hypokalemia-induced NCC activation and requires basolateral K+ and Cl- channels/cotransporters including Kir4.1/5.1 and ClC-Kb.

citation: Arginine vasopressin regulates the renal Na(+)-Cl(-) and Na(+)-K(+)-Cl(-) cotransporters through with-no-lysine kinase 4 and inhibitor 1 phosphorylation (PMID: 38096266)
summary: In HEK-293 cells, only wild-type WNK4 (not WNK1, WNK3, or a WNK4 mutant lacking PKA phosphorylation motifs) could upregulate SPAK or cotransporter phosphorylation in response to forskolin or desmopressin, identifying WNK4 as the specific mediator of vasopressin-cAMP signaling to the SPAK/OSR1-NCC/NKCC2 pathway. In WNK4-/- mice infused with desmopressin, SPAK/OSR1, NCC, and NKCC2 phosphorylation were not increased, confirming WNK4 is essential for vasopressin-mediated cotransporter activation in vivo. WNK4 acts as a central node where PKA kinase and PP1 phosphatase signaling converge.

citation: KLHL3-dependent WNK4 degradation affected by potassium through the neddylation and autophagy pathway (PMID: 37481568)
summary: In vitro (HEK293 cells) and in vivo (mouse dietary K+ manipulation) experiments showed that WNK4 abundance and phosphorylation are regulated by potassium through the KLHL3-CUL3 E3 ligase complex via neddylation and autophagy pathways. Low potassium conditions increased WNK4 and pWNK4 abundance, and inhibiting neddylation (with MLN4924) or autophagy further elevated WNK4 levels. These findings reveal a complex potassium-dependent regulatory mechanism controlling WNK4 degradation and NCC activity.

citation: Transport activity regulates mitochondrial bioenergetics and biogenesis in renal tubules (PMID: 38370657)
summary: Deletion of Wnk4 in mice chronically decreased maximal mitochondrial respiratory capacity and downregulated mitochondrial DNA mass and mitochondrial length/density in thick ascending limbs (TALs) and distal convoluted tubules (DCTs). Conversely, a gain-of-function Wnk4 mutation increased maximal mitochondrial capacity and mitochondrial length/density without increasing mitochondrial DNA mass. These results demonstrate that WNK4-mediated transport activity tightly regulates mitochondrial bioenergetics and biogenesis in renal tubules.

citation: NRBP1 pseudokinase binds to and activates the WNK pathway in response to osmotic stress (PMID: 40668933)
summary: Using proximity labeling, immunoprecipitation, and mass spectrometry, NRBP1 pseudokinase was found to associate with WNK1 under osmotic stress conditions. Recombinant NRBP1 was shown to directly activate WNK4 in vitro, establishing NRBP1 as an upstream activator of the WNK pathway. AlphaFold-3 modeling predicted a complex involving WNK1, SPAK, NRBP1, and TSC22D4, with TSC22D4 RΦ-motifs interacting with the CCT-like domain of WNK1 and the CCT domain of NRBP1.

citation: Distal convoluted tubule-specific disruption of the COP9 signalosome but not its regulatory target cullin 3 causes tubular injury (PMID: 39205661)
summary: DCT-specific knockout of Cul3 or Jab1 (CSN subunit) using Slc12a3-Cre-ERT2 mice caused elevated WNK4, pSPAK, and pNCC abundance in the short term, confirming that CUL3-mediated degradation of WNK4 controls the WNK4-SPAK-NCC pathway in the DCT. Despite WNK4-SPAK-NCC pathway activation, neither model showed changes in plasma K+, Cl-, or total CO2, suggesting insufficient NCC activation for full FHHt phenotype. Long-term DCT-Jab1-/- but not DCT-Cul3-/- mice developed tubule injury and DCT atrophy.

citation: Regulation of the WNK4-SPAK-NCC pathway by the calcium-sensing receptor (PMID: 37530086)
summary: The calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) activates NCC in the distal convoluted tubule through a PKC-WNK4-SPAK signaling pathway, independent of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. Apical CaSR activation in DCT stimulates PKC, which activates WNK4 and subsequently SPAK to increase NCC phosphorylation and NaCl reabsorption. Glucose and fructose acting as calcimimetics enhance apical CaSR sensitivity, increasing WNK4-SPAK-NCC activity and contributing to hypertension in diabetic patients or those with high fructose consumption.

citation: ASHG 2017 - Statistical framework for biological interpretation and improvement of genetic association studies (M. Artomov et al.)
sample_size: 11 PHAII index cases (original FSGS study cohort)
significance: posterior p-value significant (>10-fold improvement over threshold of 3x10-5)
summary: A network-based statistical framework applied to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) GWAS data identified WNK4 as one of five genes in the most associated protein-protein interaction network, with WNK4 achieving more than 10-fold improvement in association signal after network integration. Mouse model evidence (PMID: 26901816) confirmed that mice with non-functional WNK4 develop histologically confirmed FSGS, supporting WNK4 as a causal gene for FSGS. WNK4 and COL4A4 were the two genes that reached statistical significance in the posterior association analysis.

citation: ZMYND8 protects breast cancer stem cells against oxidative stress and ferroptosis through activation of NRF2 (PMID: 38488001)
summary: ZMYND8 is upregulated in aldehyde dehydrogenase-high breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) and reduces ROS and iron to inhibit ferroptosis, promoting BCSC expansion and tumor initiation in mice. Mechanistically, ZMYND8 silences KEAP1 to stabilize NRF2 protein and recruits NRF2 to antioxidant gene promoters, forming a positive feedback loop where NRF2 also directly controls ZMYND8 expression in mammospheres.

citation: Targeting the histone reader ZMYND8 inhibits antiandrogen-induced neuroendocrine tumor transdifferentiation of prostate cancer (PMID: 40102673)
summary: CRISPR-Cas9 screening combined with single-cell RNA sequencing showed that ZMYND8-dependent epigenetic programming orchestrates neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) transdifferentiation under antiandrogen therapy. FOXM1 stabilizes ZMYND8 binding to H3K4me1-H3K14ac chromatin regions, and the SWI/SNF complex released from androgen receptor interacts with ZMYND8-FOXM1 to upregulate neuroendocrine lineage regulators; a small molecule inhibitor iZMYND8-34 blocking ZMYND8 histone recognition effectively blocks NEPC development.

citation: The ZMYND8-regulated mevalonate pathway endows YAP-high intestinal cancer with metabolic vulnerability (PMID: 33932349)
summary: YAP-mediated ZMYND8 expression drives de novo cholesterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate (MVA) pathway in colorectal cancer, sensitizing YAP-high intestinal tumors to statin treatment. Mechanistically, ZMYND8 and SREBP2 drive enhancer-promoter interactions to recruit the Mediator complex and upregulate MVA pathway genes, and disruption of this pathway restricts Lgr5+ intestinal stem cell self-renewal and intestinal tumorigenesis.

citation: ZMYND8-regulated IRF8 transcription axis is an acute myeloid leukemia dependency (PMID: 34358447)
summary: ZMYND8 functions as a chromatin reader that directly activates IRF8 and MYC through their lineage-specific enhancers in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and is essential for AML proliferation both in vitro and in vivo. ZMYND8 occupancy at IRF8 and MYC enhancers requires BRD4, and ZMYND8 binds the ET domain of BRD4 via its chromatin reader cassette (PHD-BRD-PWWP), which is required for proper chromatin occupancy and maintenance of leukemic growth.

citation: ZMYND8 mediated liquid condensates spatiotemporally decommission the latent super-enhancers during macrophage polarization (PMID: 34764296)
summary: ZMYND8 forms liquid-liquid phase-separated condensates with NF-κB/p65 to silence latent super-enhancers and restrict macrophage-mediated inflammation during polarization. Signal-induced acetylation of p65 reinforces fusion of ZMYND8 and p65 condensates, guiding ZMYND8 redistribution onto latent super-enhancers where it recruits LSD1 to decommission them; mutations that coagulate ZMYND8 into solid compartments abolish this regulatory function.

citation: Zinc Finger MYND-Type Containing 8 (ZMYND8) Is Epigenetically Regulated in Mutant Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) Glioma to Promote Radioresistance (PMID: 36692427)
summary: ZMYND8 expression is decreased in patient-derived mIDH1 glioma cell cultures (GCCs) treated with the mIDH1 inhibitor AGI-5198, and shRNA knockdown or genetic knockout of ZMYND8 sensitizes these cells to ionizing radiation. ZMYND8 KO mIDH1 GCCs show significant ATM phosphorylation and sustained γH2AX activation after irradiation, and are further sensitized by BRD4, HDAC, or PARP inhibitors, indicating ZMYND8 maintains genomic integrity and DNA damage repair in mIDH1 glioma.

citation: The endogenous retrovirus-derived long noncoding RNA TROJAN promotes triple-negative breast cancer progression via ZMYND8 degradation (PMID: 30854423)
summary: The lncRNA TROJAN binds directly to ZMYND8, a metastasis-repressing factor, and promotes its degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway by repelling the stabilizing protein ZNF592, thereby epigenetically upregulating metastasis-related genes in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Antisense oligonucleotide therapy targeting TROJAN substantially suppressed TNBC progression in vivo, and inverse correlation between TROJAN and ZMYND8 was confirmed in clinical samples.

citation: USP7 deubiquitinates epigenetic reader ZMYND8 to promote breast cancer cell migration and invasion (PMID: 39128723)
summary: USP7 was identified as a deubiquitinase for ZMYND8, binding its PHD-BRD-PWWP domain via USP7's TRAF and UBL domains and removing FBXW7-catalyzed poly-ubiquitin chains on ZMYND8 K1034, thereby stabilizing ZMYND8 and stimulating transcription of ZEB1 and VEGFA to enhance breast cancer cell migration and invasion. USP7 protein levels positively correlate with ZMYND8 levels in breast cancer tissues.

citation: ZMYND8 Reads H3K36me2 to Activate CEBPE Transcription and Suppress Multiple Myeloma Progression through the Inhibition of Adaptive UPR Pathways (PMID: 40347515)
sample_size: 283 HCC cases (protein), 234 HCC cases (mRNA) referenced in a different study; MM patient cohort size not specified
summary: ZMYND8 acts as a reader of the H3K36me2 histone mark via its PWWP domain and activates CEBPE transcription in multiple myeloma (MM), where CEBPE in turn represses ERN1, XBP1, and ATF6 to inhibit adaptive unfolded protein response (UPR) pathways and suppress MM cell survival. Low ZMYND8 expression correlates with adverse clinicopathological features and poor survival in MM patients, and ZMYND8 upregulation increases MM cell sensitivity to carfilzomib.

citation: The hypoxia-induced chromatin reader ZMYND8 drives HIF-dependent metabolic rewiring in breast cancer (PMID: 40912652)
summary: ZMYND8 expression is elevated under hypoxic conditions in adherent breast cancer cells and 3D multicellular tumor spheroids (MCTS), and immunohistochemistry shows a positive correlation between ZMYND8 and HIF1α expression in breast cancer tissues. ZMYND8 regulates glycolysis by elevating hexokinase II and lactate dehydrogenase A expression (directly promoting LDHA transcription via S5-phosphorylated RNA Pol II recruitment), bifurcating metabolism toward anaerobic glycolysis and impacting CD8+ T cell activity in the tumor microenvironment.

citation: Bidirectional histone monoaminylation dynamics regulate neural rhythmicity (PMID: 39779849)
summary: H3Q5 histaminylation (H3Q5his) inhibits the binding of WDR5, a core member of histone H3 Lys4 (H3K4) methyltransferase complexes, thereby antagonizing methyltransferase activities on H3K4. This represents a mechanism by which histone monoaminylation regulates chromatin state through modulation of WDR5 binding. The finding was demonstrated in brain tissue in the context of diurnally rhythmic gene expression.

citation: WDR5 represents a therapeutically exploitable target for cancer stem cells in glioblastoma (PMID: 36732025)
summary: WDR5 was identified as indispensable for the SOX2-enriched, therapy-resistant cancer stem cell (CSC) niche in GBM patient-derived organoids via a spatially resolved loss-of-function screen. WDR5 inhibitors blocked WRAD complex assembly, reduced H3K4 trimethylation, and disrupted CSC in vitro growth, self-renewal, and in vivo tumor growth. H3K4me3 peaks lost upon WDR5 inhibition were disproportionately associated with POU transcription factor motifs including the OCT4::SOX2 motif.

citation: MLL/WDR5 complex recruits centriolar satellite protein Cep72 to regulate microtubule nucleation and spindle formation (PMID: 39661677)
summary: WDR5, as part of the MLL/WDR5 complex, localizes to the pericentriolar material and interacts with centriolar satellite protein Cep72 and γ-tubulin ring complex proteins (γ-TuRCs), revealing a non-epigenetic role at the centrosome. Loss of WDR5 impairs microtubule nucleation and regrowth, affects spindle formation, and leads to misaligned chromosomes during mitosis. MLL and WDR5 recruit Cep72 to the centrosome, and this phenotype is also observed in cells from patients with Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome.

citation: The MYC-WDR5 Nexus and Cancer (PMID: 26383167)
summary: MYC oncoproteins interact directly with WDR5, a WD40-repeat protein component of chromatin-regulatory complexes, to create an avidity-based chromatin recognition mechanism that allows MYC to select target genes in response to both genetic and epigenetic determinants. This interaction provides plasticity in MYC target gene selection and is proposed to occur in the context of WDR5's role in multiple chromatin-regulatory complexes. The MYC-WDR5 interface is highlighted as an attractive target for small-molecule inhibitors of MYC function in cancer.

citation: MBD2 regulates the progression and chemoresistance of cholangiocarcinoma through interaction with WDR5 (PMID: 39350229)
summary: MBD2 directly interacts with WDR5 and binds to the ABCB1 promoter, promoting H3K4 trimethylation via KMT2A and activating ABCB1 expression to drive chemoresistance in cholangiocarcinoma. Knockdown of WDR5 or KMT2A blocked MBD2-mediated transcriptional activation of ABCB1. The WDR5-KMT2A interaction inhibitor MM-102 suppressed ABCB1 expression and decreased CCA chemoresistance to cisplatin in cell and xenograft models.

citation: Targeting WDR5/ATAD2 signaling by the CK2/IKAROS axis demonstrates therapeutic efficacy in T-ALL (PMID: 39785511)
summary: WDR5 is highly expressed in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) and plays an oncogenic role by activating cell cycle signaling through its downstream effector ATAD2. IKAROS directly regulates WDR5 transcription, and CK2 inhibition with CX-4945 suppresses WDR5 expression by restoring IKAROS function. Combining CX-4945 with a WDR5 inhibitor showed synergistic antileukemic efficacy in patient-derived xenograft mouse models.

citation: lncRNA VELRP Modulates Pulmonary Arterial Smooth Muscle Cell Proliferation and Promotes Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension (PMID: 39360410)
summary: The lncRNA VELRP interacts with WDR5 to enhance H3K4 trimethylation, leading to increased expression of CDK1, CDK2, and CDK4 and consequent hyperproliferation of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). This WDR5-dependent epigenetic mechanism was validated by RNA immunoprecipitation and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays. In vivo, smooth muscle cell-specific knockdown of VELRP reduced right ventricular systolic pressure and vascular remodeling in rat pulmonary hypertension models.

citation: Direct mapping of ligandable tyrosines and lysines in cells with chiral sulfonyl fluoride probes (PMID: 37460812)
summary: A chemoproteomic screen using enantiomeric pairs of clickable arylsulfonyl fluoride probes identified Y228 in the MYC binding site of WDR5 as a ligandable residue in intact cells. A high-resolution crystal structure confirmed covalent modification of Y228 by a chiral probe. This finding provides a covalent chemical probe targeting the WDR5-MYC interaction interface for potential therapeutic development.

citation: STING mediates hepatocyte pyroptosis in liver fibrosis by Epigenetically activating the NLRP3 inflammasome (PMID: 37018971)
summary: WDR5 and DOT1L were identified as regulators of NLRP3 expression in STING-overexpressing hepatocytes, where WDR5/DOT1L-mediated histone methylation enhances IRF3 binding to the Nlrp3 promoter and promotes STING-induced Nlrp3 transcription. This defines a STING-WDR5/DOT1L/IRF3-NLRP3 epigenetic signaling axis in hepatocyte pyroptosis and liver fibrosis. The pathway was validated in primary murine hepatocytes and in vivo fibrotic liver models.

citation: Targeting IP(6) signaling to destabilize homologous recombination proteins to overcome PARP inhibitor resistance (PMID: 41935081)
summary: WDR5 was identified as a DCAF (DDB1- and CUL4-associated factor) protein that facilitates Cul4A-mediated proteolysis of RAD51 and CHK1, revealing a novel non-epigenetic role for WDR5 in regulating homologous recombination protein stability. This Cul4A-WDR5-dependent proteolysis pathway is activated by reduction of inositol hexaphosphate (IP6) levels via PIKfyve/PIP5K1C inhibition. Functionally, this mechanism suppresses homologous recombination and enhances tumor sensitivity to PARP inhibitors in vitro and in xenograft models.

citation: UPF1 helicase orchestrates mutually exclusive interactions with the SMG6 endonuclease and UPF2 (PMID: 38709891)
summary: Using mass spectrometry, structural biology, and biochemical approaches, a conserved short linear motif in SMG6 was identified that interacts with the cysteine/histidine-rich (CH) domain of UPF1. The UPF1-SMG6 interaction is mutually exclusive with UPF2 binding to the CH domain, and cryo-EM data suggest that distinct SMG6-containing and UPF2-containing NMD complexes are dictated by different conformational states linked to UPF1's RNA-binding status.

citation: Structure-Mediated RNA Decay by UPF1 and G3BP1 (PMID: 32017897)
summary: Depletion of UPF1 (and its associated protein G3BP1) increased steady-state levels of mRNAs with highly structured 3' UTRs as well as highly structured circular RNAs, demonstrating that UPF1 is required for a genome-wide structure-mediated RNA decay pathway independent of specific single-stranded sequences. This pathway enables cells to selectively regulate coding and noncoding RNAs based on overall 3' UTR base-pairing structure.

citation: UPF1 deficiency enhances mitochondrial ROS which promotes an immunosuppressive microenvironment in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PMID: 40591563)
summary: shRNA-mediated silencing of Upf1 in murine KPC pancreatic cancer cells and orthotopic implantation into immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice showed that Upf1-deficient tumors were markedly larger, enriched in myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and depleted of CD8+ T cells. Mechanistically, Upf1 deficiency increased mitochondrial complex I activity, elevating ROS levels that drove secretion of immunosuppressive cytokines (G-CSF, CXCL2), promoting immune evasion and tumor growth.

citation: UPF1 plays critical roles in early B cell development (PMID: 38982067)
summary: UPF1 is upregulated during early stages of B cell development in the bone marrow. B-cell-specific Upf1 deletion in mice severely impedes the early-to-late LPre-B cell transition, blocks VH-DHJH recombination at the Igh locus, and ultimately prevents development into immature B cells, demonstrating an essential role for UPF1 in B cell differentiation beyond its canonical NMD function.

citation: Caspases compromise SLU7 and UPF1 stability and NMD activity during hepatocarcinogenesis (PMID: 39105183)
sample_size: non-tumoral=50, HCC=374 (TCGA); animal models n≥3; cell lines n≥4 replicates
summary: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments in cultured cell lines, primary hepatocytes, and animal models of liver injury demonstrated that the splicing factor SLU7 physically interacts with UPF1 and is required to preserve UPF1 protein levels and correct NMD activity. Caspase activation during liver damage mediates cleavage and degradation of SLU7, leading to downstream UPF1 downregulation and NMD inhibition, contributing to malignant transcriptome reshaping in HCC.

citation: CRISPR/Cas9 screen reveals that targeting TRIM34 enhances ferroptosis sensitivity and augments immunotherapy efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 38704136)
summary: TRIM34 was found to directly interact with UPF1, a core NMD component, promoting its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation in HCC cells. This suppression of UPF1 inhibited NMD-mediated degradation of GPX4 transcripts, elevating GPX4 protein levels and conferring ferroptosis resistance; knockdown of TRIM34 restored UPF1 activity and sensitized HCC cells to ferroptosis and anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

citation: Inhibiting UPF1 methylation enhances tumor immunotherapy sensitivity by reducing nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (PMID: 40570371)
summary: UPF1 protein levels were found to differ significantly between microsatellite-stable (MSS) and microsatellite-unstable (MSI) colorectal cancer clinical samples, and UPF1 levels negatively regulated tumor immunogenicity and anti-PD-1 sensitivity in CRC mouse models. Mechanistically, asymmetric di-methylation of UPF1 at R433 by PRMT4 inhibits autophagic degradation of UPF1; blocking this methylation weakened NMD, increased neoantigen expression, and enhanced immunotherapy response.

citation: Staufen-mediated mRNA decay (PMID: 23681777)
summary: UPF1 is a key factor in Staufen-mediated mRNA decay (SMD), directly interacting with both STAU1 and STAU2 to enhance UPF1's helicase activity and promote effective mRNA degradation. Because both SMD and NMD employ UPF1, the two pathways compete, and this competition regulates cellular differentiation processes such as myogenesis and adipogenesis.

citation: Rapid UPF1 depletion illuminates the temporal dynamics of the NMD-regulated human transcriptome (PMID: 40934927)
summary: Human cell lines were engineered with endogenous UPF1 fused to conditional degron tags, enabling rapid depletion; temporal transcriptomic analyses identified direct NMD target mRNAs that are mostly stabilized within hours of UPF1 loss. Integration of long-read sequencing and ribosome profiling defined the consolidated NMD-regulated human transcriptome (NMDRHT), revealing that alternative splicing is a major contributor of NMD-targeted mRNAs and uncovering non-canonical NMD events.

citation: ASHG 2023 - An adult male with UPF1-related neurodevelopmental disorder (M. Chung, K. Baker, M. Wiznitzer, J. Chenbhanich)
summary: Trio exome sequencing identified a de novo c.1846A>G (p.Thr616Ala) variant in exon 14 of UPF1 (classified as Likely Pathogenic) in a 38-year-old male presenting with infantile hypotonia, global developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, myoclonic epilepsy, bilateral hearing loss, and overgrowth features. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of UPF1-related neurodevelopmental disorder, with overgrowth being a previously unreported feature, and highlights disruption of the NMD pathway as the underlying mechanism.
